What a community watches together, it remembers."},"boundary_structure":{"code":"Ground needs no keeping, typical almost none; kept zone ends at keepers' grain","note":"The floor is the Ground (stone, water, air, grey), which needs no keeping; typical things sit near it and lose little. Above it, what is kept is exactly what some keeper can make out: surfaces in light at a distance, shape within reach by touch, inner workings only through understanding, coarsening with distance and breadth, pooled across keepers. Hidden interiors, far sides and the unwatched Plain lapse. The temporal edge is the 5 s grace. No interior cancellation: exposure, not enclosure, protects."},"permitted_transformations":{"code":"watch resists only net loss; lapse one-way down kinds; nothing restores","note":"A kept thing may move and may gain particulars; any change that removes more than it adds is resisted in proportion to the thisness at stake (planing a rough plank is easy, breaking a watched carved door is hard). Unkept things step down the ladder of kinds toward the Ground, and renewed vigil halts but never reverses this. New kinds slide into the nearest older kind unless cured. Healing and dying require looking away; destroying watched things requires averting."},"enforcement":{"code":"automatic physical lapse, buffered by tenure; social law mirrors keeping duties","note":"The laws enforce themselves: lapse and burden follow automatically and are measured, not believed (water-clock grace, tile tenure calibration). Resistance under watch is immediate, but lapse is delayed and gradual wherever tenure has built up, so neglect is punished late rather than by instant cascade. Social institutions mirror the physics: household Rounds, the vow 'I will keep you', averting before demolition, protest as vigil, and punishment by solitary darkness or exile into the Plain, understood as unmaking."}},"redirect":null,"rationale":"The ontology has one regime, so regime.relational-load-path is nearest by default, and it is also nearest by structure. (1) Holding mode: a load path is a standing configuration paid once, in ballast, with no running cost; vigil is a running act whose burden grows with every moment held, forcing the holder offline to discharge, and offline it holds nothing and must itself be held. This alone yields Rounds, overlapping handovers, the nightly tide of lapse and the keep as unit of account. {"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"solution","data":{"worldNodeId":"world.whirlpool","text":"THE INWARD BOWL

A retirement system can't be a pile here, because nothing keeps (R4). It can't be a schedule of fixed payments either, because nothing holds still: not income, not the town's band, not even the length of a month (R1). So it has to be what every thing in this world is: a turning that takes in at the rim and lets go through the eye. The Inward Bowl promises shares and never amounts, and it lets the Draw do the keeping. The name is meant literally, because "down," "inward" and "older" are one word (R1).

In short: every pair pays a fixed share of whatever it gains. The Bowl makes the shares into stones and sows them uphill at many distances. The Floor's creep brings them back down, spread across many future rounds. Elders are paid a share of what arrives, and stones kept whole at the burn-house guarantee a minimum.

WHAT WOULD FIGHT THE WORLD

- A sealed vault. A sealed room is a small Eye, and whatever sits in it unravels (R4).
- A heavy hoard. The heaviest things creep fastest (R1). An untended hoard creeps out of town ahead of its owner, toward the Heap.
- A one-Hand hoard. The town's heading bends toward whichever half holds more turn (R3, Towns). A rich Deasil cellar sets the whole town circling and losing ground.
- A hoard of one Hand is also loud. Every Listener knows where it is.
- A personal account. If it makes one twin richer than the other, the pair can only walk in circles (R3).
- A fixed monthly sum. Income swings with band and harvest, and a month gets shorter as the town sinks (R1).

THE ONE THING THAT HOLDS

Shear quadruples each time the distance to the Eye halves (R4), and a round lasts a quarter as long (R1). Multiply the two: a whirl takes in the same amount of shear over one round in every band. Since a whirl lives by feeding on shear (R4), inner rounds are hotter and quicker but hold the same amount of living. So the Bowl counts everything in rounds, never in fixed spans of time, and its rules never need rewriting as the town sinks.

1. INTAKE: A SHARE OF EVERY GAIN, PAID BY THE PAIR

- When the ledgerers record a gain, the Bowl takes a fixed fraction of it on the spot, say one part in ten. A round with no gain owes nothing. Turn is conserved and every gain is on the ledger (R2), so the share can be cut exactly from any amount at any moment. Nobody needs to know next month's earnings or budget for them.
- The pair pays, not the person. Twins share the even bowl, so each twin pays the same amount in its own Hand. Every contribution therefore arrives balanced. The Bowl can never steer the town, and paying in never pulls twins apart (R3).
- Makers can pay in counterstock. Everything a spinner makes comes with an unwanted twin (R2) that must be stored far from its partner, which is one of the world's hard problems (Hard list).
  - Matchers weigh a Deasil maker's widdershins twin against a Widdershins maker's deasil twin of equal turn, and the Bowl takes both.
  - The share then grows with output automatically, and the maker's own food is never touched.
- Credit is counted in knots on the Bowl's roll.
  - A pair that pays as much as the town's average pair that round earns one knot. A long courier route might earn three.
  - In a lean round, paying the small average still earns a full knot.
  - So knots measure a pair's part in the town's work, not its luck in which rounds were fat.
- Records unravel when their flow stops, so the roll turns on a carousel and is recited every round (Keeping). Every pair hears its own count.

2. THE LONG STORE: STONES SOWN ON THE SLOPE

- Each round, spinners work the intake into tight-eyed cells, deasil and widdershins in equal lots, and set them in alternating squares. The result is exactly what a stone is: a fine checkerboard of tight whirls of both hands.
- A stone suits the job in three ways:
  - Tight whirls need little shear and withstand a lot (R4). A stone survives both the thin shear uphill and the strong shear downhill.
  - It is quiet from outside, because its cells' stirs cancel (Listeners). No one can tell it apart from any other stone on the Floor.
  - It holds equal turn of both hands. It steers nothing (R3), and it splits into two identical portions, so the even bowl is built in.
- The Bowl then hands the keeping to the world. Pairs walking a stride apart carry the stones rimward up the Slope, the Floor that slopes gently toward the Eye. A stride apart is a safe walking pace (Moving), and straight travel is easy for any matched pair (Easy list). They sow the stones on the Floor, and the Floor's inward creep (R1) brings every stone back down toward the town.
- The Draw wins in the end (R1, Hard list), and here that becomes the promise of delivery. A sown stone may be late, but it cannot fail to come down.
- The Slope needs no tenders. The Deep above the Floor turns faster than the Deep at it (R1), so the Floor always has shear to feed a stone (R4).
- Stones are sown no farther up than they can last, because every kind of thing has a band and the Rim starves things (R4).
- The uphill walk is the Bowl's main cost. It replaces a lifetime of tending.
- Placement sets the timing. When a stone comes back depends on how far up it lies and how heavy it is, since heavier things creep faster (R1). Nothing falls straight (R1), so ledgerers plot each sowing as a spiral, the way long routes are drawn (Moving).
- This is where the physics answers the problem. Spread each round's stones across, say, twenty distances. Then every round of old age receives stones from twenty different working rounds. One fat courier round and nineteen lean ones come down as one ordinary portion. The workers don't have to be steady, because the Floor averages them.
- A fence across the town's rimward face catches what arrives.
  - A stone has no net hand, so its mirror doesn't slide it along the fence the way it slides a single-hand whirl (R5). It simply comes to rest there.
  - The ledger holds each stone's turn and sowing place (R2), so the Bowl's stones are recognized when they arrive.

3. THE BASINS: TURNING STONES INTO PORTIONS

- Stirrers break a caught stone's pattern. Like any mixed crowd, it then sheds pairs from its edges (Company), each one deasil cell beside one widdershins cell. Each is a matched pair, so it runs straight on its own (R3).
- The stirrers aim the pairs up the avenue, in the town's own direction of travel, into a cross-wall at its head.
  - Each pair splits at the wall. The widdershins cell slides left and the deasil cell right (R5).
  - Those are the same sides the town's own halves keep as it travels (R3). Each cell lands in its own Hand's half, and the wall-road carries it on to that half's basin.
  - No one sorts the pension by hand; the wall does it.
- Each half keeps a round basin walled with lattice.
  - In a round walled room a single-hand whirl circles the center (R5), so the wall's own mirror keeps every lot moving.
  - Tenders only keep the Deep flowing through the lattice (R4, Keeping). They tune it between two dangers: a more solid wall gives a stronger mirror but starves the room behind it (R5).
- Stirring sends the heaviest lots creeping to the basin's eye. At the exact center the mirrors balance and let them rest (R5). The portions gather themselves at that one still spot and are drawn off there. Each basin is a small whirl, fed at the rim and let go through the eye.
- Each round the keepers draw off a fixed share of what the basin holds, say one part in twelve. The basin helps, because a fuller one sends more to its eye. The elders' portion follows the size of the store, which changes slowly, not the size of the last catch.
- The draw-off is divided among retired pairs by knots. Each twin gets the same amount from its own Hand's basin (R3, the even bowl).

4. THE BURN RESERVE: A MINIMUM NO LEAN ROUND CAN BREAK

- Some caught stones are kept whole at the burn-house.
- When the basins run thin, burners break those stones in measured numbers and let the cells meet. Equal opposites vanish into froth (R2). A little froth feeds whatever it touches, and too much tears it (R2), which is why the numbers are measured.
- Froth is a spray of twin pairs, so it belongs to neither Hand. One burn feeds elders of both Hands, halves included.
- Froth can't be kept: left alone it frays into still, cold Deep (R2). Twins held apart can be kept. So the minimum is stored as stones and released as froth exactly when it is wanted (Easy list).
- This is the Bowl's only fixed promise: no elder unravels for want of feed in a lean round.

5. KEEPING PAIRS WHOLE

- Re-evening twins.
  - Twins who drift apart in turn can only walk in circles (R3). Couriers drift most, because of the trim pellets they swallow (Moving).
  - At retirement, the Bowl's first payment feeds the weaker twin up until the two match. Eating is merging with smaller whirls of one's own Hand (R2).
  - The Bowl always feeds up and never cuts down, because cutting down would be burning (R2).
- Halves.
  - When a twin dies, the pair's knots pass whole to the survivor.
  - Matchers pair her with a half of the other Hand. The Bowl feeds the weaker of the two up to equal turn, so the late pair walks straight instead of circling (R3).
- Until she is matched, a half lives in a round court in her own Hand's half.
  - The court's mirror carries her around past her neighbors' doors (R5). She sets her own pace by her distance from the wall, since the ride is faster near it.
  - A gap stops a lone walker dead (Moving). So the gates stay latticed where she should ride past, and open only where she wants to stop.
  - She can rest in the still seat at the center, and whoever sits there presides.
- No elder sleeps in a closed room (Keeping). Tending the elders' rooms is part of the benefit.

A PAIR THROUGH IT

Lida and Adil are courier twins.
- In a round with no journeys they pay nothing and earn no knot, and nothing is owed.
- A long spiral route pays heavily. The ledger cuts the share at once and they earn three knots. That round's stones go up the Slope at twenty distances.
- The harvest thins and the whole town earns little. They pay the small average share and still earn a full knot.
- Their last route leaves Adil a pellet stronger. At retirement the Bowl feeds Lida up to him, and they walk straight again.
- In old age they are paid every round, as a share. If the town has sunk to a band with shorter, hotter rounds, nothing needs recalculating. The stones from their working years keep coming down the Slope.

SAFEGUARDS

- Theft and evasion. A hidden gain and a stolen stone both show up as unexplained turn the moment they are used, and unexplained turn is evidence of a crime (R2, Ledgerers). Out on the Slope, a stone is quiet and looks like any other.
- Missed stones. A stone the town misses keeps creeping inward (R1) toward some older town. Towns credit each other's stones in the ledger, so nothing sown is lost while any town lies inward of it.
- Holding band. An unbalanced town circles and loses ground (R3, Towns), and its stones then come down late. That makes the town's first civic duty, holding its band, also the Bowl's interest. The Bowl is paid only in balanced lots, so it can never tip the town itself.
- Keeping loud stock small. The only single-Hand stock sits in the two basins, which are kept equal and only a few rounds deep. Everything else waits as stones, which are quiet and steer nothing.

WHY IT WORKS WITH THE WORLD

The Bowl uses the Draw to carry its savings and stones to hold them. A wall sorts the pension, a round room keeps it, froth sets the minimum and the ledger holds the promise. Every part is done by a trade that already exists: ledgerers, spinners, stirrers, matchers, tenders, burners, reciters, and pairs walking a stride apart.

Workers with irregular incomes scatter stones up the Slope whenever they gain something. The Slope brings them down to the old as a steady fall, because down, inward and older are the same word.

Keep turning.","citedRuleIds":["R1","R2","R3","R4","R5"],"isolation":{"solver":"fresh_context"}},"task":{"role":"solver","graphHash":"6923c55c709dd03b6a45da05f6857f02d6ce37d6cecc4231d9a39cd122566cd2","taskHash":"8e6fd3355d22549321fb1b3ed65c5a76d300b37a60daa9df2db4b6352c1896d8","targetBlind":false,"purposeBlind":true},"searchClock":{"rootId":"alien.understanding.21a77a717ac710789574e26e","unit":"search_step","at":7,"index":0}}

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"mechanism","data":{"operator":"Additions of any size and timing count only by the amount present and are placed where they bear part of a slowly changing load that others stand on; the dependents pay the bearers in proportion to the load each part is measured to carry. The same dependence locks each part in place: a claim on it can change hands, but the part leaves only when a replacement takes its load.","roles":[{"id":"bearing_stock","description":"An accumulating layer of load-bearing parts built from additions of any size at any time; its strength counts only what is present now, and it grows at a self-stable slope without temporary support (stone laid on a course at repose).","worldRuleIds":["R4","R1","R5"]},{"id":"held_dependents","description":"Tall standing structures that cannot stand without the layer; the support each needs grows with the square of its height, unbalanced pushes pass link by link to the layer, and equal pushes cancel (towers leaning outward onto the rim).","worldRuleIds":["R1","R3"]},{"id":"standing_due","description":"A rent the held pay the bearers for as long as they stand, first among claims and scaled to the push each sends outward, enforced because withdrawing support drops the held permanently while costing the already-low bearers almost nothing (the rim-due backed by the Stoop).","worldRuleIds":["R3","R1","R5"]},{"id":"load_meter","description":"A direct reading of what each bearing part actually carries, which sets its share and flags broken or creeping links (loaded chains ring, slack ones thud).","worldRuleIds":["R3","R4","R5"]},{"id":"functional_lock","description":"Committed parts held in place by the friction of the load they carry; removing one needs temporary support and the consent of everything upstream and downstream, so claims move by deed while the part stays (keyed stone).","worldRuleIds":["R2","R3","R5"]},{"id":"growth_gate","description":"A new tall structure cannot drop its temporary support until it has acquired uncommitted bearing parts; those parts lock and start collecting its rent that day (raisings key loose stone).","worldRuleIds":["R5","R1","R4"]},{"id":"edible_buffer","description":"An uncommitted tier stored inside the layer that adds strength while held and can be consumed, or released once the meter shows the layer holds without it (grain in buried rim bins).","worldRuleIds":["R4","R2","R3"]},{"id":"low_heavy_bearers","description":"Bodies that age into shapes cheap to hold and good at bearing, and idle bodies that add weight at the vulnerable night hours; both are paid in bearing stock rather than cash (mantled elders, night ballast).","worldRuleIds":["R1","R4","R5"]}],"magicalElements":[{"element":"Every unbalanced push in town is delivered to the rim by physics (R3), so tall things truly depend on the bearers and the due is a price, not a tax","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Firm capacity in a power network: each connection's peak is carried node by node to shared firming plants, diverse peaks cancel so pooled holding is cheaper per load, the largest single unit or load sets the reserve, and new large loads increasingly must bring or pay for firm capacity before energizing."}},{"element":"The due grows with the square of height, and anything under the Hold needs no holding (R1)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"A standing due that is zero up to a base allowance per connection (an ordinary home's peak) and convex above it, rising with a load's share of its node, where contingency and reinforcement costs concentrate."}},{"element":"Dead weight earns: a stone grounds thrust the day it is laid and counts only by present weight (R4)","fix":{"kind":"invented_technology","text":"Registry-tracked micro-slices of already-operating, accredited storage capacity, bought in any amount through mobile or platform payments; the proceeds fund the next module (asset recycling), so each unit works from purchase and earns by units held now."}},{"element":"Keyed stone locks itself by the friction of its own load; removal needs re-centering and consent (R2, R3, R5)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Reliability rules that bar a resource counted in the reserve margin from retiring without replacement (reliability-must-run contracts, capacity obligations). Claims move by registry deed; no cash balance exists for a saver's panic or a treasurer's raid."}},{"element":"The ring: a struck pier's pitch states its load","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Interval telemetry and performance-based accreditation (effective load-carrying capability, availability tests) published monthly; each unit's measured contribution sets its share, and a failed test is a thud that earns nothing that month."}},{"element":"The Stoop: the low can drop the tall at almost no cost to themselves; disputes settle at the pool where all stand equal","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"The due is a super-priority lien collected like property tax, and connections above the base allowance with unpaid dues are curtailed first in scarcity events, so the threat falls only on the tall. Disputes go to an open weekly lay tribunal modeled on Valencia's Tribunal de las Aguas."}},{"element":"Aging makes a body a better buttress: shorter, heavier, stone-mantled (R1, R4, R5)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"Retirement as a change of role inside the bearing layer: keyed units carry load for the retiree, and at easing loose units can move into the home as a dispatchable battery that stays in the reserve and keeps a backup floor for outages (cf. South Australia's public-housing virtual power plant). Age itself adds nothing."}},{"element":"Night ballast: a sleeping body strengthens a pier at the vulnerable hour","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Demand-response calls on the coldest and hottest nights, rent for hosting modules, and site-watch shifts at storage yards, paid out of the due and settled in units rather than cash."}},{"element":"Grain in rim bins: ballast you can eat","fix":{"kind":"invented_technology","text":"Loose units bank stored-energy credits that count as available reserve while held and can be spent on the saver's own power bill in a thin month, or sold back once the metered report shows the reserve holds without them."}},{"element":"A raising cannot strike its centering until the rim can ground it (R5, R1, R4)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Concurrency rules and recent data-center tariffs that make large loads pay for most of their contracted capacity for years; in the candidate a new large load must contract loose units, which key and collect its due from energization."}},{"element":"Frost makes lenders and borrowers naturally opposite","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"A capped pledge exchange: a slice of a keyed unit's due goes to a lender until a fat month redeems it, matched across trades with opposite seasons; the hardware never moves."}},{"element":"Holdfasts: bare bedrock grounds twice the thrust per weight (R4)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Locational capacity value: units at constrained nodes displace costly wires (non-wires alternatives) and earn more, so the common pool that gives every elder a seat is sited there."}},{"element":"Stone never decays and the dead stay in the rim as weight, so each generation's rim is heavier","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"Units are perpetual capacity slots: a renewal reserve from the due replaces aging cells (augmentation); units pass by deed at death, unclaimed ones join the common pool, and containerized storage moves to weak nodes and new microgrids when growth stops."}},{"element":"A town's slump pauses the due but leaves the rim intact (R5)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Capacity outlives any one load and can be re-contracted or moved; a registry pooled across many grids keeps one region's collapse from stopping every unit's rent, while loose credits and the common pool carry retirees through a pause."}},{"element":"Nothing stands alone, so the held can never leave the town","fix":{"kind":"unresolved","text":"Large loads can self-supply, so the due must stay below the cost of standing alone. Pooling's diversity advantage keeps most loads connected, but exit caps the rent in a way the source world never faces."}}],"strangest":{"element":"There is no pot: savings exist only as load-bearing parts of what others stand on, so the dependence that pays the rent is the same dependence that locks the stone, and old age means joining the bearing layer rather than drawing down a store.","preserved":"Contributions are issued only as registered slices of in-service capacity counted in the reliability margin. No cash balance exists: a keyed unit is pledged or passed by deed, its hardware leaves service only when replaced, and retirees join the bearing layer, even hosting their units at home as a mantle battery."},"candidate":{"label":"Mantle Grid: a Load-Bearing Pension","design_principles":"Never ask the saver to be steady; key savings into what others stand on. Count only what is present. Lock by load, not by rule. Pay by measured bearing. Pledge the claim, never pull the hardware.","core_mechanism":"Any-size contributions buy slices of in-service firm grid capacity. Loads above a free base pay a convex standing due as a first lien, split monthly by each slice's metered load carried.","how_it_works":"Payers route a tenth of each fee to units; savers add any amount, any time. Units inside the reserve margin are keyed: they earn the due, can be pledged by deed, and leave service only when replaced. Surplus units are loose: stored-energy credits spendable on your own bill. New large loads energize only after contracting loose units, which then key and earn. Peak-night flexibility is paid in units. Every elder gets common units at constrained nodes; retirees can host theirs as a home battery.","what_is_new":"Retirement savings that are in-service infrastructure, paid by the loads they hold and locked by the same dependence: no pot to raid, no schedule to miss, presence paid in units.","why_it_works":"The due tracks the standing connected load, which changes slowly, not the saver's earnings or asset prices. Pooled capacity is cheaper per load because peaks cancel, so big loads want to lean on it. The lock is the grid's own reliability need, so lean months can't drain it; pledges cover them.","why_it_fails":"Big loads can self-supply, capping the due; regulators can bend its level; batteries age and cheaper tech can strand units; local units tie old age to the local economy unless pooled across grids; and the grid alone is too small to absorb every worker's savings.","medium_term":"Pilot where load is surging: data-center tariffs require contracted community units, platforms withhold a tenth, demand-response pay settles in units, and a registry publishes metered shares.","long_term_vision":"Power first, then water, heat and flood defense: every network's bearing layer is owned by people who never had a steady month. Each generation's reserve is larger, so the town can carry more; spare units move to weak nodes and new microgrids, and the old are the base it stands on."},"selfAudit":{"bottleneckRelief":"clear","fiat":"borderline","capabilityProvenance":"mixed","rationale":"In the source, R3 delivers every unbalanced push to the rim and R4 counts only present weight, so collection, timing-blindness and the lock come free by assumption. The candidate rebuilds them with telemetry, liens and reliability rules, and the due's steadiness then rests partly on regulators treating it as a long-term standing charge. Steadiness is direct from world rules in the source; withholding, pledges, edible credits, paid presence and easing are design amplifications."},"isolation":{"compiler":"fresh_context"},"operatorTargetTerms":[],"source":{"kind":"world","worldNodeId":"world.buttress","solutionNodeId":"solve.buttress","commissionNodeId":null,"retryOfNodeId":null}},"task":{"role":"compiler","graphHash":"434e8e9b46e8d1ae703f278d1ebb1ff80f83862df07ac180b4b4320a79860495","taskHash":"7e76ec232fc7262ad40c29e957e256cb59fd3a5dc71164111cf0fd730d69af68","targetBlind":false,"purposeBlind":false},"searchClock":{"rootId":"alien.understanding.21a77a717ac710789574e26e","unit":"search_step","at":8,"index":0}}

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"mechanism","data":{"operator":"Value that grows with the square of the unbroken length of a maintained state, and restarts its count at any gap, is supplied to each maintained party by a rotating pool of intermittent maintainers who are released and credited only when a successor confirms takeover. Because each maintainer contributes whichever resource they have spare at the moment, continuity becomes a property of the maintained party, produced by the pool's overlap rather than by any one member's regularity.","roles":[{"id":"maintained_party","description":"The one whose accrued value depends on how long its maintained state has gone unbroken; it owns the span even though others produce it.","worldRuleIds":["R2","R4"]},{"id":"intermittent_maintainers","description":"Many irregular contributors who each hold the state for a while; whatever any of them can make out is held, so together they cover more than any one could.","worldRuleIds":["R1","R3"]},{"id":"overlap_handover","description":"The only regularity asked of anyone: do not release until a successor confirms takeover within a short grace; a no-show lengthens the current hold instead of breaking it.","worldRuleIds":["R1"]},{"id":"superlinear_span_accrual","description":"Accrued value grows with the square of each unbroken span; a gap keeps what was gained but restarts the count, so gaps, not unevenness, destroy value.","worldRuleIds":["R4"]},{"id":"convertible_contribution","description":"One unit that accepts whichever resource is spare now, money when busy or hours when idle, weighted by how heavy the hold is.","worldRuleIds":["R1","R2","R5"]},{"id":"successor_minted_record","description":"A witnessed record in media that do not decay, in which each credit is issued by the successor at takeover and so proves unbrokenness; entries are added freely but removed only with everyone's consent.","worldRuleIds":["R1","R2"]},{"id":"knowing_circle","description":"A small mixed group whose members know one another; understanding gives the deepest hold, cannot be bought, and never accrues to those who do not take part.","worldRuleIds":["R3","R2"]},{"id":"continuity_backstop","description":"Standbys, a store for lean periods, doubled holds where a gap would be costly, rest limits, and assessors who measure how heavy each hold is.","worldRuleIds":["R1","R3","R5"]}],"magicalElements":[{"element":"Unkept things and selves lose their particulars (R2)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Tend what really decays here without upkeep, fastest for uneven earners: pots raided in lean months, contribution records with gaps under minimum-weeks rules, scattered small pots and dormant accounts, ties that fade within months without contact, and being known."}},{"element":"Tenure grows with the square of the unbroken span; a break restarts the count (R4)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"Share the surplus by the sum of squared unbroken membership spans, with a flat floor. A span breaks only on exit or a year not kept, never in a lean month; sickness and caring count as kept; spans move between circles by overlapping transfer. Real echo: interest on an untouched steady trickle grows at least with the square of its span, and a withdrawal is the break."}},{"element":"Unbroken vigil with a five-second grace and overlapping handover (R1)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"Continuity of responsibility, not of gaze: every member always has a named holder (monthly while working, daily or nightly when frail, continuous when dying), with a grace set per service. The holder is released and credited only on relief; no-shows extend the shift at double credit; standbys cover."}},{"element":"Stones and seats as a ledger lapse cannot touch, because ink fades (R2, R1)","fix":{"kind":"invented_technology","text":"Relief-signed tokens: the incoming holder's phone signs the outgoing holder's credit by tap or QR (a countersigned passbook without a smartphone), hash-chained per member so any gap beyond the grace shows, copied to every circle phone, and recounted in the open each year as in savings groups (VSLAs); one lifelong seat stapled to one pot held by a licensed custodian."}},{"element":"Coin is typical and keeps itself (R2)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"One locked, low-cost diversified pot for life that takes any amount at any time (Kenya's Mbao micro-pension via M-Pesa, Colombia's BEPS with a 20% match, Australia's stapled super), with no early cash-out; hour credits are denominated in hours, so inflation cannot erode them."}},{"element":"Night is the tide of lapse and the oil store keeps lamps lit (R3)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"Here the tide is the lean month. A mutual bridge fund (like a VSLA social fund or a US pension-linked emergency account) pays lapse-critical bills: voluntary pension contributions that keep state records gapless, premiums, the phone line. It is repaid in money or hours, and circles mix trades whose lean seasons differ."}},{"element":"Waking attention is productive for anyone and is paid by weight (R1, R5)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Care time banks (Japan's Fureai Kippu, St. Gallen's city-backed Zeitvorsorge) and carers' pension credits (Germany, UK Carer's Credit), plus a worker-owned care co-op selling gapless shifts (hospital sitters, which cut delirium in the Hospital Elder Life Program, respite, postpartum nights): cash now, weighted credits later."}},{"element":"Weighers feel how heavy a charge is (R5)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Yearly standardized frailty, care-need and isolation assessments (Clinical Frailty Scale, ADL scales, long-term-care grading, Lubben network scale) set hour weights and the mix of close and coarse days, and flag unexpected decline."}},{"element":"Coarse sight keeps a face; only understanding keeps a self (R3)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Coarse keeping is passive monitoring and group calls (Japan's mimamori kettles that alert family when unused). Deep keeping is people who know you: PLAN-style personal networks, life-story work, a shared life file, pooled health-care advocates, and elders who speak migrants' first languages."}},{"element":"Cradle compact: newborns are heavy, long-cured elders light (R5)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"Our frail elders are not light, so the debt is redefined: night support in the 40-day postpartum traditions (cuarentena, zuo yuezi) makes you registered cradle-kin on the godparent/compadrazgo template; the grown child owes visits, calls and advocacy, not heavy care."}},{"element":"A watched clause resists being struck; additions meet no resistance (R1)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"An anti-cutback rule on accrued credits (as ERISA section 204(g) does), an asset lock on reserves, and a personal veto on cuts to one's own accrued rights; additions pass by majority; a short charter is recited at each annual meeting."}},{"element":"Holding the dying, the Turning, the wake and the portrait (R1, R2)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"No One Dies Alone vigils and end-of-life doulas, advance care planning as the agreed letting-go, burial societies (South Africa) or iddir (Ethiopia) for the funeral, and the circle and cradle-kin for the life story."}},{"element":"Long-kept elders are cheap to keep, so the physics pays the Round (R4, R5)","fix":{"kind":"unresolved","text":"Continuity of care and social ties reduce hospital use and mortality somewhat, and capitated care (PACE) can capture part of it, but dementia and frailty stay heavy; heavy care must be paid from pots, credits and insurance, not from continuity."}},{"element":"New kinds slide into the nearest old kind (R4)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"Regulators will file a novel mutual as an insurer, a deposit-taker or a Ponzi. Charter it as existing kinds (cooperative, licensed pension provider, time bank) on standard templates, and seed it from burial societies, VSLAs and credit unions."}},{"element":"Lone travellers and the unknown go typical; the circle vouches (R2, R3)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Travellers and migrants keep a paired holder at home who keeps ties, records and payments current, and they hold others by phone; circle attestation stands in for missing papers, like introducer-based ID enrolment in India's Aadhaar."}},{"element":"Burden burns off only in sleep; sleepless keepers lapse (R5)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Rest limits: no credit for shifts beyond a cap or without rest, respite rotas, and a two-person rule on heavy shifts that also guards against abuse."}}],"strangest":{"element":"Continuity belongs to the kept and is made by others: the account is a chain of handovers, each credit minted by the successor, and its value grows with the square of its unbroken length, so the least regular member can own the longest chain.","preserved":"Every credit is minted by the next holder's signature at relief; the floor and the squared surplus share are keyed to the member's unbroken chain, not to payments; a lean month cannot break it, only exit can; moving circles is itself an overlapping handover."},"candidate":{"label":"Long Round: relief-signed continuity","design_principles":"Make the pool regular, not the person. Accrue on unbroken membership, not payments. Take money or hours. Credit on relief. Only exit breaks a chain. Keep the self in people. Cuts need unanimity.","core_mechanism":"Each member always has a named holder; a holder is credited only when the successor signs 'I have it', adding a link to the member's chain; surplus is shared by squared unbroken span.","how_it_works":"Circles of ~12 households, mixed by trade and lean season, rota a named holder for each member: monthly check-ins while working, nightly presence when frail, a vigil at death. A holder is released only on relief; a no-show extends the shift at double credit. Dues: money into one locked lifelong pot when busy, weighted care hours when idle. A bridge fund pays lapse-critical bills. Handover tokens sit in a replicated open ledger. Kept years earn the floor; squared spans share surplus.","what_is_new":"Accrual keyed to an unbroken chain others produce, not one's payments; credit minted by the successor at relief; only exit, never a bad month, breaks it; part of the payout is being known.","why_it_works":"Hold-until-relieved plus standbys turns many unreliable shifts into one gapless chain. Spare money and spare hours peak at opposite times, so dues in either are steadier than pay. Untouched pots compound, known people are noticed early, and only exit costs, so members stay.","why_it_fails":"Money still follows pay, so low earners get small pots. Hour credits need nearby demand, trust and vetting, and may be taxed as wages. Squared spans favour founders and make leaving costly. Grant-fed schemes often fade; frail elders stay heavy here. Close circles can turn nosy or coercive.","medium_term":"Pilot in existing mutuals (burial societies, VSLAs, credit unions) in one town: holder rota, relief-signed tokens, bridge fund, hospital sitter contracts paying lean-month hours.","long_term_vision":"A federation of circles where anyone, however erratic their pay, reaches old age with an unbroken chain of people who took hold of them, a pot never raided, and a dozen who know them; state pensions credit kept years, and continuity is sold to health systems as care."},"selfAudit":{"bottleneckRelief":"partial","fiat":"pass","capabilityProvenance":"mixed","rationale":"In the source, R2 makes coin and the stone ledger self-keeping and R4/R5 make long-kept elders cheap, so storage and late-life cost are relieved by assumption. The candidate rebuilds storage with a locked pot, a bridge fund and a replicated ledger, and does not rely on cheap elders, which stays unresolved. The principal operation (hold until relieved, credit on relief, standbys) produces continuity mechanically and does not assert adequacy: money still follows pay. Provenance is mixed: compounding, open-meeting accounting, time banks and care co-ops supply capability directly, and the relay amplifies many irregular contributors into gapless cover."},"isolation":{"compiler":"fresh_context"},"operatorTargetTerms":[],"source":{"kind":"world","worldNodeId":"world.vigil","solutionNodeId":"solve.vigil","commissionNodeId":null,"retryOfNodeId":null}},"task":{"role":"compiler","graphHash":"41583e439c3fb55b555b9fd0cb78130d17f4fce00b3abcfe784cbb26378cf954","taskHash":"082a8ca88e2845766cbb268db0f1820a4778e1c91683483b842b0701a2739c8e","targetBlind":false,"purposeBlind":false},"searchClock":{"rootId":"alien.understanding.21a77a717ac710789574e26e","unit":"search_step","at":10,"index":0}}

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"mechanism","data":{"operator":"A fixed fraction is cut from each irregular inflow the instant it occurs and irrevocably released, in equal parcels, at many staggered positions upstream of a common collector on a one-way drift that needs no tending and that no party can halt or reverse, so each parcel returns after a delay set by its position. The collector's intake is thereby an average over many past inflows, and it releases a fixed fraction of its stock each period, divided by credit measured against each period's average cut.","roles":[{"id":"proportional_tap","description":"Cuts a fixed fraction from each inflow at the moment it is recorded; a period with no inflow owes nothing, so no forecast is needed. Supplied by the conserved ledger, where every gain has a recorded counterpart.","worldRuleIds":["R2"]},{"id":"relative_credit","description":"Credits each paying unit by its cut divided by that period's average cut, so a period lean for everyone still earns full credit; paid and credited per balanced pair so neither member drifts from the other.","worldRuleIds":["R2","R3"]},{"id":"neutral_durable_parcel","description":"Turns each cut into parcels that hold their value without tending, look like common matter and exert no net pull on the host: balanced checkerboards of tight whirls.","worldRuleIds":["R2","R3","R4"]},{"id":"one_way_drift","description":"An unstoppable, untended conveyor that brings every placed parcel back toward the collector, with delay set by placement distance and weight; arrival can be late but cannot fail. Supplied by the inward creep, with background shear feeding parcels in transit.","worldRuleIds":["R1","R4"]},{"id":"scatter_kernel","description":"Spreads each period's parcels across about twenty positions so every later period receives parcels from many earlier ones; the averaging is fixed at placement, not decided later. Matched pairs carry the parcels out along straight paths.","worldRuleIds":["R1","R3"]},{"id":"passive_catch_and_sort","description":"A barrier that stops net-neutral arrivals, and a cross-wall that splits each broken pair and routes each half to its own store by geometry rather than judgment.","worldRuleIds":["R5","R3"]},{"id":"fixed_fraction_store","description":"A small stock kept in motion that releases a fixed fraction of itself each period from a still center, so output follows the slowly changing stock rather than the latest arrival.","worldRuleIds":["R5","R4","R1"]},{"id":"neutral_floor_reserve","description":"Whole parcels held back and annihilated on demand into a neutral form usable by either kind, guaranteeing a per-head minimum in lean periods.","worldRuleIds":["R2"]}],"magicalElements":[{"element":"A conserved ledger on which every gain appears exactly and at once, so a share can be cut from any gain and hidden gains show as crime (R2)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Cut inside the payment itself on digital rails, as Poland's VAT split payment does, plus platform, mobile-money and buyer-side withholding. A month with no gain owes nothing and nothing lapses. Cash gains remain a partial hole; a public match on rail cuts would pull some onto rails."}},{"element":"The stone: a carrier that keeps conserved value for decades without tending, looks like any other matter and steers nothing (R2, R3, R4)","fix":{"kind":"invented_technology","text":"A consumption-share strip: a sovereign zero-coupon claim paying, at one maturity, a fixed share of that year's per-capita consumption. Assembled from the SeLFIES and trills proposals, with GDP warrants and Brazil's Tesouro RendA+ as working precedents, and issued as the same fungible series the public holds."}},{"element":"The Slope and the Draw: an untended, unstoppable one-way conveyor that returns every sown stone after a delay set by where it was placed (R1, R4)","fix":{"kind":"invented_technology","text":"The calendar becomes the conveyor and a frozen registry replaces the hillside. Strips are registered to a common catch and cannot be sold, pledged or redeemed early by anyone, under statute plus a time-locked covenant on the securities registry. At maturity they can pay only into the catch, and any early movement is a public, provable breach."}},{"element":"The guarantee: a sown stone may be late but cannot fail to come down (R1)","fix":{"kind":"unresolved","text":"Nothing in our physics brings value back. Strips are only as good as the issuer and its price statistics. Fungibility with the public issue turns a selective raid into a general default, and a later multi-state issuer could make each strip a checkerboard of sovereigns, but certainty is not reached."}},{"element":"Quietness: no Listener can find or single out a stone, while a one-Hand hoard is loud and a target","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"No individual balances and only a pool one to two years deep, so members, managers and legislatures find nothing to withdraw, raid or steer. The emergency withdrawals that emptied accounts in Chile and Peru would have no object."}},{"element":"Timing set by sowing distance and stone weight, across twenty distances per round (R1)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Maturity choice, refined: each cut is split across every year of the payer's likely old age, weighted by survival odds, so every old-age year gets a slice of every working year and a lumpy career lands as a flat stream."}},{"element":"The mirror-wall that splits each pair and sends each half to its own Hand's basin (R5)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"A standing payout instruction that splits each couple's share 50/50 into each partner's own account, as Swiss pension splitting does. No clerk decides."}},{"element":"The self-centering round basin, where a fuller basin sends more to its still eye (R5, R1)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"A fixed-fraction spending rule in the manner of Norway's 3% rule, applied monthly: the pool pays 1/24 of itself by points and is held in short indexed bills."}},{"element":"Froth: balanced stock annihilated on demand into neutral feed for both Hands (R2)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"A slice of each matured strip rolls into a reserve released only when the monthly payment would fall below a per-head floor, paid per head with singles included. The Dutch solidarity reserve and Chile's pension reserve fund are close precedents."}},{"element":"Rounds that hold the same amount of living in every band, because shear per round is constant (R1, R4)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"Everything is denominated in standard-of-living units: points against the month's average cut (the logic of German earnings points), strips paying shares of per-capita consumption, and a floor set as a share of it. No nominal promise appears anywhere."}},{"element":"Twins as the paying unit, re-evened by feeding the weaker up and never cutting down; a half keeps the pair's knots (R2, R3)","fix":{"kind":"institutional_substitute","text":"A household cut with points split equally. At claiming, the first payments top up the lower-credited partner, and a survivor keeps the pair's full points."}},{"element":"Missed stones creep on to an inward town that credits them (R1)","fix":{"kind":"existing_approximation","text":"Totalization and portability rules in the style of EU Regulation 883/2004, plus a statutory successor catch, so no strip matures with nobody downstream."}}],"strangest":{"element":"Keeping is surrendered to the very drift that ruins keeping: each share is placed upstream at many distances, held by no one in transit, and the unstoppable inward creep delivers it, averaged, to whoever stands downstream.","preserved":"The candidate keeps no balance and has no manager. Each cut becomes frozen strips that only the calendar can move and that can land only in the common catch, in the years their payer would be old. Placement is the only decision ever made, averaging is done by the scatter rather than by judgment, and strips of the dead land for the living."},"candidate":{"label":"Delay-Line Share Pension","design_principles":"Shares, never amounts. Cut at the moment of gain. Keep no balance: release each cut, frozen, across many future years. Let the calendar deliver. Credit relative to peers. Floor from reserve.","core_mechanism":"A fixed share of each payment is cut at the rail and turned into frozen consumption-share strips maturing over the payer's old age into a common pool that pays a fixed fraction by points.","how_it_works":"Payment rails split ~10% off every gain; a month with no gain owes nothing. Points = your cut / that month's average cut, split 50/50 in couples. Each cut buys sovereign strips paying shares of per-capita consumption, one per year of the payer's likely old age (survival-weighted). Strips sit frozen: no sale, loan or early cash-in. Matured strips land in one pool paying 1/24 of itself monthly by points; strips of the dead feed the living. A reserve slice pays a per-head floor in lean years.","what_is_new":"A pension with no balance and no manager: savings exist only as frozen strips in transit, so nothing can be raided, withdrawn or steered, and smoothing comes from scatter geometry, not judgment.","why_it_works":"Proportional cuts need no forecast; relative points protect common lean months; slicing every cut across all old-age years flattens a lumpy career into a flat stream; consumption shares keep pace without recalculation; frozen strips shut the leakage that drained Chile's and Peru's accounts.","why_it_fails":"No law of nature guarantees arrival: strips are only as good as the issuing state and its statistics office (Argentina bent its CPI). Cash gains dodge the rail; a cut with no emergency access may push workers into cash; real yields are low; a legislature can still unfreeze the registry.","medium_term":"Pilot on one gig platform or mobile-money rail using existing inflation-linked zero-coupon debt in a locked trust; publish every cut, catch and payout; seek a first consumption-share strip issue.","long_term_vision":"Every payment rail carries a share-cut; states issue consumption-share strips for every future year; schemes credit each other's strips; old age is paid as a steady share of the living standard, built from whatever people earned, whenever they happened to earn it."},"selfAudit":{"bottleneckRelief":"partial","fiat":"pass","capabilityProvenance":"mixed","rationale":"R2 makes recording automatic and R1 with R4 make keeping and delivery automatic by assumption, but the irregularity bottleneck itself, turning lumpy intake into a steady outflow, is solved by the scatter and the fixed-fraction draw, which transplant intact; hence partial. Smoothness is derived arithmetically, not asserted, and the floor is bounded by a finite reserve. Keeping is direct from R1 and R4; smoothing is amplified by design. In our world the relieved functions become the weak points: rail capture is partial and the delivery guarantee is unresolved."},"isolation":{"compiler":"fresh_context"},"operatorTargetTerms":[],"source":{"kind":"world","worldNodeId":"world.whirlpool","solutionNodeId":"solve.whirlpool","commissionNodeId":null,"retryOfNodeId":null}},"task":{"role":"compiler","graphHash":"29bd726909f7c928ffe9ec4029250c91d61560b7093bb354aa156ad8b2c856c9","taskHash":"e2c2812c74dbd834758e231789dcb7ca259744d6b2811299d62d64f0b42bdd92","targetBlind":false,"purposeBlind":false},"searchClock":{"rootId":"alien.understanding.21a77a717ac710789574e26e","unit":"search_step","at":12,"index":0}}

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"ontology_revision","data":{"ontology":"worlds","previousRevisionNodeId":"wrev.2","decision":{"verdict":"admit_new","subjectNodeId":"world.whirlpool","conceptId":"regime.twinned-induction","nearestConceptId":"regime.held-metastability","equivalence":{"nameChanged":true,"actorChanged":true,"parameterChanged":true,"inputSignalChanged":true,"primaryOperatorChanged":true,"explanation":"Nearest: the root held metastability; its leaves overlap only in part (observational upkeep on flow-kept records and rote reciters, relational load path on cancelling opposites and wall-completed balance). Test: is the Turning Deep that operator with only names, actors, parameters or signals swapped? No. Held metastability needs a holder distinct from the held thing that takes on the displaced pressure and passes it on or sheds it. Here a whirl answers its own unravelling by feeding on ambient shear, and nothing accrues in the Maelstrom, tenders or reciters. Failure is two-sided (starve or tear), and the conserved quantity is the thing's own turn, which death spreads rather than drains. Most structure comes from operators the ontology lacks: twin-only creation and company-only motion with mirror partners."},"fit":null,"signature":{"temporality":{"code":"one-way inward drift, no stable orbit; round ~ r^2 per band; instant stir","note":"The Draw makes every orbit decay inward, so aging, sinking and 'older' coincide: towns are founded at the Rim, grow rich inward and are torn apart at the Wall. A round quarters when distance halves, so each band keeps its own calendar and inner lives run hot and short. Stir acts instantly at any range. Unravelling spreads a whirl into its surroundings; the laws give no way back."},"conservation":{"code":"signed turn conserved: made/unmade only in opposite twins; death spreads it","note":"Turn is never created or destroyed, only divided. Equal opposites meeting become froth, itself paired spray, which frays into still Deep; eating merges like hands, burning cancels unlike ones. A starved whirl's turn widens into its surroundings instead of vanishing, so a graveyard carries a faint net hand. The ledger can therefore close exactly: every gain has a twin somewhere, and unexplained turn is evidence of crime."},"agency":{"code":"company-only: no self-motion; pairs travel, walls carry; steering spends turn","note":"No whirl or braid can move its own heart by moving its parts. Alone, a person goes only where the Floor's drift carries her or one way along a wall; with an equal opposite partner she travels straight, and every corner costs a trim pellet swallowed by one partner and later matched by the other. Towns steer by the balance of turn between their halves, so trade is navigation. Power is choosing company: pairing, splitting at walls, seating a checkerboard, or forcing a merge."},"identity":{"code":"processual: a thing is its turning, not its matter; the twin pair is the unit","note":"The Deep passes through every whirl, so what persists is pattern, never substance; hand, turn, eye and draw describe a thing completely, and a person is a braid of whirls around one heart-eye. Every birth is a twin birth, so the pair, with mirrored names and an even bowl, is the social unit, and one whose twin has died is a half. A thing ends by unravelling, by being torn, or by merging with a like hand within three eye-widths, after which neither survives as itself."},"scarcity":{"code":"scarce: livable shear band, outward ground, keeping flow, matched partners","note":"Only the middle bands are livable: the Rim starves, the Wall tears, the Eye stills. Holding a town's band against the inward creep is the steady work of civic life. Keeping anything needs moving Deep, so tending is the largest trade, and every wall trades mirror against feed. Travel needs an equal opposite partner, hence matchers; and making one thing makes an unwanted twin that must be stored far from its partner."},"information_flow":{"code":"instant stir, any range: loners loud, pairs quiet; records live while turning","note":"Every whirl stirs the whole Deep instantly; there is no light and no contact. A loner's stir carries far, while a pair's two stirs cancel at a distance, the closer the quieter: any loner can be placed, a close pair hardly found, and the Hum of all loners swells toward the Wall. To be felt far away needs a strong lone whirl whose twin is kept far off. Records are knotted whirl-patterns that unravel when their flow stops, so archives are carousels kept turning by rote."},"boundary_structure":{"code":"walls mirror opposite hand; calm in walled checkerboards; life in mid-bands","note":"A solid boundary answers each nearby whirl with an opposite-handed mirror, so walls carry loners one way, split arriving pairs, sort crowds by Hand and starve the rooms they shelter; a sealed room is a small Eye. Stillness needs a checkerboard of both hands: a stone is one, and a council is one walled on its outer cell edges so the mirrors complete the pattern; one wrong seat sets the room creeping. At world scale the Rim starves, the Wall tears and the Eye stills; the Throat is a one-way exit."},"permitted_transformations":{"code":"make only in twins, merge like, burn unlike; sinking free, outward costly","note":"Spinning up needs an equal opposite twin, so goods come in twin lots and counterstock must be stored apart; equal opposites meeting become froth, which burners meter into heat. Like hands within three eye-widths merge (eating, welding, growth); unlike hands cancel in part (burning). Stirring sorts heavy to the eye and loose to the rim. Sinking inward is the default; holding a band or climbing outward takes a balanced town and steady work. Too little shear spreads a whirl; too much tears it to froth."},"enforcement":{"code":"automatic, instant physical; social law mirrors the turn ledger and pairing","note":"Physics enforces itself: an unequal pair circles, a one-handed crush merges into one whirl, a sealed room starves. Social law copies the conservation: ledgerers record where every twin lies, and the gravest crime, a forced merge, shows as sudden unexplained turn. Twins share the even bowl so they can keep travelling straight together; stillness is taboo; councils need every seat correctly filled."}},"redirect":null,"rationale":"Primary operator. The Turning Deep runs on one integrated mechanism. A thing is a signed turning of a medium that can only flow, and it keeps no material. Its turn is conserved and is made only with an equal opposite twin (R2). It cannot move or feed itself; it is carried and fed only by others' stir (core, R3, R4). Walls act as opposite-handed partners (R5), and every whirl is a sink (R1). Most of the society follows from R2, R3 and R5: twin births and the pair as the unit, the two Hands, one-way wall-roads, checkerboard councils, towns steered by the turn balance between their halves, matchers and couriers, counterstock and burners, the turn-ledger, and listeners who hear loners loudly and pairs quietly. R4 and R1 add the livable band, the inward creep, band calendars and upkeep by flow. Equivalence test. Only one clause resembles held metastability: things unravel toward still Deep unless something keeps them. But it differs in the parts that make held metastability a regime. Nothing takes on displaced pressure: whirls feed on ambient shear, and tenders and reciters supply flow without accruing anything, resting, or passing anything on. Failure is two-sided (starve at the Rim, tear at the Wall), not one-way relaxation. The conserved quantity is the order's own turn, which death spreads rather than drains. The operators that carry most of the world (twin creation, company-only motion, mirror partners) have no counterpart in either leaf. The primary operator changed, not only names, actors (tenders for keepers), parameters (the band) or signals (shear for attention or contact). Admit_new. Restructuring. The new root is regime.twinned-induction. The world also exposes an assumption in the only existing root: that decay is answered by a distinct bearer. Here order is kept moving and fed rather than held still. Stillness is the taboo, 'keep turning' the blessing, and a town holds its band by balanced travel, not by support. I record this as an opposition to held metastability rather than building an empty parent from one world; the operations say what should trigger the lift. I add paired analogy and opposition relations with relational load path (cancelling opposites, boundary-completed balance and one missing element versus contact chains, ballasted sinks and instant collapse) and with observational upkeep (rote reciters and carousel archives versus borne burden, rest and tenure). No existing concept is merged, split or reworded. Signature. No existing code matches any axis, so all nine codes are new. The nearest overlaps are boundary_structure (a cancelling interior as in load path, but walls complete the balance by mirroring, not by bearing net load) and enforcement (automatic physics, but social law copies the turn-ledger). Consistency. The laws cohere: speed doubling at half distance, rounds quartering and shear quadrupling all follow from one inverse-distance field. {"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"assessment","data":{"subjectNodeIds":["search.retirement.problem"],"verdict":"Target model context review (revision 1)","text":"Context review of the target model irregular-income-retirement, revision 1 (34182691), done after reading the Meaning Model paper and before any transfer.

Question: ideas for a retirement system for people whose monthly earnings are unpredictable.

Focal interval: an illustrative household life course of forty years of working life (months 0 to 480) and twenty years of retirement (480 to 720).

Broader context, partly represented: the household, its clients and platforms, a pension provider, the state's pension, tax and benefit rules, and the household's close circle are referents, so transfers can bind roles to them. Not represented as processes: the labour market and platform economy, prices and interest rates, and asset returns. At this resolution they are out of scope. No mechanism's value is computed from the model, so leaving them out cannot bias a transfer, but it means no transfer is evaluated here.

Longer-term developments, explicitly unknown: demographic ageing, the growth of platform work, and changes to public pension rules over the sixty-year horizon. They bear on whether a transferred mechanism would hold over a lifetime. The model has no sources for them, so they stay unknown rather than guessed.

Values: every process value is an authored illustrative figure with no source. Revision 0 marked them observed, which was wrong; revision 1 marks them unspecified and says they are illustrative. They support role mapping, not estimation.

Consequence for the search: transfers may bind mechanism roles to the model's actors, phases and stocks. Any claim about effects needs later modeling with sources."},"searchClock":{"rootId":"alien.understanding.21a77a717ac710789574e26e","unit":"search_step","at":15,"index":0}}

{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"task","data":{"role":"curator","inputs":{"subjectNodeId":"mech.delay-line","ontology":"mechanisms"},"text":"You are the curator of this search's mechanism ontology. You own admission and every change to it.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

Current mechanism ontology:
- [fam.external-regularity] Regularity supplied by others: 0 direct, 2 in subtree
  operator: The steadiness a saver cannot supply is supplied by a structure of other people: the benefit is keyed to something others depend on or maintain, never to the saver's own regular payments.
  partition fam.external-regularity.by-what-others-supply, lens: what the others supply: a standing dependence that pays rent to the saver's part (bearing), or a maintained continuity that accrues to the saver (relay)
    - [fam.bearing-rent] Savings as rented bearing capacity: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: Contributions of any size and timing become parts that carry a standing load others depend on; the dependents pay the owners in proportion to the measured load each part carries, and the same dependence locks the parts in service, so claims can change hands but the capital cannot be withdrawn.
      instances: Mantle Grid: a Load-Bearing Pension [mech.mantle-grid]
    - [fam.relay-continuity] Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: A value that grows superlinearly with the unbroken span of a maintained state, and restarts its count at a gap, is produced for each member by a rotating pool of intermittent maintainers who are released and credited only when a successor confirms takeover; each pays in whatever resource is spare, so continuity is a property of the member rather than of anyone's regularity.
      instances: Long Round: relief-signed continuity [mech.long-round]

Candidate under review (mech.delay-line, compiled from world world.whirlpool (seed whirlpool)):
Operator: A fixed fraction is cut from each irregular inflow the instant it occurs and irrevocably released, in equal parcels, at many staggered positions upstream of a common collector on a one-way drift that needs no tending and that no party can halt or reverse, so each parcel returns after a delay set by its position. The collector's intake is thereby an average over many past inflows, and it releases a fixed fraction of its stock each period, divided by credit measured against each period's average cut.
Roles: proportional_tap (Cuts a fixed fraction from each inflow at the moment it is recorded; a period with no inflow owes nothing, so no forecast is needed. Supplied by the conserved ledger, where every gain has a recorded counterpart.); relative_credit (Credits each paying unit by its cut divided by that period's average cut, so a period lean for everyone still earns full credit; paid and credited per balanced pair so neither member drifts from the other.); neutral_durable_parcel (Turns each cut into parcels that hold their value without tending, look like common matter and exert no net pull on the host: balanced checkerboards of tight whirls.); one_way_drift (An unstoppable, untended conveyor that brings every placed parcel back toward the collector, with delay set by placement distance and weight; arrival can be late but cannot fail. Supplied by the inward creep, with background shear feeding parcels in transit.); scatter_kernel (Spreads each period's parcels across about twenty positions so every later period receives parcels from many earlier ones; the averaging is fixed at placement, not decided later. Matched pairs carry the parcels out along straight paths.); passive_catch_and_sort (A barrier that stops net-neutral arrivals, and a cross-wall that splits each broken pair and routes each half to its own store by geometry rather than judgment.); fixed_fraction_store (A small stock kept in motion that releases a fixed fraction of itself each period from a still center, so output follows the slowly changing stock rather than the latest arrival.); neutral_floor_reserve (Whole parcels held back and annihilated on demand into a neutral form usable by either kind, guaranteeing a per-head minimum in lean periods.)
Strangest element: Keeping is surrendered to the very drift that ruins keeping: each share is placed upstream at many distances, held by no one in transit, and the unstoppable inward creep delivers it, averaged, to whoever stands downstream.. Kept as: The candidate keeps no balance and has no manager. Each cut becomes frozen strips that only the calendar can move and that can land only in the common catch, in the years their payer would be old. Placement is the only decision ever made, averaging is done by the scatter rather than by judgment, and strips of the dead land for the living.
Magical elements: A conserved ledger on which every gain appears exactly and at once, so a share can be cut from any gain and hidden gains show as crime (R2) -> existing_approximation: Cut inside the payment itself on digital rails, as Poland's VAT split payment does, plus platform, mobile-money and buyer-side withholding. A month with no gain owes nothing and nothing lapses. Cash gains remain a partial hole; a public match on rail cuts would pull some onto rails.; The stone: a carrier that keeps conserved value for decades without tending, looks like any other matter and steers nothing (R2, R3, R4) -> invented_technology: A consumption-share strip: a sovereign zero-coupon claim paying, at one maturity, a fixed share of that year's per-capita consumption. Assembled from the SeLFIES and trills proposals, with GDP warrants and Brazil's Tesouro RendA+ as working precedents, and issued as the same fungible series the public holds.; The Slope and the Draw: an untended, unstoppable one-way conveyor that returns every sown stone after a delay set by where it was placed (R1, R4) -> invented_technology: The calendar becomes the conveyor and a frozen registry replaces the hillside. Strips are registered to a common catch and cannot be sold, pledged or redeemed early by anyone, under statute plus a time-locked covenant on the securities registry. At maturity they can pay only into the catch, and any early movement is a public, provable breach.; The guarantee: a sown stone may be late but cannot fail to come down (R1) -> unresolved: Nothing in our physics brings value back. Strips are only as good as the issuer and its price statistics. Fungibility with the public issue turns a selective raid into a general default, and a later multi-state issuer could make each strip a checkerboard of sovereigns, but certainty is not reached.; Quietness: no Listener can find or single out a stone, while a one-Hand hoard is loud and a target -> institutional_substitute: No individual balances and only a pool one to two years deep, so members, managers and legislatures find nothing to withdraw, raid or steer. The emergency withdrawals that emptied accounts in Chile and Peru would have no object.; Timing set by sowing distance and stone weight, across twenty distances per round (R1) -> existing_approximation: Maturity choice, refined: each cut is split across every year of the payer's likely old age, weighted by survival odds, so every old-age year gets a slice of every working year and a lumpy career lands as a flat stream.; The mirror-wall that splits each pair and sends each half to its own Hand's basin (R5) -> institutional_substitute: A standing payout instruction that splits each couple's share 50/50 into each partner's own account, as Swiss pension splitting does. No clerk decides.; The self-centering round basin, where a fuller basin sends more to its still eye (R5, R1) -> existing_approximation: A fixed-fraction spending rule in the manner of Norway's 3% rule, applied monthly: the pool pays 1/24 of itself by points and is held in short indexed bills.; Froth: balanced stock annihilated on demand into neutral feed for both Hands (R2) -> existing_approximation: A slice of each matured strip rolls into a reserve released only when the monthly payment would fall below a per-head floor, paid per head with singles included. The Dutch solidarity reserve and Chile's pension reserve fund are close precedents.; Rounds that hold the same amount of living in every band, because shear per round is constant (R1, R4) -> institutional_substitute: Everything is denominated in standard-of-living units: points against the month's average cut (the logic of German earnings points), strips paying shares of per-capita consumption, and a floor set as a share of it. No nominal promise appears anywhere.; Twins as the paying unit, re-evened by feeding the weaker up and never cutting down; a half keeps the pair's knots (R2, R3) -> institutional_substitute: A household cut with points split equally. At claiming, the first payments top up the lower-credited partner, and a survivor keeps the pair's full points.; Missed stones creep on to an inward town that credits them (R1) -> existing_approximation: Totalization and portability rules in the style of EU Regulation 883/2004, plus a statutory successor catch, so no strip matures with nobody downstream.
Candidate:
  label: Delay-Line Share Pension
  design_principles: Shares, never amounts. Cut at the moment of gain. Keep no balance: release each cut, frozen, across many future years. Let the calendar deliver. Credit relative to peers. Floor from reserve.
  core_mechanism: A fixed share of each payment is cut at the rail and turned into frozen consumption-share strips maturing over the payer's old age into a common pool that pays a fixed fraction by points.
  how_it_works: Payment rails split ~10% off every gain; a month with no gain owes nothing. Points = your cut / that month's average cut, split 50/50 in couples. Each cut buys sovereign strips paying shares of per-capita consumption, one per year of the payer's likely old age (survival-weighted). Strips sit frozen: no sale, loan or early cash-in. Matured strips land in one pool paying 1/24 of itself monthly by points; strips of the dead feed the living. A reserve slice pays a per-head floor in lean years.
  what_is_new: A pension with no balance and no manager: savings exist only as frozen strips in transit, so nothing can be raided, withdrawn or steered, and smoothing comes from scatter geometry, not judgment.
  why_it_works: Proportional cuts need no forecast; relative points protect common lean months; slicing every cut across all old-age years flattens a lumpy career into a flat stream; consumption shares keep pace without recalculation; frozen strips shut the leakage that drained Chile's and Peru's accounts.
  why_it_fails: No law of nature guarantees arrival: strips are only as good as the issuing state and its statistics office (Argentina bent its CPI). Cash gains dodge the rail; a cut with no emergency access may push workers into cash; real yields are low; a legislature can still unfreeze the registry.
  medium_term: Pilot on one gig platform or mobile-money rail using existing inflation-linked zero-coupon debt in a locked trust; publish every cut, catch and payout; seek a first consumption-share strip issue.
  long_term_vision: Every payment rail carries a share-cut; states issue consumption-share strips for every future year; schemes credit each other's strips; old age is paid as a steady share of the living standard, built from whatever people earned, whenever they happened to earn it.
