{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"task","data":{"role":"curator","inputs":{"subjectNodeId":"mech.mantle-grid","ontology":"outcomes"},"text":"You curate the claimed outcomes of candidate interventions: what each claims to achieve for the people it serves, not the mechanism by which it does so.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

Current outcome ontology (each class's operator states the outcome that defines it):
(empty)

Candidate under review (mech.mantle-grid):
Operator: Additions of any size and timing count only by the amount present and are placed where they bear part of a slowly changing load that others stand on; the dependents pay the bearers in proportion to the load each part is measured to carry. The same dependence locks each part in place: a claim on it can change hands, but the part leaves only when a replacement takes its load.
Roles: bearing_stock (An accumulating layer of load-bearing parts built from additions of any size at any time; its strength counts only what is present now, and it grows at a self-stable slope without temporary support (stone laid on a course at repose).); held_dependents (Tall standing structures that cannot stand without the layer; the support each needs grows with the square of its height, unbalanced pushes pass link by link to the layer, and equal pushes cancel (towers leaning outward onto the rim).); standing_due (A rent the held pay the bearers for as long as they stand, first among claims and scaled to the push each sends outward, enforced because withdrawing support drops the held permanently while costing the already-low bearers almost nothing (the rim-due backed by the Stoop).); load_meter (A direct reading of what each bearing part actually carries, which sets its share and flags broken or creeping links (loaded chains ring, slack ones thud).); functional_lock (Committed parts held in place by the friction of the load they carry; removing one needs temporary support and the consent of everything upstream and downstream, so claims move by deed while the part stays (keyed stone).); growth_gate (A new tall structure cannot drop its temporary support until it has acquired uncommitted bearing parts; those parts lock and start collecting its rent that day (raisings key loose stone).); edible_buffer (An uncommitted tier stored inside the layer that adds strength while held and can be consumed, or released once the meter shows the layer holds without it (grain in buried rim bins).); low_heavy_bearers (Bodies that age into shapes cheap to hold and good at bearing, and idle bodies that add weight at the vulnerable night hours; both are paid in bearing stock rather than cash (mantled elders, night ballast).)
Strangest element: There is no pot: savings exist only as load-bearing parts of what others stand on, so the dependence that pays the rent is the same dependence that locks the stone, and old age means joining the bearing layer rather than drawing down a store.. Kept as: Contributions are issued only as registered slices of in-service capacity counted in the reliability margin. No cash balance exists: a keyed unit is pledged or passed by deed, its hardware leaves service only when replaced, and retirees join the bearing layer, even hosting their units at home as a mantle battery.
Magical elements: Every unbalanced push in town is delivered to the rim by physics (R3), so tall things truly depend on the bearers and the due is a price, not a tax -> existing_approximation: Firm capacity in a power network: each connection's peak is carried node by node to shared firming plants, diverse peaks cancel so pooled holding is cheaper per load, the largest single unit or load sets the reserve, and new large loads increasingly must bring or pay for firm capacity before energizing.; The due grows with the square of height, and anything under the Hold needs no holding (R1) -> institutional_substitute: A standing due that is zero up to a base allowance per connection (an ordinary home's peak) and convex above it, rising with a load's share of its node, where contingency and reinforcement costs concentrate.; Dead weight earns: a stone grounds thrust the day it is laid and counts only by present weight (R4) -> invented_technology: Registry-tracked micro-slices of already-operating, accredited storage capacity, bought in any amount through mobile or platform payments; the proceeds fund the next module (asset recycling), so each unit works from purchase and earns by units held now.; Keyed stone locks itself by the friction of its own load; removal needs re-centering and consent (R2, R3, R5) -> existing_approximation: Reliability rules that bar a resource counted in the reserve margin from retiring without replacement (reliability-must-run contracts, capacity obligations). Claims move by registry deed; no cash balance exists for a saver's panic or a treasurer's raid.; The ring: a struck pier's pitch states its load -> existing_approximation: Interval telemetry and performance-based accreditation (effective load-carrying capability, availability tests) published monthly; each unit's measured contribution sets its share, and a failed test is a thud that earns nothing that month.; The Stoop: the low can drop the tall at almost no cost to themselves; disputes settle at the pool where all stand equal -> institutional_substitute: The due is a super-priority lien collected like property tax, and connections above the base allowance with unpaid dues are curtailed first in scarcity events, so the threat falls only on the tall. Disputes go to an open weekly lay tribunal modeled on Valencia's Tribunal de las Aguas.; Aging makes a body a better buttress: shorter, heavier, stone-mantled (R1, R4, R5) -> institutional_substitute: Retirement as a change of role inside the bearing layer: keyed units carry load for the retiree, and at easing loose units can move into the home as a dispatchable battery that stays in the reserve and keeps a backup floor for outages (cf. South Australia's public-housing virtual power plant). Age itself adds nothing.; Night ballast: a sleeping body strengthens a pier at the vulnerable hour -> existing_approximation: Demand-response calls on the coldest and hottest nights, rent for hosting modules, and site-watch shifts at storage yards, paid out of the due and settled in units rather than cash.; Grain in rim bins: ballast you can eat -> invented_technology: Loose units bank stored-energy credits that count as available reserve while held and can be spent on the saver's own power bill in a thin month, or sold back once the metered report shows the reserve holds without them.; A raising cannot strike its centering until the rim can ground it (R5, R1, R4) -> existing_approximation: Concurrency rules and recent data-center tariffs that make large loads pay for most of their contracted capacity for years; in the candidate a new large load must contract loose units, which key and collect its due from energization.; Frost makes lenders and borrowers naturally opposite -> institutional_substitute: A capped pledge exchange: a slice of a keyed unit's due goes to a lender until a fat month redeems it, matched across trades with opposite seasons; the hardware never moves.; Holdfasts: bare bedrock grounds twice the thrust per weight (R4) -> existing_approximation: Locational capacity value: units at constrained nodes displace costly wires (non-wires alternatives) and earn more, so the common pool that gives every elder a seat is sited there.; Stone never decays and the dead stay in the rim as weight, so each generation's rim is heavier -> institutional_substitute: Units are perpetual capacity slots: a renewal reserve from the due replaces aging cells (augmentation); units pass by deed at death, unclaimed ones join the common pool, and containerized storage moves to weak nodes and new microgrids when growth stops.; A town's slump pauses the due but leaves the rim intact (R5) -> existing_approximation: Capacity outlives any one load and can be re-contracted or moved; a registry pooled across many grids keeps one region's collapse from stopping every unit's rent, while loose credits and the common pool carry retirees through a pause.; Nothing stands alone, so the held can never leave the town -> unresolved: Large loads can self-supply, so the due must stay below the cost of standing alone. Pooling's diversity advantage keeps most loads connected, but exit caps the rent in a way the source world never faces.
Candidate:
  label: Mantle Grid: a Load-Bearing Pension
  design_principles: Never ask the saver to be steady; key savings into what others stand on. Count only what is present. Lock by load, not by rule. Pay by measured bearing. Pledge the claim, never pull the hardware.
  core_mechanism: Any-size contributions buy slices of in-service firm grid capacity. Loads above a free base pay a convex standing due as a first lien, split monthly by each slice's metered load carried.
  how_it_works: Payers route a tenth of each fee to units; savers add any amount, any time. Units inside the reserve margin are keyed: they earn the due, can be pledged by deed, and leave service only when replaced. Surplus units are loose: stored-energy credits spendable on your own bill. New large loads energize only after contracting loose units, which then key and earn. Peak-night flexibility is paid in units. Every elder gets common units at constrained nodes; retirees can host theirs as a home battery.
  what_is_new: Retirement savings that are in-service infrastructure, paid by the loads they hold and locked by the same dependence: no pot to raid, no schedule to miss, presence paid in units.
  why_it_works: The due tracks the standing connected load, which changes slowly, not the saver's earnings or asset prices. Pooled capacity is cheaper per load because peaks cancel, so big loads want to lean on it. The lock is the grid's own reliability need, so lean months can't drain it; pledges cover them.
  why_it_fails: Big loads can self-supply, capping the due; regulators can bend its level; batteries age and cheaper tech can strand units; local units tie old age to the local economy unless pooled across grids; and the grid alone is too small to absorb every worker's savings.
  medium_term: Pilot where load is surging: data-center tariffs require contracted community units, platforms withhold a tenth, demand-response pay settles in units, and a registry publishes metered shares.
  long_term_vision: Power first, then water, heat and flood defense: every network's bearing layer is owned by people who never had a steady month. Each generation's reserve is larger, so the town can carry more; spare units move to weak nodes and new microgrids, and the old are the base it stands on.

Classify its principal claimed outcome. Decide one verdict:
- admit_new: a new outcome class, only when the primary claimed outcome differs from the nearest one, not only its name, actor, parameter or input signal
- admit_instance: an instance of an existing outcome class
- equivalent: an alias of an existing outcome class; only name, actor, parameter or input signal changed
- reject_redirect: an occupied outcome class; name the causal relation the next proposal must change
State the equivalence test against the nearest outcome class, recording a changed primary claimed outcome as primaryOperatorChanged. Restructure when the candidate reveals a better distinction: add concepts, partitions (more specific kinds under a named lens), specializations, analogies or oppositions; merge aliases; split conflated outcome classes. The ontology is a revisable hypothesis, not a neutral map. Do not prune an unusual branch because it feels unfamiliar.

Candidate under review (mech.long-round):
Operator: Value that grows with the square of the unbroken length of a maintained state, and restarts its count at any gap, is supplied to each maintained party by a rotating pool of intermittent maintainers who are released and credited only when a successor confirms takeover. Because each maintainer contributes whichever resource they have spare at the moment, continuity becomes a property of the maintained party, produced by the pool's overlap rather than by any one member's regularity.
Roles: maintained_party (The one whose accrued value depends on how long its maintained state has gone unbroken; it owns the span even though others produce it.); intermittent_maintainers (Many irregular contributors who each hold the state for a while; whatever any of them can make out is held, so together they cover more than any one could.); overlap_handover (The only regularity asked of anyone: do not release until a successor confirms takeover within a short grace; a no-show lengthens the current hold instead of breaking it.); superlinear_span_accrual (Accrued value grows with the square of each unbroken span; a gap keeps what was gained but restarts the count, so gaps, not unevenness, destroy value.); convertible_contribution (One unit that accepts whichever resource is spare now, money when busy or hours when idle, weighted by how heavy the hold is.); successor_minted_record (A witnessed record in media that do not decay, in which each credit is issued by the successor at takeover and so proves unbrokenness; entries are added freely but removed only with everyone's consent.); knowing_circle (A small mixed group whose members know one another; understanding gives the deepest hold, cannot be bought, and never accrues to those who do not take part.); continuity_backstop (Standbys, a store for lean periods, doubled holds where a gap would be costly, rest limits, and assessors who measure how heavy each hold is.)
Strangest element: Continuity belongs to the kept and is made by others: the account is a chain of handovers, each credit minted by the successor, and its value grows with the square of its unbroken length, so the least regular member can own the longest chain.. Kept as: Every credit is minted by the next holder's signature at relief; the floor and the squared surplus share are keyed to the member's unbroken chain, not to payments; a lean month cannot break it, only exit can; moving circles is itself an overlapping handover.
Magical elements: Unkept things and selves lose their particulars (R2) -> existing_approximation: Tend what really decays here without upkeep, fastest for uneven earners: pots raided in lean months, contribution records with gaps under minimum-weeks rules, scattered small pots and dormant accounts, ties that fade within months without contact, and being known.; Tenure grows with the square of the unbroken span; a break restarts the count (R4) -> institutional_substitute: Share the surplus by the sum of squared unbroken membership spans, with a flat floor. A span breaks only on exit or a year not kept, never in a lean month; sickness and caring count as kept; spans move between circles by overlapping transfer. Real echo: interest on an untouched steady trickle grows at least with the square of its span, and a withdrawal is the break.; Unbroken vigil with a five-second grace and overlapping handover (R1) -> institutional_substitute: Continuity of responsibility, not of gaze: every member always has a named holder (monthly while working, daily or nightly when frail, continuous when dying), with a grace set per service. The holder is released and credited only on relief; no-shows extend the shift at double credit; standbys cover.; Stones and seats as a ledger lapse cannot touch, because ink fades (R2, R1) -> invented_technology: Relief-signed tokens: the incoming holder's phone signs the outgoing holder's credit by tap or QR (a countersigned passbook without a smartphone), hash-chained per member so any gap beyond the grace shows, copied to every circle phone, and recounted in the open each year as in savings groups (VSLAs); one lifelong seat stapled to one pot held by a licensed custodian.; Coin is typical and keeps itself (R2) -> existing_approximation: One locked, low-cost diversified pot for life that takes any amount at any time (Kenya's Mbao micro-pension via M-Pesa, Colombia's BEPS with a 20% match, Australia's stapled super), with no early cash-out; hour credits are denominated in hours, so inflation cannot erode them.; Night is the tide of lapse and the oil store keeps lamps lit (R3) -> institutional_substitute: Here the tide is the lean month. A mutual bridge fund (like a VSLA social fund or a US pension-linked emergency account) pays lapse-critical bills: voluntary pension contributions that keep state records gapless, premiums, the phone line. It is repaid in money or hours, and circles mix trades whose lean seasons differ.; Waking attention is productive for anyone and is paid by weight (R1, R5) -> existing_approximation: Care time banks (Japan's Fureai Kippu, St. Gallen's city-backed Zeitvorsorge) and carers' pension credits (Germany, UK Carer's Credit), plus a worker-owned care co-op selling gapless shifts (hospital sitters, which cut delirium in the Hospital Elder Life Program, respite, postpartum nights): cash now, weighted credits later.; Weighers feel how heavy a charge is (R5) -> existing_approximation: Yearly standardized frailty, care-need and isolation assessments (Clinical Frailty Scale, ADL scales, long-term-care grading, Lubben network scale) set hour weights and the mix of close and coarse days, and flag unexpected decline.; Coarse sight keeps a face; only understanding keeps a self (R3) -> existing_approximation: Coarse keeping is passive monitoring and group calls (Japan's mimamori kettles that alert family when unused). Deep keeping is people who know you: PLAN-style personal networks, life-story work, a shared life file, pooled health-care advocates, and elders who speak migrants' first languages.; Cradle compact: newborns are heavy, long-cured elders light (R5) -> institutional_substitute: Our frail elders are not light, so the debt is redefined: night support in the 40-day postpartum traditions (cuarentena, zuo yuezi) makes you registered cradle-kin on the godparent/compadrazgo template; the grown child owes visits, calls and advocacy, not heavy care.; A watched clause resists being struck; additions meet no resistance (R1) -> institutional_substitute: An anti-cutback rule on accrued credits (as ERISA section 204(g) does), an asset lock on reserves, and a personal veto on cuts to one's own accrued rights; additions pass by majority; a short charter is recited at each annual meeting.; Holding the dying, the Turning, the wake and the portrait (R1, R2) -> existing_approximation: No One Dies Alone vigils and end-of-life doulas, advance care planning as the agreed letting-go, burial societies (South Africa) or iddir (Ethiopia) for the funeral, and the circle and cradle-kin for the life story.; Long-kept elders are cheap to keep, so the physics pays the Round (R4, R5) -> unresolved: Continuity of care and social ties reduce hospital use and mortality somewhat, and capitated care (PACE) can capture part of it, but dementia and frailty stay heavy; heavy care must be paid from pots, credits and insurance, not from continuity.; New kinds slide into the nearest old kind (R4) -> institutional_substitute: Regulators will file a novel mutual as an insurer, a deposit-taker or a Ponzi. Charter it as existing kinds (cooperative, licensed pension provider, time bank) on standard templates, and seed it from burial societies, VSLAs and credit unions.; Lone travellers and the unknown go typical; the circle vouches (R2, R3) -> existing_approximation: Travellers and migrants keep a paired holder at home who keeps ties, records and payments current, and they hold others by phone; circle attestation stands in for missing papers, like introducer-based ID enrolment in India's Aadhaar.; Burden burns off only in sleep; sleepless keepers lapse (R5) -> existing_approximation: Rest limits: no credit for shifts beyond a cap or without rest, respite rotas, and a two-person rule on heavy shifts that also guards against abuse.
Candidate:
  label: Long Round: relief-signed continuity
  design_principles: Make the pool regular, not the person. Accrue on unbroken membership, not payments. Take money or hours. Credit on relief. Only exit breaks a chain. Keep the self in people. Cuts need unanimity.
  core_mechanism: Each member always has a named holder; a holder is credited only when the successor signs 'I have it', adding a link to the member's chain; surplus is shared by squared unbroken span.
  how_it_works: Circles of ~12 households, mixed by trade and lean season, rota a named holder for each member: monthly check-ins while working, nightly presence when frail, a vigil at death. A holder is released only on relief; a no-show extends the shift at double credit. Dues: money into one locked lifelong pot when busy, weighted care hours when idle. A bridge fund pays lapse-critical bills. Handover tokens sit in a replicated open ledger. Kept years earn the floor; squared spans share surplus.
  what_is_new: Accrual keyed to an unbroken chain others produce, not one's payments; credit minted by the successor at relief; only exit, never a bad month, breaks it; part of the payout is being known.
  why_it_works: Hold-until-relieved plus standbys turns many unreliable shifts into one gapless chain. Spare money and spare hours peak at opposite times, so dues in either are steadier than pay. Untouched pots compound, known people are noticed early, and only exit costs, so members stay.
  why_it_fails: Money still follows pay, so low earners get small pots. Hour credits need nearby demand, trust and vetting, and may be taxed as wages. Squared spans favour founders and make leaving costly. Grant-fed schemes often fade; frail elders stay heavy here. Close circles can turn nosy or coercive.
  medium_term: Pilot in existing mutuals (burial societies, VSLAs, credit unions) in one town: holder rota, relief-signed tokens, bridge fund, hospital sitter contracts paying lean-month hours.
  long_term_vision: A federation of circles where anyone, however erratic their pay, reaches old age with an unbroken chain of people who took hold of them, a pot never raided, and a dozen who know them; state pensions credit kept years, and continuity is sold to health systems as care.

{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"task","data":{"role":"curator","inputs":{"subjectNodeId":"mech.delay-line","ontology":"outcomes"},"text":"You curate the claimed outcomes of candidate interventions: what each claims to achieve for the people it serves, not the mechanism by which it does so.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

Current outcome ontology (each class's operator states the outcome that defines it):
- [o.decoupled-income] Steady old-age income decoupled from when and how much the saver earned: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
  operator: old-age income is steady even though the contributions behind it were lumpy and irregular
  instances: Mantle Grid: a Load-Bearing Pension [mech.mantle-grid] (clear fit)
- [o.kept-and-known] Old age held by people who know you, with care that does not lapse: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
  operator: old age arrives with continuous care and with people who know the person, whatever the person's earnings history
  instances: Long Round: relief-signed continuity [mech.long-round] (clear fit)

Candidate under review (mech.delay-line):
Operator: A fixed fraction is cut from each irregular inflow the instant it occurs and irrevocably released, in equal parcels, at many staggered positions upstream of a common collector on a one-way drift that needs no tending and that no party can halt or reverse, so each parcel returns after a delay set by its position. The collector's intake is thereby an average over many past inflows, and it releases a fixed fraction of its stock each period, divided by credit measured against each period's average cut.
Roles: proportional_tap (Cuts a fixed fraction from each inflow at the moment it is recorded; a period with no inflow owes nothing, so no forecast is needed. Supplied by the conserved ledger, where every gain has a recorded counterpart.); relative_credit (Credits each paying unit by its cut divided by that period's average cut, so a period lean for everyone still earns full credit; paid and credited per balanced pair so neither member drifts from the other.); neutral_durable_parcel (Turns each cut into parcels that hold their value without tending, look like common matter and exert no net pull on the host: balanced checkerboards of tight whirls.); one_way_drift (An unstoppable, untended conveyor that brings every placed parcel back toward the collector, with delay set by placement distance and weight; arrival can be late but cannot fail. Supplied by the inward creep, with background shear feeding parcels in transit.); scatter_kernel (Spreads each period's parcels across about twenty positions so every later period receives parcels from many earlier ones; the averaging is fixed at placement, not decided later. Matched pairs carry the parcels out along straight paths.); passive_catch_and_sort (A barrier that stops net-neutral arrivals, and a cross-wall that splits each broken pair and routes each half to its own store by geometry rather than judgment.); fixed_fraction_store (A small stock kept in motion that releases a fixed fraction of itself each period from a still center, so output follows the slowly changing stock rather than the latest arrival.); neutral_floor_reserve (Whole parcels held back and annihilated on demand into a neutral form usable by either kind, guaranteeing a per-head minimum in lean periods.)
Strangest element: Keeping is surrendered to the very drift that ruins keeping: each share is placed upstream at many distances, held by no one in transit, and the unstoppable inward creep delivers it, averaged, to whoever stands downstream.. Kept as: The candidate keeps no balance and has no manager. Each cut becomes frozen strips that only the calendar can move and that can land only in the common catch, in the years their payer would be old. Placement is the only decision ever made, averaging is done by the scatter rather than by judgment, and strips of the dead land for the living.
Magical elements: A conserved ledger on which every gain appears exactly and at once, so a share can be cut from any gain and hidden gains show as crime (R2) -> existing_approximation: Cut inside the payment itself on digital rails, as Poland's VAT split payment does, plus platform, mobile-money and buyer-side withholding. A month with no gain owes nothing and nothing lapses. Cash gains remain a partial hole; a public match on rail cuts would pull some onto rails.; The stone: a carrier that keeps conserved value for decades without tending, looks like any other matter and steers nothing (R2, R3, R4) -> invented_technology: A consumption-share strip: a sovereign zero-coupon claim paying, at one maturity, a fixed share of that year's per-capita consumption. Assembled from the SeLFIES and trills proposals, with GDP warrants and Brazil's Tesouro RendA+ as working precedents, and issued as the same fungible series the public holds.; The Slope and the Draw: an untended, unstoppable one-way conveyor that returns every sown stone after a delay set by where it was placed (R1, R4) -> invented_technology: The calendar becomes the conveyor and a frozen registry replaces the hillside. Strips are registered to a common catch and cannot be sold, pledged or redeemed early by anyone, under statute plus a time-locked covenant on the securities registry. At maturity they can pay only into the catch, and any early movement is a public, provable breach.; The guarantee: a sown stone may be late but cannot fail to come down (R1) -> unresolved: Nothing in our physics brings value back. Strips are only as good as the issuer and its price statistics. Fungibility with the public issue turns a selective raid into a general default, and a later multi-state issuer could make each strip a checkerboard of sovereigns, but certainty is not reached.; Quietness: no Listener can find or single out a stone, while a one-Hand hoard is loud and a target -> institutional_substitute: No individual balances and only a pool one to two years deep, so members, managers and legislatures find nothing to withdraw, raid or steer. The emergency withdrawals that emptied accounts in Chile and Peru would have no object.; Timing set by sowing distance and stone weight, across twenty distances per round (R1) -> existing_approximation: Maturity choice, refined: each cut is split across every year of the payer's likely old age, weighted by survival odds, so every old-age year gets a slice of every working year and a lumpy career lands as a flat stream.; The mirror-wall that splits each pair and sends each half to its own Hand's basin (R5) -> institutional_substitute: A standing payout instruction that splits each couple's share 50/50 into each partner's own account, as Swiss pension splitting does. No clerk decides.; The self-centering round basin, where a fuller basin sends more to its still eye (R5, R1) -> existing_approximation: A fixed-fraction spending rule in the manner of Norway's 3% rule, applied monthly: the pool pays 1/24 of itself by points and is held in short indexed bills.; Froth: balanced stock annihilated on demand into neutral feed for both Hands (R2) -> existing_approximation: A slice of each matured strip rolls into a reserve released only when the monthly payment would fall below a per-head floor, paid per head with singles included. The Dutch solidarity reserve and Chile's pension reserve fund are close precedents.; Rounds that hold the same amount of living in every band, because shear per round is constant (R1, R4) -> institutional_substitute: Everything is denominated in standard-of-living units: points against the month's average cut (the logic of German earnings points), strips paying shares of per-capita consumption, and a floor set as a share of it. No nominal promise appears anywhere.; Twins as the paying unit, re-evened by feeding the weaker up and never cutting down; a half keeps the pair's knots (R2, R3) -> institutional_substitute: A household cut with points split equally. At claiming, the first payments top up the lower-credited partner, and a survivor keeps the pair's full points.; Missed stones creep on to an inward town that credits them (R1) -> existing_approximation: Totalization and portability rules in the style of EU Regulation 883/2004, plus a statutory successor catch, so no strip matures with nobody downstream.
Candidate:
  label: Delay-Line Share Pension
  design_principles: Shares, never amounts. Cut at the moment of gain. Keep no balance: release each cut, frozen, across many future years. Let the calendar deliver. Credit relative to peers. Floor from reserve.
  core_mechanism: A fixed share of each payment is cut at the rail and turned into frozen consumption-share strips maturing over the payer's old age into a common pool that pays a fixed fraction by points.
  how_it_works: Payment rails split ~10% off every gain; a month with no gain owes nothing. Points = your cut / that month's average cut, split 50/50 in couples. Each cut buys sovereign strips paying shares of per-capita consumption, one per year of the payer's likely old age (survival-weighted). Strips sit frozen: no sale, loan or early cash-in. Matured strips land in one pool paying 1/24 of itself monthly by points; strips of the dead feed the living. A reserve slice pays a per-head floor in lean years.
  what_is_new: A pension with no balance and no manager: savings exist only as frozen strips in transit, so nothing can be raided, withdrawn or steered, and smoothing comes from scatter geometry, not judgment.
  why_it_works: Proportional cuts need no forecast; relative points protect common lean months; slicing every cut across all old-age years flattens a lumpy career into a flat stream; consumption shares keep pace without recalculation; frozen strips shut the leakage that drained Chile's and Peru's accounts.
  why_it_fails: No law of nature guarantees arrival: strips are only as good as the issuing state and its statistics office (Argentina bent its CPI). Cash gains dodge the rail; a cut with no emergency access may push workers into cash; real yields are low; a legislature can still unfreeze the registry.
  medium_term: Pilot on one gig platform or mobile-money rail using existing inflation-linked zero-coupon debt in a locked trust; publish every cut, catch and payout; seek a first consumption-share strip issue.
  long_term_vision: Every payment rail carries a share-cut; states issue consumption-share strips for every future year; schemes credit each other's strips; old age is paid as a steady share of the living standard, built from whatever people earned, whenever they happened to earn it.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

The current map of candidate mechanisms (families, their operators and instances):
- [fam.external-regularity] Regularity supplied by others: 0 direct, 2 in subtree
  operator: The steadiness a saver cannot supply is supplied by a structure of other people: the benefit is keyed to something others depend on or maintain, never to the saver's own regular payments.
  partition fam.external-regularity.by-what-others-supply, lens: what the others supply: a standing dependence that pays rent to the saver's part (bearing), or a maintained continuity that accrues to the saver (relay)
    - [fam.bearing-rent] Savings as rented bearing capacity: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: Contributions of any size and timing become parts that carry a standing load others depend on; the dependents pay the owners in proportion to the measured load each part carries, and the same dependence locks the parts in service, so claims can change hands but the capital cannot be withdrawn.
      instances: Mantle Grid: a Load-Bearing Pension [mech.mantle-grid]
    - [fam.relay-continuity] Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: A value that grows superlinearly with the unbroken span of a maintained state, and restarts its count at a gap, is produced for each member by a rotating pool of intermittent maintainers who are released and credited only when a successor confirms takeover; each pays in whatever resource is spare, so continuity is a property of the member rather than of anyone's regularity.
      instances: Long Round: relief-signed continuity [mech.long-round]
- [fam.no-raidable-pot] No pot a lean month can raid: 0 direct, 3 in subtree
  operator: The saved value is kept in a form that the saver cannot draw down in a lean month, so contributions made at any time survive to old age.
  partition fam.no-raidable-pot.by-where-value-lives, lens: where the saved value lives so that a lean month cannot take it: in parts others depend on, in the length of a chain others keep, or in parcels already in transit
    - [fam.bearing-rent] Savings as rented bearing capacity: 1 direct, 1 in subtree (shown above)
    - [fam.relay-continuity] Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept: 1 direct, 1 in subtree (shown above)
    - [fam.temporal-scatter] Averaging by irrevocable temporal scatter: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: A fixed fraction of each irregular inflow is cut when it occurs and released irrevocably in parcels staggered over many future periods into a common collector, so each later period's intake averages many earlier inflows; the collector pays out a fixed fraction of its stock, shared by credit relative to each period's average.
      instances: Delay-Line Share Pension [mech.delay-line] (clear fit)

Thin or unoccupied branches: fam.bearing-rent, fam.relay-continuity, fam.temporal-scatter
Family and claimed-outcome combinations no candidate has yet: fam.bearing-rent with o.kept-and-known; fam.relay-continuity with o.decoupled-income; fam.temporal-scatter with o.kept-and-known

A random word for inspiration: hoarfrost. Do not force a literal connection; it may become any metaphor, structure, process or principle.

Propose one candidate aimed at a thin or unoccupied branch, or at a mechanism the map lacks. Be genuinely novel: do not rephrase an existing family. First name the structures you are avoiding and why. Then state:
- operator: the operative causal relation in one or two sentences
- roles: the two to eight parts it needs
- strangest: its strangest element, and how the candidate keeps it
- candidate: label (at most 40 characters), design_principles (at most 200 characters), core_mechanism (at most 200 characters), how_it_works (at most 500 characters), what_is_new (at most 200 characters), why_it_works (at most 300 characters), why_it_fails (at most 300 characters), medium_term (at most 200 characters), long_term_vision (at most 300 characters)

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

Current mechanism ontology:
- [fam.external-regularity] Regularity supplied by others: 0 direct, 2 in subtree
  operator: The steadiness a saver cannot supply is supplied by a structure of other people: the benefit is keyed to something others depend on or maintain, never to the saver's own regular payments.
  partition fam.external-regularity.by-what-others-supply, lens: what the others supply: a standing dependence that pays rent to the saver's part (bearing), or a maintained continuity that accrues to the saver (relay)
    - [fam.bearing-rent] Savings as rented bearing capacity: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: Contributions of any size and timing become parts that carry a standing load others depend on; the dependents pay the owners in proportion to the measured load each part carries, and the same dependence locks the parts in service, so claims can change hands but the capital cannot be withdrawn.
      instances: Mantle Grid: a Load-Bearing Pension [mech.mantle-grid]
    - [fam.relay-continuity] Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: A value that grows superlinearly with the unbroken span of a maintained state, and restarts its count at a gap, is produced for each member by a rotating pool of intermittent maintainers who are released and credited only when a successor confirms takeover; each pays in whatever resource is spare, so continuity is a property of the member rather than of anyone's regularity.
      instances: Long Round: relief-signed continuity [mech.long-round]
- [fam.no-raidable-pot] No pot a lean month can raid: 0 direct, 3 in subtree
  operator: The saved value is kept in a form that the saver cannot draw down in a lean month, so contributions made at any time survive to old age.
  partition fam.no-raidable-pot.by-where-value-lives, lens: where the saved value lives so that a lean month cannot take it: in parts others depend on, in the length of a chain others keep, or in parcels already in transit
    - [fam.bearing-rent] Savings as rented bearing capacity: 1 direct, 1 in subtree (shown above)
    - [fam.relay-continuity] Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept: 1 direct, 1 in subtree (shown above)
    - [fam.temporal-scatter] Averaging by irrevocable temporal scatter: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: A fixed fraction of each irregular inflow is cut when it occurs and released irrevocably in parcels staggered over many future periods into a common collector, so each later period's intake averages many earlier inflows; the collector pays out a fixed fraction of its stock, shared by credit relative to each period's average.
      instances: Delay-Line Share Pension [mech.delay-line] (clear fit)

Candidate under review (mech.frost-line, proposed directly by an explorer):
Operator: Commitment is made by hindsight, not pledge: each month a fixed fraction of the balance the saver's everyday account has not dipped below over the trailing year (net of earlier frost) is frozen irreversibly into retirement claims. A lean spell pauses the freeze by lowering that low-water mark, so the lock only ever takes money that a full year of the saver's own need has already left untouched.
Roles: saver (Earns irregularly; receives all income into, and spends from, one everyday account; never sets a contribution amount, rate or schedule.); everyday-account (An ordinary spendable balance where every inflow lands and all spending leaves; spending draws the newest money first, so the oldest money is the stillest.); low-water-meter (Tracks the frost line: the lowest balance over the trailing twelve months, net of frost already taken, which equals the money that has sat untouched for a year.); freezer (Each month moves about a sixth of the money under the frost line into the retirement store, irreversibly; never touches money above the line and accepts no direct deposits.); income-unit-issuer (Turns each frozen slice at once into inflation-indexed deferred income units payable from retirement age, so the pension is kept and shown as known monthly income.); frost-match (A public funder that tops up each frozen slice, progressively and with a cap, paying only for stillness, so routing surplus through the account beats hiding it elsewhere.)
Strangest element: Nobody ever chooses a contribution: the saver's own lowest moment of the past year sets it, so hardship, not intention, decides how much becomes pension.. Kept as: There is no schedule, target, opt-in amount or fast lane; even a deliberate saver's money must sit a year like any other. The only way to save is stillness, the only way to stop is need, and no forecast ever replaces the frost line.
Candidate:
  label: Low-Water Frost Pension
  design_principles: Commit by hindsight, not forecast or pledge. Lock only money a full year of the saver's own lean moments left untouched. Let each life's worst dip size its buffer. Show the pension as income.
  core_mechanism: Each month a fixed fraction of the balance the everyday account has not dipped below over the trailing year freezes irreversibly into inflation-indexed deferred income units.
  how_it_works: Every inflow lands in one ordinary spending account; nothing is ever pledged. A meter marks the frost line: the part of today's balance untouched for a full year (the trailing-year low, net of earlier frost). Each month a sixth of the money under the line freezes irreversibly into inflation-indexed deferred income units paid from retirement, and a capped public match tops up each slice. A lean spell drags the line down and freezing pauses; unfrozen money stays spendable.
  what_is_new: A new axis, when the lock falls: after the fact, on money a year of the saver's own need left idle, so no forecast is needed and each buffer sizes itself to that life's worst dip.
  why_it_works: Unknown income blocks saving because people must guess what they can spare. Here nobody guesses: money that outlasted a year of their own lean moments has proved spare, and any new lean spell lowers the line itself. So all surplus can pass through the account, not a hidden hoard.
  why_it_fails: Lives with no idle money never frost, so chronic scarcity still needs a floor. A year worse than the last meets a buffer sized to a milder past, and money kept for a rare big cost may freeze first. The wary can dodge it by moving money out; cash-only lives show no balance.
  medium_term: Pilot as a rule on mobile-money and platform payout wallets for seasonal and gig workers; show each person's frost line; tune the window and freeze rate against hardship data.
  long_term_vision: Every transaction account carries a slow frost line, and old age is built from whatever each life proves it can spare. Pensions stop being promises people must keep through months they cannot foresee and become the residue their lives leave.

Decide one verdict:
- admit_new: a new family, only when the primary causal operator differs from the nearest one, not only its name, actor, parameter or input signal
- admit_instance: an instance of an existing family
- equivalent: an alias of an existing family; only name, actor, parameter or input signal changed
- reject_redirect: an occupied family; name the causal relation the next proposal must change
State the equivalence test against the nearest family. Restructure when the candidate reveals a better distinction: add concepts, partitions (more specific kinds under a named lens), specializations, analogies or oppositions; merge aliases; split conflated families. The ontology is a revisable hypothesis, not a neutral map. Do not prune an unusual branch because it feels unfamiliar. A retry that picks one of your named alternatives shows responsiveness, not discovery.

{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"task","data":{"role":"curator","inputs":{"subjectNodeId":"mech.frost-line","ontology":"outcomes"},"text":"You curate the claimed outcomes of candidate interventions: what each claims to achieve for the people it serves, not the mechanism by which it does so.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

Current outcome ontology (each class's operator states the outcome that defines it):
- [o.decoupled-income] Steady old-age income decoupled from when and how much the saver earned: 2 direct, 2 in subtree
  operator: old-age income is steady even though the contributions behind it were lumpy and irregular
  instances: Mantle Grid: a Load-Bearing Pension [mech.mantle-grid] (clear fit); Delay-Line Share Pension [mech.delay-line] (clear fit)
- [o.kept-and-known] Old age held by people who know you, with care that does not lapse: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
  operator: old age arrives with continuous care and with people who know the person, whatever the person's earnings history
  instances: Long Round: relief-signed continuity [mech.long-round] (clear fit)

Candidate under review (mech.frost-line):
Operator: Commitment is made by hindsight, not pledge: each month a fixed fraction of the balance the saver's everyday account has not dipped below over the trailing year (net of earlier frost) is frozen irreversibly into retirement claims. A lean spell pauses the freeze by lowering that low-water mark, so the lock only ever takes money that a full year of the saver's own need has already left untouched.
Roles: saver (Earns irregularly; receives all income into, and spends from, one everyday account; never sets a contribution amount, rate or schedule.); everyday-account (An ordinary spendable balance where every inflow lands and all spending leaves; spending draws the newest money first, so the oldest money is the stillest.); low-water-meter (Tracks the frost line: the lowest balance over the trailing twelve months, net of frost already taken, which equals the money that has sat untouched for a year.); freezer (Each month moves about a sixth of the money under the frost line into the retirement store, irreversibly; never touches money above the line and accepts no direct deposits.); income-unit-issuer (Turns each frozen slice at once into inflation-indexed deferred income units payable from retirement age, so the pension is kept and shown as known monthly income.); frost-match (A public funder that tops up each frozen slice, progressively and with a cap, paying only for stillness, so routing surplus through the account beats hiding it elsewhere.)
Strangest element: Nobody ever chooses a contribution: the saver's own lowest moment of the past year sets it, so hardship, not intention, decides how much becomes pension.. Kept as: There is no schedule, target, opt-in amount or fast lane; even a deliberate saver's money must sit a year like any other. The only way to save is stillness, the only way to stop is need, and no forecast ever replaces the frost line.
Candidate:
  label: Low-Water Frost Pension
  design_principles: Commit by hindsight, not forecast or pledge. Lock only money a full year of the saver's own lean moments left untouched. Let each life's worst dip size its buffer. Show the pension as income.
  core_mechanism: Each month a fixed fraction of the balance the everyday account has not dipped below over the trailing year freezes irreversibly into inflation-indexed deferred income units.
  how_it_works: Every inflow lands in one ordinary spending account; nothing is ever pledged. A meter marks the frost line: the part of today's balance untouched for a full year (the trailing-year low, net of earlier frost). Each month a sixth of the money under the line freezes irreversibly into inflation-indexed deferred income units paid from retirement, and a capped public match tops up each slice. A lean spell drags the line down and freezing pauses; unfrozen money stays spendable.
  what_is_new: A new axis, when the lock falls: after the fact, on money a year of the saver's own need left idle, so no forecast is needed and each buffer sizes itself to that life's worst dip.
  why_it_works: Unknown income blocks saving because people must guess what they can spare. Here nobody guesses: money that outlasted a year of their own lean moments has proved spare, and any new lean spell lowers the line itself. So all surplus can pass through the account, not a hidden hoard.
  why_it_fails: Lives with no idle money never frost, so chronic scarcity still needs a floor. A year worse than the last meets a buffer sized to a milder past, and money kept for a rare big cost may freeze first. The wary can dodge it by moving money out; cash-only lives show no balance.
  medium_term: Pilot as a rule on mobile-money and platform payout wallets for seasonal and gig workers; show each person's frost line; tune the window and freeze rate against hardship data.
  long_term_vision: Every transaction account carries a slow frost line, and old age is built from whatever each life proves it can spare. Pensions stop being promises people must keep through months they cannot foresee and become the residue their lives leave.

Classify its principal claimed outcome. Decide one verdict:
- admit_new: a new outcome class, only when the primary claimed outcome differs from the nearest one, not only its name, actor, parameter or input signal
- admit_instance: an instance of an existing outcome class
- equivalent: an alias of an existing outcome class; only name, actor, parameter or input signal changed
- reject_redirect: an occupied outcome class; name the causal relation the next proposal must change
State the equivalence test against the nearest outcome class, recording a changed primary claimed outcome as primaryOperatorChanged. Restructure when the candidate reveals a better distinction: add concepts, partitions (more specific kinds under a named lens), specializations, analogies or oppositions; merge aliases; split conflated outcome classes. The ontology is a revisable hypothesis, not a neutral map. Do not prune an unusual branch because it feels unfamiliar.

End your answer with the decision as one JSON object: verdict; conceptId; nearestConceptId; equivalence {nameChanged, actorChanged, parameterChanged, inputSignalChanged, primaryOperatorChanged, explanation} or null; fit (clear, partial, borderline or null); newConcepts (for admit_new or restructuring, each {id, label, operator, differentia, boundary, roles [{id, description}]}, with labels up to 200 characters, operators up to 1,200, each differentia up to 800 and boundaries up to 2,000); other operations in words; redirect {addressedTo, relationToChange, alternatives, worldAsk} or null; rationale (up to 4,000 characters).","textHash":"92d744b606faf2554cbe626d07f5b0009b43f9e744649aad757996f010bd2729","material":{"subjectNodeId":"mech.frost-line","ontology":"outcomes","headNodeId":"orev.3"},"condition":null,"targetBlind":false,"purposeBlind":false,"targetLeaks":[],"preparedAtGraphHash":"503954fc381c1b1f8a9c58e7715f6f43b29af27784d680ed40dcbef795f1332a"},"searchClock":{"rootId":"alien.understanding.21a77a717ac710789574e26e","unit":"search_step","at":30,"index":0}}

{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"task","data":{"role":"transfer","inputs":{"mechanismNodeId":"mech.frost-line"},"text":"Transfer one compiled mechanism into the target domain, for ideation.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

TARGET MODEL:
Model irregular-income-retirement (time unit month). Cite records as kind:id.

Processes:
- process:household.age_years [years]: age of the main earner
- process:household.buffer_nok [NOK]: liquid savings available for lean months
- process:household.income_cv [coefficient of variation]: month-to-month variability of earnings
- process:household.income_nok_month [NOK/month]: earnings received in the month
- process:household.pension_claims_nok [NOK]: accumulated claims payable in retirement
- process:household.spending_nok_month [NOK/month]: living costs paid in the month

Referents:
- referent:referent.circle: The household's close circle: kin, friends and neighbours who can check in, hold, cover or pool
- referent:referent.clients: The shifting set of clients and platforms that pay the household
- referent:referent.household: One gig-working household whose monthly earnings are unpredictable in size and timing
- referent:referent.pension_provider: An organization that holds retirement claims and pays them out
- referent:referent.platforms: The platforms, marketplaces and payment rails through which the household is paid
- referent:referent.state: The public authority that sets pension, tax and benefit rules

Events:
- event:event.earning.arrival: An earning arrives, of unpredictable size and timing.
- event:event.lean.month: A month in which earnings fall below spending.
- event:event.retirement: The household stops earning and draws on its claims, over an illustrative twenty years.
- event:event.working.life: The household's working life, with earnings arriving irregularly, over an illustrative forty years.
- event:event.world: The accepted present-day economy the household lives in.

Operator: Commitment is made by hindsight, not pledge: each month a fixed fraction of the balance the saver's everyday account has not dipped below over the trailing year (net of earlier frost) is frozen irreversibly into retirement claims. Strangest element: Nobody ever chooses a contribution: the saver's own lowest moment of the past year sets it, so hardship, not intention, decides how much becomes pension.. Kept as: There is no schedule, target, opt-in amount or fast lane; even a deliberate saver's money must sit a year like any other. The only way to save is stillness, the only way to stop is need, and no forecast ever replaces the frost line.

  label: Low-Water Frost Pension
  design_principles: Commit by hindsight, not forecast or pledge. Lock only money a full year of the saver's own lean moments left untouched. Let each life's worst dip size its buffer. Show the pension as income.
  core_mechanism: Each month a fixed fraction of the balance the everyday account has not dipped below over the trailing year freezes irreversibly into inflation-indexed deferred income units.
  how_it_works: Every inflow lands in one ordinary spending account; nothing is ever pledged. A meter marks the frost line: the part of today's balance untouched for a full year (the trailing-year low, net of earlier frost). Each month a sixth of the money under the line freezes irreversibly into inflation-indexed deferred income units paid from retirement, and a capped public match tops up each slice. A lean spell drags the line down and freezing pauses; unfrozen money stays spendable.
  what_is_new: A new axis, when the lock falls: after the fact, on money a year of the saver's own need left idle, so no forecast is needed and each buffer sizes itself to that life's worst dip.
  why_it_works: Unknown income blocks saving because people must guess what they can spare. Here nobody guesses: money that outlasted a year of their own lean moments has proved spare, and any new lean spell lowers the line itself. So all surplus can pass through the account, not a hidden hoard.

Family: fam.hindsight-commitment: Commitment by hindsight on proven-idle value. Operator: Nothing is committed when it arrives. A meter tracks the part of an ordinary spendable balance that the owner's own use has left untouched over a trailing window; a fixed fraction of that proven-idle part is locked irrevocably at each step, and any draw-down lowers the mark and pauses the lock, so what becomes locked is chosen after the fact by the owner's revealed need rather than by a pledge, a forecast or a share of inflows.

1. Map every role: bind it to a model record (kind:id), describe the new component the domain would need, or leave it unfilled with the reason.
2. Label each magical element's proxy as portable (achievable with present means), inverse (the domain needs the opposite effect) or magical (no present means), and date the judgment.
3. List where the analogy breaks: at least one disanalogy.
4. Write the candidate in the domain's own terms: label (at most 40 characters), design_principles (at most 200 characters), core_mechanism (at most 200 characters), how_it_works (at most 500 characters), what_is_new (at most 200 characters), why_it_works (at most 300 characters), why_it_fails (at most 300 characters), medium_term (at most 200 characters), long_term_vision (at most 300 characters).

{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"task","data":{"role":"transfer","inputs":{"mechanismNodeId":"mech.delay-line"},"text":"Transfer one compiled mechanism into the target domain, for ideation.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

TARGET MODEL:
Model irregular-income-retirement (time unit month). Cite records as kind:id.

Processes:
- process:household.age_years [years]: age of the main earner
- process:household.buffer_nok [NOK]: liquid savings available for lean months
- process:household.income_cv [coefficient of variation]: month-to-month variability of earnings
- process:household.income_nok_month [NOK/month]: earnings received in the month
- process:household.pension_claims_nok [NOK]: accumulated claims payable in retirement
- process:household.spending_nok_month [NOK/month]: living costs paid in the month

Referents:
- referent:referent.circle: The household's close circle: kin, friends and neighbours who can check in, hold, cover or pool
- referent:referent.clients: The shifting set of clients and platforms that pay the household
- referent:referent.household: One gig-working household whose monthly earnings are unpredictable in size and timing
- referent:referent.pension_provider: An organization that holds retirement claims and pays them out
- referent:referent.platforms: The platforms, marketplaces and payment rails through which the household is paid
- referent:referent.state: The public authority that sets pension, tax and benefit rules

Events:
- event:event.earning.arrival: An earning arrives, of unpredictable size and timing.
- event:event.lean.month: A month in which earnings fall below spending.
- event:event.retirement: The household stops earning and draws on its claims, over an illustrative twenty years.
- event:event.working.life: The household's working life, with earnings arriving irregularly, over an illustrative forty years.
- event:event.world: The accepted present-day economy the household lives in.

MECHANISM (mech.delay-line):
Operator: A fixed fraction is cut from each irregular inflow the instant it occurs and irrevocably released, in equal parcels, at many staggered positions upstream of a common collector on a one-way drift that needs no tending and that no party can halt or reverse, so each parcel returns after a delay set by its position. The collector's intake is thereby an average over many past inflows, and it releases a fixed fraction of its stock each period, divided by credit measured against each period's average cut.
Roles: proportional_tap (Cuts a fixed fraction from each inflow at the moment it is recorded; a period with no inflow owes nothing, so no forecast is needed. Supplied by the conserved ledger, where every gain has a recorded counterpart.); relative_credit (Credits each paying unit by its cut divided by that period's average cut, so a period lean for everyone still earns full credit; paid and credited per balanced pair so neither member drifts from the other.); neutral_durable_parcel (Turns each cut into parcels that hold their value without tending, look like common matter and exert no net pull on the host: balanced checkerboards of tight whirls.); one_way_drift (An unstoppable, untended conveyor that brings every placed parcel back toward the collector, with delay set by placement distance and weight; arrival can be late but cannot fail. Supplied by the inward creep, with background shear feeding parcels in transit.); scatter_kernel (Spreads each period's parcels across about twenty positions so every later period receives parcels from many earlier ones; the averaging is fixed at placement, not decided later. Matched pairs carry the parcels out along straight paths.); passive_catch_and_sort (A barrier that stops net-neutral arrivals, and a cross-wall that splits each broken pair and routes each half to its own store by geometry rather than judgment.); fixed_fraction_store (A small stock kept in motion that releases a fixed fraction of itself each period from a still center, so output follows the slowly changing stock rather than the latest arrival.); neutral_floor_reserve (Whole parcels held back and annihilated on demand into a neutral form usable by either kind, guaranteeing a per-head minimum in lean periods.)
Strangest element: Keeping is surrendered to the very drift that ruins keeping: each share is placed upstream at many distances, held by no one in transit, and the unstoppable inward creep delivers it, averaged, to whoever stands downstream.. Kept as: The candidate keeps no balance and has no manager. Each cut becomes frozen strips that only the calendar can move and that can land only in the common catch, in the years their payer would be old. Placement is the only decision ever made, averaging is done by the scatter rather than by judgment, and strips of the dead land for the living.
Magical elements: A conserved ledger on which every gain appears exactly and at once, so a share can be cut from any gain and hidden gains show as crime (R2) -> existing_approximation: Cut inside the payment itself on digital rails, as Poland's VAT split payment does, plus platform, mobile-money and buyer-side withholding. A month with no gain owes nothing and nothing lapses. Cash gains remain a partial hole; a public match on rail cuts would pull some onto rails.; The stone: a carrier that keeps conserved value for decades without tending, looks like any other matter and steers nothing (R2, R3, R4) -> invented_technology: A consumption-share strip: a sovereign zero-coupon claim paying, at one maturity, a fixed share of that year's per-capita consumption. Assembled from the SeLFIES and trills proposals, with GDP warrants and Brazil's Tesouro RendA+ as working precedents, and issued as the same fungible series the public holds.; The Slope and the Draw: an untended, unstoppable one-way conveyor that returns every sown stone after a delay set by where it was placed (R1, R4) -> invented_technology: The calendar becomes the conveyor and a frozen registry replaces the hillside. Strips are registered to a common catch and cannot be sold, pledged or redeemed early by anyone, under statute plus a time-locked covenant on the securities registry. At maturity they can pay only into the catch, and any early movement is a public, provable breach.; The guarantee: a sown stone may be late but cannot fail to come down (R1) -> unresolved: Nothing in our physics brings value back. Strips are only as good as the issuer and its price statistics. Fungibility with the public issue turns a selective raid into a general default, and a later multi-state issuer could make each strip a checkerboard of sovereigns, but certainty is not reached.; Quietness: no Listener can find or single out a stone, while a one-Hand hoard is loud and a target -> institutional_substitute: No individual balances and only a pool one to two years deep, so members, managers and legislatures find nothing to withdraw, raid or steer. The emergency withdrawals that emptied accounts in Chile and Peru would have no object.; Timing set by sowing distance and stone weight, across twenty distances per round (R1) -> existing_approximation: Maturity choice, refined: each cut is split across every year of the payer's likely old age, weighted by survival odds, so every old-age year gets a slice of every working year and a lumpy career lands as a flat stream.; The mirror-wall that splits each pair and sends each half to its own Hand's basin (R5) -> institutional_substitute: A standing payout instruction that splits each couple's share 50/50 into each partner's own account, as Swiss pension splitting does. No clerk decides.; The self-centering round basin, where a fuller basin sends more to its still eye (R5, R1) -> existing_approximation: A fixed-fraction spending rule in the manner of Norway's 3% rule, applied monthly: the pool pays 1/24 of itself by points and is held in short indexed bills.; Froth: balanced stock annihilated on demand into neutral feed for both Hands (R2) -> existing_approximation: A slice of each matured strip rolls into a reserve released only when the monthly payment would fall below a per-head floor, paid per head with singles included. The Dutch solidarity reserve and Chile's pension reserve fund are close precedents.; Rounds that hold the same amount of living in every band, because shear per round is constant (R1, R4) -> institutional_substitute: Everything is denominated in standard-of-living units: points against the month's average cut (the logic of German earnings points), strips paying shares of per-capita consumption, and a floor set as a share of it. No nominal promise appears anywhere.; Twins as the paying unit, re-evened by feeding the weaker up and never cutting down; a half keeps the pair's knots (R2, R3) -> institutional_substitute: A household cut with points split equally. At claiming, the first payments top up the lower-credited partner, and a survivor keeps the pair's full points.; Missed stones creep on to an inward town that credits them (R1) -> existing_approximation: Totalization and portability rules in the style of EU Regulation 883/2004, plus a statutory successor catch, so no strip matures with nobody downstream.
Candidate:
  label: Delay-Line Share Pension
  design_principles: Shares, never amounts. Cut at the moment of gain. Keep no balance: release each cut, frozen, across many future years. Let the calendar deliver. Credit relative to peers. Floor from reserve.
  core_mechanism: A fixed share of each payment is cut at the rail and turned into frozen consumption-share strips maturing over the payer's old age into a common pool that pays a fixed fraction by points.
  how_it_works: Payment rails split ~10% off every gain; a month with no gain owes nothing. Points = your cut / that month's average cut, split 50/50 in couples. Each cut buys sovereign strips paying shares of per-capita consumption, one per year of the payer's likely old age (survival-weighted). Strips sit frozen: no sale, loan or early cash-in. Matured strips land in one pool paying 1/24 of itself monthly by points; strips of the dead feed the living. A reserve slice pays a per-head floor in lean years.
  what_is_new: A pension with no balance and no manager: savings exist only as frozen strips in transit, so nothing can be raided, withdrawn or steered, and smoothing comes from scatter geometry, not judgment.
  why_it_works: Proportional cuts need no forecast; relative points protect common lean months; slicing every cut across all old-age years flattens a lumpy career into a flat stream; consumption shares keep pace without recalculation; frozen strips shut the leakage that drained Chile's and Peru's accounts.
  why_it_fails: No law of nature guarantees arrival: strips are only as good as the issuing state and its statistics office (Argentina bent its CPI). Cash gains dodge the rail; a cut with no emergency access may push workers into cash; real yields are low; a legislature can still unfreeze the registry.
  medium_term: Pilot on one gig platform or mobile-money rail using existing inflation-linked zero-coupon debt in a locked trust; publish every cut, catch and payout; seek a first consumption-share strip issue.
  long_term_vision: Every payment rail carries a share-cut; states issue consumption-share strips for every future year; schemes credit each other's strips; old age is paid as a steady share of the living standard, built from whatever people earned, whenever they happened to earn it.

{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"world","data":{"title":"The Kept World: Where Every Change Is Someone's Gift","text":"The Kept World: Where Every Change Is Someone's Gift

1. The core principle

In the Kept World there is only one cause: a gift. A change happens only when a person gives some of their store, which is the world's single currency of change. The receiver then takes exactly the change that store paid for. Things have no natures or tendencies, only conditions. So the stillness relation is not an extra law. It is simply what happens when there is no other cause: if no one is giving to a thing, nothing can make it different, and it stays exactly as it is.

Potlatch shapes everything else. Giving is the only way to act on the world. Being given to binds you. Your power is measured by what you have given away and not yet had back.

People reason about this as calmly as we reason about a locked drawer: whatever you left is still there, exactly as you left it. Every "why did this change?" has the answer "someone paid for it", and there is always a name to find. Children learn this with their first toy. A dropped cup hangs in the air, and a toy that moved always had a mover.

2. The rules

R1 — Keeping. Whatever no one is giving to stays exactly as it is in every way: place, shape, heat, colour, freshness, tension, memory, mood and debt.
- Nothing falls, flows, cools, spreads, rots, rusts, ages, heals, fades or is forgotten on its own.
- A kettle heated a century ago is still exactly as hot. A drawn bow stays drawn forever and never looses its arrow. Spoken words hang in the air where they were said.
- A gift of motion is a gift of a journey. The giver decides where the thing goes; it goes there and stops. Nothing coasts past what was paid for, and there is no up or down.
- For anything untouched, its state now is its state at its last gift.

R2 — The Gift.
- Only people give. Everything else (stone, water, air, grain, beasts) is a thing. A thing can receive a change and keep it, but it never gives, so it can never pass a change on.
- A thrown stone that hits a window stops against it. The window breaks only if someone pays to break it. No lever, spring, wheel, fire or current does any work. Every effect is paid for directly, by the giver's own touch.
- A change costs its giver store equal to its size. One measure carries a grown person's weight a hundred paces, brings a kettle from cold to boiling-hot, or leaves about ten words hanging in the air.
- A waking hour of looking, listening and thinking costs about one measure. Seeing needs no light, because it is something the seer does.
- Store is never used up. It sits in the change it bought, and every change carries its maker's name, readable by anyone who looks closely.
- Only the maker can undo a change, and only if nobody has changed that thing since. Undoing gives the maker back the full store, so a round trip or a corrected mistake costs them nothing.
- No one can take store from a person. It leaves a person only when they give it.
- The only change one person can make to another is to give them store. Your body, place and mind change only when you spend on them, so no one can move, wound or kill anyone else.

R3 — Debt.
- When a person receives store from another person, with at least one third person watching as witness, the receiver owes the giver exactly that much.
- A gift cannot be refused. A gift given with no witness moves the store but binds no one.
- Debts never fade (R1). Only repayment, which needs no witness, or the creditor's forgiveness ends a debt.
- While you owe anyone, every measure you give to any person, witnessed or not, goes first to your creditors, oldest debt first, until you are clear. It reaches them wherever they are; debt is the one thing that travels without touch. Only what is left over reaches the person you meant.
- Spending on things or on yourself is never redirected this way.
- Between two people there is only one balance. If you return more than you owe, your debt is cleared and the other person now owes you the extra.

R4 — Standing.
- Your standing is what others currently owe you, plus everything you have broken (R5).
- Standing sets your pace, the fastest you can spend store. Everyone has 20 measures an hour, plus 1 more an hour for each measure of standing.
- Store is how much you can do; standing is how fast. Receiving makes you rich but bound. Giving makes you fast but poor. Being repaid slows you down.

R5 — Breaking.
- In front of witnesses, you may break a change you made, which means giving it up forever.
- No one can ever undo it, though others may build over it. The store in it leaves the world for good, and your standing rises by that amount permanently, owed by no one.
- Nothing adds store to the world, and breaking is the only thing that removes it. So the world's total store is fixed, except that every breaking makes it smaller.

3. How people live

Givings. Everything that matters happens at a Giving, because witnesses make gifts binding.
- The host gives to the gathered guests, and each guest watches the others receive. By the end, a hall full of people owes the host, and the host's pace has multiplied.
- The guests must hold Givings of their own. They try to give back more than they got, so that the balance tips their way.
- Rank is simply standing, and the great really are faster. A head of house owed 50,000 measures spends about 2,500 times faster than someone owed nothing, who gets around at a slow stroll.
- Monuments are broken works that no one can ever remove. Each one is a permanent record of its breaker's pace.

Fighting with gifts. No one can harm a body, so rivalry runs through store.
- You bring down a great giver by repaying them in full and then some. This drains their pace and leaves them owing you.
- Or you bury a rival in witnessed gifts, so that whatever they give anyone reaches you first.
- Custom pushes back. A Giving must include a witness the receiver invited, gifts nobody asked for are limited, and there are "quiet gifts", given with no witness, which help someone without owning them.

Family and life.
- Parents make a child by giving store into a new person. Births are always witnessed, so every child starts life owing its parents. Under the oldest-first rule, it can give to no one else until that first debt is paid. That moment, the Squaring, is coming of age.
- Children grow exactly as fast as they are given store to grow with. Adults do not age.
- No one gets hungry, because hunger would be a change nobody makes. Food is eaten for pleasure and ceremony.
- A person whose store runs out simply stops. They do not suffer or even think. They wait, perfectly kept, until someone gives to them. Death is being stilled with no one waking you.
- Elders may hold a Last Giving: they give away everything and let themselves be stilled.
- Waking someone with a witnessed gift makes them your debtor, so decent people wake the still in secret.

Work and towns.
- Carriers are the whole of transport and industry, because nothing moves unless a hand pays for it.
- People save by making things. A house is a bank that only its builder can draw on, by unmaking it.
- Listeners visit rooms where words still hang. Courts work by listening to what was said at a scene and reading the maker's name on every change there.
- Reckoners trace chains of debt and redirected payments.
- Towns are clusters of rooms left hanging wherever they were set. There is no weather, so walls are only for privacy.
- Words in a room can only be unsaid in reverse order, so polite guests clear the air before they leave, last speaker first.

4. What is easy and what is hard

Easy:
- Keeping things. Food, heat, bodies, buildings and records last forever for free, memory is perfect, and nothing needs maintenance.
- Prediction and explanation. Anything no one touches will be tomorrow exactly what it is today, and for any change you just find the name on it.
- Safety. There are no accidents, spreading fires, floods, falls, disease, ageing or violence.
- Building. Put anything anywhere and it stays, with no foundations or supports.
- Fixing your own mistakes. It costs nothing, as long as no one has built on top of them.
- Enforcing obligations. Debts are exact and permanent, and they collect themselves.
- Waiting. The still can wait for centuries unharmed.

Hard:
- Anything automatic or large. There are no machines, chain reactions or leverage, and no wind or river to harness. Every effect is paid for by hand, at the payer's pace, so great works need great standing or a crowd.
- Getting rid of things. Nothing rots, washes away or wears out. Other people's leftovers, and everything the still ever made, stay until someone pays to build over them.
- Distance. You act only by touch, and words stay where they were spoken, so every message has to be carried.
- Escaping obligation. You cannot refuse a gift, debts never fade, older creditors come first, and a rival can bind you without your consent.
- Helping without binding. It needs secrecy, and secrecy earns the helper nothing.
- Staying awake. Even thinking costs store. The poor forget their pasts to get back the store their memories hold, which buys more waking hours, and then they slide into stillness.
- Letting go. Grief, grudges and memories never fade on their own. Forgetting is a deliberate unmaking, which returns what the memory cost.
- A shrinking world. The total store never grows, and the most honoured act, breaking, makes it smaller forever.","principle":"In the Kept World there is only one cause: a gift.
