You live in a world with different physics:

WORLD RULES:
The Kept World: Where Every Change Is Someone's Gift

1. The core principle

In the Kept World there is only one cause: a gift. A change happens only when a person gives some of their store, which is the world's single currency of change. The receiver then takes exactly the change that store paid for. Things have no natures or tendencies, only conditions. So the stillness relation is not an extra law. It is simply what happens when there is no other cause: if no one is giving to a thing, nothing can make it different, and it stays exactly as it is.

Potlatch shapes everything else. Giving is the only way to act on the world. Being given to binds you. Your power is measured by what you have given away and not yet had back.

People reason about this as calmly as we reason about a locked drawer: whatever you left is still there, exactly as you left it. Every "why did this change?" has the answer "someone paid for it", and there is always a name to find. Children learn this with their first toy. A dropped cup hangs in the air, and a toy that moved always had a mover.

2. The rules

R1 — Keeping. Whatever no one is giving to stays exactly as it is in every way: place, shape, heat, colour, freshness, tension, memory, mood and debt.
- Nothing falls, flows, cools, spreads, rots, rusts, ages, heals, fades or is forgotten on its own.
- A kettle heated a century ago is still exactly as hot. A drawn bow stays drawn forever and never looses its arrow. Spoken words hang in the air where they were said.
- A gift of motion is a gift of a journey. The giver decides where the thing goes; it goes there and stops. Nothing coasts past what was paid for, and there is no up or down.
- For anything untouched, its state now is its state at its last gift.

R2 — The Gift.
- Only people give. Everything else (stone, water, air, grain, beasts) is a thing. A thing can receive a change and keep it, but it never gives, so it can never pass a change on.
- A thrown stone that hits a window stops against it. The window breaks only if someone pays to break it. No lever, spring, wheel, fire or current does any work. Every effect is paid for directly, by the giver's own touch.
- A change costs its giver store equal to its size. One measure carries a grown person's weight a hundred paces, brings a kettle from cold to boiling-hot, or leaves about ten words hanging in the air.
- A waking hour of looking, listening and thinking costs about one measure. Seeing needs no light, because it is something the seer does.
- Store is never used up. It sits in the change it bought, and every change carries its maker's name, readable by anyone who looks closely.
- Only the maker can undo a change, and only if nobody has changed that thing since. Undoing gives the maker back the full store, so a round trip or a corrected mistake costs them nothing.
- No one can take store from a person. It leaves a person only when they give it.
- The only change one person can make to another is to give them store. Your body, place and mind change only when you spend on them, so no one can move, wound or kill anyone else.

R3 — Debt.
- When a person receives store from another person, with at least one third person watching as witness, the receiver owes the giver exactly that much.
- A gift cannot be refused. A gift given with no witness moves the store but binds no one.
- Debts never fade (R1). Only repayment, which needs no witness, or the creditor's forgiveness ends a debt.
- While you owe anyone, every measure you give to any person, witnessed or not, goes first to your creditors, oldest debt first, until you are clear. It reaches them wherever they are; debt is the one thing that travels without touch. Only what is left over reaches the person you meant.
- Spending on things or on yourself is never redirected this way.
- Between two people there is only one balance. If you return more than you owe, your debt is cleared and the other person now owes you the extra.

R4 — Standing.
- Your standing is what others currently owe you, plus everything you have broken (R5).
- Standing sets your pace, the fastest you can spend store. Everyone has 20 measures an hour, plus 1 more an hour for each measure of standing.
- Store is how much you can do; standing is how fast. Receiving makes you rich but bound. Giving makes you fast but poor. Being repaid slows you down.

R5 — Breaking.
- In front of witnesses, you may break a change you made, which means giving it up forever.
- No one can ever undo it, though others may build over it. The store in it leaves the world for good, and your standing rises by that amount permanently, owed by no one.
- Nothing adds store to the world, and breaking is the only thing that removes it. So the world's total store is fixed, except that every breaking makes it smaller.

3. How people live

Givings. Everything that matters happens at a Giving, because witnesses make gifts binding.
- The host gives to the gathered guests, and each guest watches the others receive. By the end, a hall full of people owes the host, and the host's pace has multiplied.
- The guests must hold Givings of their own. They try to give back more than they got, so that the balance tips their way.
- Rank is simply standing, and the great really are faster. A head of house owed 50,000 measures spends about 2,500 times faster than someone owed nothing, who gets around at a slow stroll.
- Monuments are broken works that no one can ever remove. Each one is a permanent record of its breaker's pace.

Fighting with gifts. No one can harm a body, so rivalry runs through store.
- You bring down a great giver by repaying them in full and then some. This drains their pace and leaves them owing you.
- Or you bury a rival in witnessed gifts, so that whatever they give anyone reaches you first.
- Custom pushes back. A Giving must include a witness the receiver invited, gifts nobody asked for are limited, and there are "quiet gifts", given with no witness, which help someone without owning them.

Family and life.
- Parents make a child by giving store into a new person. Births are always witnessed, so every child starts life owing its parents. Under the oldest-first rule, it can give to no one else until that first debt is paid. That moment, the Squaring, is coming of age.
- Children grow exactly as fast as they are given store to grow with. Adults do not age.
- No one gets hungry, because hunger would be a change nobody makes. Food is eaten for pleasure and ceremony.
- A person whose store runs out simply stops. They do not suffer or even think. They wait, perfectly kept, until someone gives to them. Death is being stilled with no one waking you.
- Elders may hold a Last Giving: they give away everything and let themselves be stilled.
- Waking someone with a witnessed gift makes them your debtor, so decent people wake the still in secret.

Work and towns.
- Carriers are the whole of transport and industry, because nothing moves unless a hand pays for it.
- People save by making things. A house is a bank that only its builder can draw on, by unmaking it.
- Listeners visit rooms where words still hang. Courts work by listening to what was said at a scene and reading the maker's name on every change there.
- Reckoners trace chains of debt and redirected payments.
- Towns are clusters of rooms left hanging wherever they were set. There is no weather, so walls are only for privacy.
- Words in a room can only be unsaid in reverse order, so polite guests clear the air before they leave, last speaker first.

4. What is easy and what is hard

- Keeping things. Food, heat, bodies, buildings and records last forever for free, memory is perfect, and nothing needs maintenance.

- Safety. There are no accidents, spreading fires, floods, falls, disease, ageing or violence.
- Building. Put anything anywhere and it stays, with no foundations or supports.
- Fixing your own mistakes. It costs nothing, as long as no one has built on top of them.

- Waiting. The still can wait for centuries unharmed.

- Getting rid of things. Nothing rots, washes away or wears out. Other people's leftovers, and everything the still ever made, stay until someone pays to build over them.
- Distance. You act only by touch, and words stay where they were spoken, so every message has to be carried.
- Escaping obligation. You cannot refuse a gift, debts never fade, older creditors come first, and a rival can bind you without your consent.
- Helping without binding. It needs secrecy, and secrecy earns the helper nothing.

- Letting go. Grief, grudges and memories never fade on their own. Forgetting is a deliberate unmaking, which returns what the memory cost.

Current regime ontology:
- [regime.held-metastability] Held metastability: excess order persists only while a holder answers its relaxation, and holding moves the unbalanced pressure into the holder, never dissolving it: 0 direct, 2 in subtree
  operator: A state above its ground carries a one-way pressure to relax toward that ground. The state cannot answer the pressure by its form alone; the answer must come from a holder, which is a structure or an act distinct from what it holds. Holding does not dissolve the unbalanced pressure: it moves it into the holder, which must pass it to a sink. Holders therefore need holding, holding capacity is the scarce resource, the amount of order a world can carry is bounded by that capacity, and whatever is raised or new needs intensive temporary holding until it sets. Unanswered excess relaxes irreversibly.
  partition regime.held-metastability.by-holding-mode, lens: holding mode: standing (a configuration paid once in ballast or anchorage; instant transmission; no memory; instant upstream cascade) versus running (an act paid per moment held; compulsory holder rest in which the holder must be held; stored tenure; gradual failure)
    - [regime.relational-load-path] Relational support by conserved load paths: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: Any configuration steeper than its material's repose generates an outward demand that grows superlinearly with its height; the ambient medium answers it only up to a threshold scale, and the thing can never answer it itself. The remainder is answered only by one-sided contact from the side the demand points toward. Equal opposing demands cancel; unequal ones pass their difference cumulatively along unbroken contact chains to a single sink, which accepts it only when enough ballast accompanies it. Removing any link unanswers everything upstream at once, and unanswered excess relaxes the configuration irreversibly toward its ground state, so ascent requires temporary scaffolding.
      instances: The Buttressed World, Where Only Children Stand Alone [world.buttress]
    - [regime.observational-upkeep] Observational upkeep: specific detail persists only under unbroken, resolution-limited attention, and the holder carries the decay it prevents as a burden shed only in rest: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: Specific detail drains spontaneously and one way: first to its kind's typical form, then down a ladder of kinds to a Ground that needs no holding. Drain is fastest on the intricate and new, near nil on the typical. The only counter is unbroken attention by an active, discerning holder. It only keeps: it never creates or restores, and it resists net loss of detail, not motion or accretion, harder the more is at stake. It holds exactly what some holder can resolve, a resolution set by sense, distance, breadth and understanding, pooled across holders. Gaps under a grace interval do not count, so relays must overlap. Holding is a running act: the drain it prevents is conserved, accruing in the holder as burden for as long as it holds. Co-holders share it, each holder has a capacity, and overflow drains the holder's own detail. Burden discharges only in the holder's rest, when it holds nothing and must itself be held. Unbroken holding accrues tenure superlinearly with span, and a break restarts the count; tenure shields the unwatched thing until spent. Kinds sum the tenure of all their members, so old kinds are deep attractors and a new kind falls into the nearest old one.
      instances: The Unbroken Watch: Where Only the Watched Stay Themselves [world.vigil]
- [regime.twinned-induction] Twinned induction: things are conserved signed turnings of one medium, born and cancelled only in opposite twins; nothing moves or feeds itself; each is carried and fed by others' stir: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
  operator: Every thing is a standing turning of one medium that can only flow; it keeps no material, only its pattern. Each carries a signed, conserved turn. Turn is made only together with an equal twin of opposite sign; equal opposites meeting annihilate into fine paired spray, which is heat; like signs within a threshold merge, and unlike ones cancel in part. Nothing can move or sustain itself. Each thing is carried and fed only by the flow the others induce, instantly and at any range, fading with distance. So like signs circle their shared center; an equal opposite pair travels straight, faster the closer, and an unequal pair curves toward the stronger; a lone thing goes only where ambient flow carries it or along a boundary, which answers it with an opposite-signed mirror partner. A turning lasts only inside a band of ambient shear: too little and it unravels, spreading its turn diffusely; too much and it is torn to spray. Every turning is also a sink that draws the medium into an inward spiral with no stable orbit, so all things drift toward some eye.
  instances: The Turning Deep: Where To Be Is To Turn [world.whirlpool]

- People save by making things. A house is a bank that only its builder can draw on, by unmaking it.
- Listeners visit rooms where words still hang. Courts work by listening to what was said at a scene and reading the maker's name on every change there.
- Reckoners trace chains of debt and redirected payments.
- Towns are clusters of rooms left hanging wherever they were set. There is no weather, so walls are only for privacy.
- Words in a room can only be unsaid in reverse order, so polite guests clear the air before they leave, last speaker first.

4. What is easy and what is hard

Easy:
- Keeping things. Food, heat, bodies, buildings and records last forever for free, memory is perfect, and nothing needs maintenance.
- Prediction and explanation. Anything no one touches will be tomorrow exactly what it is today, and for any change you just find the name on it.
- Safety. There are no accidents, spreading fires, floods, falls, disease, ageing or violence.
- Building. Put anything anywhere and it stays, with no foundations or supports.
- Fixing your own mistakes. It costs nothing, as long as no one has built on top of them.
- Enforcing obligations. Debts are exact and permanent, and they collect themselves.
- Waiting. The still can wait for centuries unharmed.

Hard:
- Anything automatic or large. There are no machines, chain reactions or leverage, and no wind or river to harness. Every effect is paid for by hand, at the payer's pace, so great works need great standing or a crowd.
- Getting rid of things. Nothing rots, washes away or wears out. Other people's leftovers, and everything the still ever made, stay until someone pays to build over them.
- Distance. You act only by touch, and words stay where they were spoken, so every message has to be carried.
- Escaping obligation. You cannot refuse a gift, debts never fade, older creditors come first, and a rival can bind you without your consent.
- Helping without binding. It needs secrecy, and secrecy earns the helper nothing.
- Staying awake. Even thinking costs store. The poor forget their pasts to get back the store their memories hold, which buys more waking hours, and then they slide into stillness.
- Letting go. Grief, grudges and memories never fade on their own. Forgetting is a deliberate unmaking, which returns what the memory cost.
- A shrinking world. The total store never grows, and the most honoured act, breaking, makes it smaller forever.

Rules as recorded:
R1: Keeping. Whatever no one is giving to stays exactly as it is in every way: place, shape, heat, colour, freshness, tension, memory, mood and debt. - Nothing falls, flows, cools, spreads, rots, rusts, ages, heals, fades or is forgotten on its own. - A kettle heated a century ago is still exactly as hot. A drawn bow stays drawn forever and never looses its arrow. Spoken words hang in the air where they were said. - A gift of motion is a gift of a journey. The giver decides where the thing goes; it goes there and stops. Nothing coasts past what was paid for, and there is no up or down. - For anything untouched, its state now is its state at its last gift.
R2: The Gift. - Only people give. Everything else (stone, water, air, grain, beasts) is a thing. A thing can receive a change and keep it, but it never gives, so it can never pass a change on. - A thrown stone that hits a window stops against it. The window breaks only if someone pays to break it. No lever, spring, wheel, fire or current does any work. Every effect is paid for directly, by the giver's own touch. - A change costs its giver store equal to its size. One measure carries a grown person's weight a hundred paces, brings a kettle from cold to boiling-hot, or leaves about ten words hanging in the air. - A waking hour of looking, listening and thinking costs about one measure. Seeing needs no light, because it is something the seer does. - Store is never used up. It sits in the change it bought, and every change carries its maker's name, readable by anyone who looks closely. - Only the maker can undo a change, and only if nobody has changed that thing since. Undoing gives the maker back the full store, so a round trip or a corrected mistake costs them nothing. - No one can take store from a person. It leaves a person only when they give it. - The only change one person can make to another is to give them store. Your body, place and mind change only when you spend on them, so no one can move, wound or kill anyone else.
R3: Debt. - When a person receives store from another person, with at least one third person watching as witness, the receiver owes the giver exactly that much. - A gift cannot be refused. A gift given with no witness moves the store but binds no one. - Debts never fade (R1). Only repayment, which needs no witness, or the creditor's forgiveness ends a debt. - While you owe anyone, every measure you give to any person, witnessed or not, goes first to your creditors, oldest debt first, until you are clear. It reaches them wherever they are; debt is the one thing that travels without touch. Only what is left over reaches the person you meant. - Spending on things or on yourself is never redirected this way. - Between two people there is only one balance. If you return more than you owe, your debt is cleared and the other person now owes you the extra.
R4: Standing. - Your standing is what others currently owe you, plus everything you have broken (R5). - Standing sets your pace, the fastest you can spend store. Everyone has 20 measures an hour, plus 1 more an hour for each measure of standing. - Store is how much you can do; standing is how fast. Receiving makes you rich but bound. Giving makes you fast but poor. Being repaid slows you down.
R5: Breaking. - In front of witnesses, you may break a change you made, which means giving it up forever. - No one can ever undo it, though others may build over it. The store in it leaves the world for good, and your standing rises by that amount permanently, owed by no one. - Nothing adds store to the world, and breaking is the only thing that removes it. So the world's total store is fixed, except that every breaking makes it smaller.

Lean months lower the year-low and pause locking; money above it stays spendable.","what_is_new":"New axis: the lock falls after the fact, on NOK that a year of the household's own lean months left idle, so no income forecast or pledge is needed and each household's buffer fits its worst dip.","why_it_works":"Untested rationale: irregular earners must guess what they can spare. Here nobody guesses: NOK that outlasted a year of the household's own lean months has shown it was not needed that year, and any new lean month lowers the year-low itself. The top-up aims to route surplus through the account.","why_it_fails":"Households with no idle NOK never lock anything, so chronic scarcity still needs the state's floor. sensitivity to window length and lock rate.","The share of still balances that is owed or earmarked (tax settled after the income year, rare large costs, money held for referent:referent.circle), by month.","How much household liquidity passes through a single account, and how much routing and dodging the top-up actually changes, measured in a pilot rather than assumed.","Legal and fiscal fit with referent:referent.state rules in force at the pilot date: tax treatment of slices and top-up, means tests that count balances, interaction with existing public accrual, and a lawful irreversible lock that refuses deposits.","Whether referent:referent.pension_provider or the state can guarantee inflation-indexed NOK/month deferred units, and at what cost.","Distribution: who receives the top-up, given that stillness tracks income and wealth; whether the progressive cap offsets that; and which floor covers households that never lock.","Data protection: who may compute and see the year-low, and on what legal basis, since the meter and the top-up need account-level balance data.","Comprehension and effects: whether households read the year-low and NOK/month claims correctly, and what happens to lean-month distress, credit use and saving elsewhere, with outcomes registered before the pilot."],"families":["fam.hindsight-commitment"],"note":"Transfer by a fresh context (task task.task-transfer-frost-line), onto successor model 34182691."},"task":{"taskNodeId":"task.task-transfer-frost-line","role":"transfer","graphHash":"18b5f7b60f31585912370407aaa783af57649bdccf3308e1a1261e4092172e11","taskHash":"06e632a42b5cbc5235b0bdb66170a161fb08057f0486b0f6f789cfb17cfdb361","targetBlind":false,"purposeBlind":false},"searchClock":{"rootId":"alien.understanding.21a77a717ac710789574e26e","unit":"search_step","at":37,"index":0}}

Cash paid off the rails escapes the cut."}},{"roleId":"relative_credit","binding":{"kind":"new_component","description":"A points register kept by referent:referent.state or referent:referent.pension_provider: each month's cut divided by that month's average cut over all payers, split 50/50 between partners, with first payments topping up the lower-credited partner and a survivor keeping the pair's points. It re-denominates process:household.pension_claims_nok from NOK into points and needs a payer population and partner records that the one-household model lacks."}},{"roleId":"neutral_durable_parcel","binding":{"kind":"new_component","description":"A consumption-share strip: a zero-coupon claim issued by referent:referent.state that pays, at one maturity, a fixed share of per-capita consumption in its maturity year, fungible with the series the public holds, with no votes and no upkeep. It is an invented instrument; inflation-linked zero-coupon debt and Tesouro RendA+ are the nearest working precedents. A steady flow into one issuer's debt is not neutral to that issuer."}},{"roleId":"one_way_drift","binding":{"kind":"new_component","description":"The calendar plus a locked registry: strips are registered to the common pool and cannot be sold, pledged or redeemed early, under statute and a time-lock on the securities registry, so time alone carries each strip from event:event.working.life to its maturity in event:event.retirement and any early move is a public breach. Time needs no tending, but payment at maturity can fail and a legislature can repeal the lock."}},{"roleId":"scatter_kernel","binding":{"kind":"model","ref":"event:event.retirement","how":"Each month's cut is split into strips maturing once in each of the roughly twenty years of the payer's likely retirement, dated from process:household.age_years, weighted by survival odds and set in the cut's calendar month, so the pool in any retirement year is fed by cuts from across event:event.working.life and placement is the only decision."}},{"roleId":"passive_catch_and_sort","binding":{"kind":"new_component","description":"Two standing rules in place of a barrier and a cross-wall: a matured strip can pay only into the common pool, and each couple's payment is split 50/50 into each partner's own account, as Swiss pension splitting does, with no clerk deciding. The model has no partner record, and the split comes after one common store, whereas the source sorts each pair before storing."}},{"roleId":"fixed_fraction_store","binding":{"kind":"model","ref":"referent:referent.pension_provider","how":"The provider holds the common pool in short indexed bills and, by fixed rule with no investment discretion, pays out 1/24 of it each month divided by points, so payouts follow the slowly changing pool rather than the latest maturity. Households hold points, not balances, so process:household.pension_claims_nok becomes a share of the pool rather than a NOK sum."}},{"roleId":"neutral_floor_reserve","binding":{"kind":"new_component","description":"A floor reserve: a slice of each matured strip is held back and released only when the monthly payment per head would fall below a floor set as a share of per-capita consumption, paid per head with singles included. It covers retirement payouts only; event:event.lean.month in working life stays with process:household.buffer_nok."}}],"proxies":[{"element":"Conserved ledger","label":"portable","proxy":"Cut inside the payment on digital rails, as Poland's VAT split payment does, plus platform, mobile-money and buyer-side withholding; a month with no gain owes nothing. Delay set by placement is present means; unstoppability is not, since a legislature can repeal the lock.","asOf":"2026-09-23"},{"element":"The guarantee","label":"magical","proxy":"None with present means: nothing brings value back of itself. Strips are only as good as the issuer and its statistics; fungibility with the public issue turns a selective raid into a general default and a multi-state issuer would spread the risk, but neither makes arrival certain.","asOf":"2026-09-23"},{"element":"Quietness","label":"portable","proxy":"No individual balances and a pool about two years deep, so there is no personal account to withdraw and no large fund to steer. The locked strips in transit remain a visible stock in the registry, guarded by rule and publicity rather than by concealment.","asOf":"2026-09-23"},{"element":"Timing by sowing distance and stone weight","label":"portable","proxy":"Maturity choice: each cut split across every year of the payer's likely old age, weighted by survival odds and set in the cut's calendar month so maturities arrive through the year.","asOf":"2026-09-23"},{"element":"The mirror-wall","label":"portable","proxy":"A standing instruction splitting each couple's payment 50/50 into each partner's own account, as Swiss pension splitting does; no clerk decides.","asOf":"2026-09-23"},{"element":"The self-centering round basin","label":"portable","proxy":"A fixed-fraction payout rule in the manner of Norway's 3% rule, applied monthly: the pool pays 1/24 of itself by points and is held in short indexed bills. With annual maturities, a pool paying 1/24 of itself a month would pay, eleven months after a maturity, about 63% of what it paid just after it, which is why the candidate matures each slice in the cut's calendar month.","Here lean months fall on the earning side: event:event.lean.month is a working-life event, while the floor reserve protects only retirement payouts. upsertEdges.explanation: Role proportional_tap: The platforms and payment rails withhold a fixed share (about 10%) of each event:event.earning.arrival as it clears, so the cut follows process:household.income_nok_month, a month with no earnings owes nothing, and process:household.income_cv never turns into arrears. Cash paid off the rails escapes the cut.
provenance: Search clock: search_step, not world time.

upsertEdges.explanation: Role scatter_kernel: Each month's cut is split into strips maturing once in each of the roughly twenty years of the payer's likely retirement, dated from process:household.age_years, weighted by survival odds and set in the cut's calendar month, so the pool in any retirement year is fed by cuts from across event:event.working.life and placement is the only decision.
provenance: Search clock: search_step, not world time.

upsertEdges.explanation: Role fixed_fraction_store: The provider holds the common pool in short indexed bills and, by fixed rule with no investment discretion, pays out 1/24 of it each month divided by points, so payouts follow the slowly changing pool rather than the latest maturity. Households hold points, not balances, so process:household.pension_claims_nok becomes a share of the pool rather than a NOK sum.

Store is conserved: it lodges in the change it bought, signed with its maker, and only the maker can undo that change, for a full refund, while nothing has changed the thing since. Coupled to this, as physical law rather than custom, is a binding operator: a witnessed person-to-person gift creates an exact, permanent, netted debt that seizes the debtor's later person-directed gifts, oldest creditor first, at any range; standing (claims owed plus store broken) sets the rate of spending; witnessed breaking deletes store from the world and is the one change no one can undo. Standing: a configuration pays once (ballast, anchorage), transmits instantly, keeps no memory and fails as an instant upstream cascade (regime.relational-load-path). Running: an act pays per unit time held, forces holder rest, stores continuity as tenure and fails gradually (regime.observational-upkeep)."],"boundary":"Introduced as a hypothesis on the second world. Keep it only if a later world falls under it without fitting either child, or if the standing/running cut predicts a world's consequences (instant cascade versus tenure; fixed structures versus rotas and rest). Collapse it if every later member is plainly one child. Not a home for every world where things decay without care: membership needs one-way relaxation to a ground, holding by a structure or act distinct from the held form, and the unbalanced pressure reappearing in the holder and passing to a sink. Possible further children: periodic re-performance, if the prevented decay still lands on the performers; hybrids in which a standing structure must also be tended.","roles":[],"status":"active","mergedInto":null,"createdAt":6},{"id":"regime.twinned-induction","label":"Twinned induction: things are conserved signed turnings of one medium, born and cancelled only in opposite twins; nothing moves or feeds itself; each is carried and fed by others' stir","operator":"Every thing is a standing turning of one medium that can only flow; it keeps no material, only its pattern. Each carries a signed, conserved turn. Turn is made only together with an equal twin of opposite sign; equal opposites meeting annihilate into fine paired spray, which is heat; like signs within a threshold merge, and unlike ones cancel in part. Nothing can move or sustain itself. Each thing is carried and fed only by the flow the others induce, instantly and at any range, fading with distance. So like signs circle their shared center; an equal opposite pair travels straight, faster the closer, and an unequal pair curves toward the stronger; a lone thing goes only where ambient flow carries it or along a boundary, which answers it with an opposite-signed mirror partner. A turning lasts only inside a band of ambient shear: too little and it unravels, spreading its turn diffusely; too much and it is torn to spray. Every turning is also a sink that draws the medium into an inward spiral with no stable orbit, so all things drift toward some eye.","differentia":["Against held metastability: decay is answered not by a distinct holder that takes on the displaced pressure, but by the pattern itself consuming an ambient gradient; nothing accrues in a supplier, no holder needs rest or holding, and failure is two-sided (starving or tearing), not one-way relaxation of excess. What is conserved is the order's own signed quantity, not the pressure against it: death spreads turn, never destroys it. Power is pairing, not bearing or keeping: a thing moves only with an opposite partner or its mirror at a wall, and every steer is a conserved transfer of turn. Interaction is an instant long-range field in which opposites cancel, not contact chains or attention."],"boundary":"Inside: worlds whose things are signed, conserved quantities that arise and cancel only in opposite sets and cannot move themselves, moving only in the field the others induce, whatever the medium, names, ranges or thresholds. Changing the merge distance, the field's fall-off, the shear-scaling law, the width of the livable band, the number of signs (if they are made only in cancelling sets), or dropping the world-whirl changes parameters, not the regime. The feed band is part of the operator as found here; a world that keeps twins and company-only motion but lets things last unfed stays inside as a specialization under a persistence cut, not a new root. Outside, to held metastability: worlds where order is kept by a structure or act distinct from it that takes on the displaced pressure and must pass it to a sink or shed it in rest. Rote reciters here resemble vigil keepers but supply feed, not holding: nothing accrues in them and nothing is shed. Outside, to relational load path: worlds where opposing demands cancel statically and the net passes through contact chains to a ballasted sink; here cancellation is annihilation or co-travel, imbalance steers, and there is no contact. Outside, as regimes still to be admitted: throughput-fed patterns with unsigned quantities or self-propulsion, which share only the feed band and would justify a 'fed pattern' parent opposed to held metastability; and conserved signed charges that act by contact or push themselves, which lack company-only motion.","roles":[],"status":"active","mergedInto":null,"createdAt":13},{"id":"regime.paid-change","label":"Paid change: unattended state is kept exactly; every change is an agent's conserved, signed expenditure, lodged in what it changed and refundable only by its maker until overwritten","operator":"Things have no natures or tendencies, only conditions, and an unattended condition is kept exactly: nothing falls, coasts, cools, decays or is forgotten; there is no ground, up or down. The only cause is an agent spending a single conserved currency by direct touch; a change in any direction costs currency equal to its size. Non-agents receive and keep change but never pass it on, so there are no mechanisms, chains or cascades. Spent currency is not consumed: it lodges in the change, signed by its maker, who alone can undo it for a full refund, and only while nothing has changed that thing since, so later work locks earlier work in stack order. No agent can take another's currency or alter another; it can only give currency, which cannot be refused. A witnessed transfer between agents creates an exact, permanent, bilaterally netted obligation that seizes the debtor's later agent-directed outflows, oldest creditor first, at any range. Witnessed renunciation fixes a change forever and deletes its currency from the world, so total currency only shrinks. What an agent is owed, plus what it has renounced, sets how fast it can spend.","differentia":["Against answered decay: there the unattended drifts and persistence must be supplied, by a holder that bears the displaced pressure or by a feed nobody bears; here the unattended is kept exactly and only change is bought, once, in any direction. Against observational upkeep, its nearest by shared structure, it is the dual: acts only change, keeping is free, and the maker can restore. The spent quantity is not a live pressure passed to a sink but an inert, signed deposit only its maker can reclaim, so making is saving and every change is attributable and reversible until built over. Causation is agent-only and contact-only, with no transmission through things; only debt seizure acts at range. A coupled binding operator turns the ledger into rank: being owed sets pace."],"boundary":"Necessary: the unattended state is kept exactly, with no spontaneous dynamics of any kind (no relaxation, momentum, diffusion or decay), and every change is caused by an agent paying for it, at a cost set by its size, by direct action on the thing. Full fit adds what the first instance shows: the payment is conserved, lodged in the change under its maker's name and reclaimable only by the maker until overwritten; witnessed transfers between agents create netted obligations that seize outflows; being owed sets pace; renunciation destroys currency. A world that keeps inert state and paid change but dissipates the payment (no refunds, no signatures) is a partial fit and the test of a partition by the fate of spent currency; one that drops binding, or binds without tying rate to claims, is a partial fit and the test of a partition by what a transfer between agents does. Out: any world where something changes unattended, even slowly, belongs under answered decay, even if agents also pay for change; worlds whose stillness is itself held by an agent's act (a freeze that must be sustained) are held metastability, since there keeping is what is paid. A world where change propagates through things (levers, contagion, chains of cause) has a mechanism rather than this operator. Newtonian inertia is out, because there motion coasts and here nothing does. Occasionalist worlds in which one agent causes every change at no cost are out too: nothing is paid, so nothing is ledgered.","roles":[],"status":"active","mergedInto":null,"createdAt":39},{"id":"regime.answered-decay","label":"Answered decay: left alone, a thing's state does not stay; it relaxes, lapses, unravels or drifts, and it lasts only while something outside it answers that tendency","operator":"Every ordered thing is off the rest point of some spontaneous tendency: relaxation toward a ground, lapse toward the typical, unravelling, or an inward spiral. It cannot answer the tendency by its own form; it lasts only while something outside it does, and unanswered it degrades irreversibly. What must be supplied is persistence, not change: the unattended changes by itself, and effort or feed goes into staying. Worlds under this concept differ in what answers and what answering costs the answerer: a distinct holder that takes the displaced pressure into itself and must pass or shed it, failing one way, by relaxation, when holding lapses; or an ambient feed that others induce and nothing bears, failing two ways, by starving or tearing. Scarcity follows the answer: holding capacity where the answer is borne, a livable band of feed where it is not.","differentia":["Names the premise that held metastability and twinned induction share and that stayed invisible until a world lacked it: the unattended drifts, so persistence has to be supplied. Their recorded opposition, borne holder versus unborne feed, becomes this concept's partition (by-answerer). The contrast class is paid change, where the unattended is kept exactly and only change is bought, so effort goes into altering rather than staying."],"boundary":"In: any world whose things have a spontaneous tendency away from their present state (toward a ground, the typical, dispersal or a sink) and persist only through an outside answer, whether a holder, a feed, a field or an act, and whether the answer is paid once or per moment. Both former roots sit here unchanged: held metastability under the borne branch, twinned induction under the unborne branch. Out: worlds where the unattended state is kept exactly (paid change); worlds whose unattended states change without degrading toward any rest point, such as purely reversible oscillation, which neither this concept nor paid change covers and which should be admitted on its own if it appears. A world with a slow drift plus paid change stays in, because some persistence must still be answered.","roles":[],"status":"active","mergedInto":null,"createdAt":39}],"relations":[{"id":"rel.opposition.cancellation","kind":"opposition","sourceConceptId":"regime.relational-load-path","targetConceptId":"regime.observational-upkeep","label":"cancellation: load-path's equal opposing demands cancel, while vigil's lapse is never cancelled, only moved or shared"},{"id":"rel.opposition.failure","kind":"opposition","sourceConceptId":"regime.relational-load-path","targetConceptId":"regime.observational-upkeep","label":"failure dynamics: instant total failure upstream when a link goes, versus tenure-buffered, local, gradual lapse"},{"id":"rel.analogy.holding","kind":"analogy","sourceConceptId":"regime.relational-load-path","targetConceptId":"regime.observational-upkeep","label":"analogies, not identities: unbroken contact chain and overlapping relay within the grace; two-sided failure (starve or tear) versus one-way relaxation"},{"id":"rel.analogy.cancelling-opposites","kind":"analogy","sourceConceptId":"regime.twinned-induction","targetConceptId":"regime.relational-load-path","label":"analogies, not identities: equal opposites cancel and only the net acts; the outer boundary completes the balance; one missing element sets the whole going"},{"id":"rel.opposition.how-imbalance-acts","kind":"opposition","sourceConceptId":"regime.twinned-induction","targetConceptId":"regime.relational-load-path","label":"how imbalance acts: cancellation by annihilation or co-travel in a contactless field where imbalance steers motion, versus static cancellation passed by contact chains to a ballasted sink with instant upstream collapse"},{"id":"rel.analogy.kept-by-flow","kind":"analogy","sourceConceptId":"regime.twinned-induction","targetConceptId":"regime.observational-upkeep","label":"analogies, not identities: rote reciters and carousel archives against the unbroken watch; the unfed widen into faint swirls as the unwatched go typical; a sealed room is a small Eye"},{"id":"rel.opposition.feed-not-burden","kind":"opposition","sourceConceptId":"regime.twinned-induction","targetConceptId":"regime.observational-upkeep","label":"feed, not borne burden: nothing accrues in the suppliers, and there is no compulsory rest, tenure or ladder of kinds"},{"id":"rel.paid-change-vs-answered-decay","kind":"opposition","sourceConceptId":"regime.paid-change","targetConceptId":"regime.answered-decay","label":"default of the unattended and what effort buys: exact keeping, so only change is bought, once and in any direction, with no ground, versus a drift that persistence must answer"},{"id":"rel.paid-change-vs-held-metastability","kind":"opposition","sourceConceptId":"regime.paid-change","targetConceptId":"regime.held-metastability","label":"what the outlay becomes: an inert, signed deposit only its maker can reclaim, so making is saving, versus a live pressure moved into a holder that must pass it to a sink"},{"id":"rel.paid-change-vs-observational-upkeep","kind":"opposition","sourceConceptId":"regime.paid-change","targetConceptId":"regime.observational-upkeep","label":"change-only versus keep-only: here acts only alter, keeping is free and the maker’s undo restores for a full refund; there the watch only keeps and nothing restores; unwatched records last forever versus only while watched"},{"id":"rel.paid-change-like-observational-upkeep","kind":"analogy","sourceConceptId":"regime.paid-change","targetConceptId":"regime.observational-upkeep","label":"analogies, not identities: debt and burden, conserved loads that accrue in persons, never fade and end only by a specific act (repayment or forgiveness versus rest); {"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"task","data":{"role":"transfer","inputs":{"mechanismNodeId":"mech.long-round"},"text":"Transfer one compiled mechanism into the target domain, for ideation.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

TARGET MODEL:
Model irregular-income-retirement (time unit month). Cite records as kind:id.

Processes:
- process:household.age_years [years]: age of the main earner
- process:household.buffer_nok [NOK]: liquid savings available for lean months
- process:household.income_cv [coefficient of variation]: month-to-month variability of earnings
- process:household.income_nok_month [NOK/month]: earnings received in the month
- process:household.pension_claims_nok [NOK]: accumulated claims payable in retirement
- process:household.spending_nok_month [NOK/month]: living costs paid in the month

Referents:
- referent:referent.circle: The household's close circle: kin, friends and neighbours who can check in, hold, cover or pool
- referent:referent.clients: The shifting set of clients and platforms that pay the household
- referent:referent.household: One gig-working household whose monthly earnings are unpredictable in size and timing
- referent:referent.pension_provider: An organization that holds retirement claims and pays them out
- referent:referent.platforms: The platforms, marketplaces and payment rails through which the household is paid
- referent:referent.state: The public authority that sets pension, tax and benefit rules

Events:
- event:event.earning.arrival: An earning arrives, of unpredictable size and timing.
- event:event.lean.month: A month in which earnings fall below spending.
- event:event.retirement: The household stops earning and draws on its claims, over an illustrative twenty years.
- event:event.working.life: The household's working life, with earnings arriving irregularly, over an illustrative forty years.
- event:event.world: The accepted present-day economy the household lives in.

MECHANISM (mech.long-round):
Operator: Value that grows with the square of the unbroken length of a maintained state, and restarts its count at any gap, is supplied to each maintained party by a rotating pool of intermittent maintainers who are released and credited only when a successor confirms takeover. Because each maintainer contributes whichever resource they have spare at the moment, continuity becomes a property of the maintained party, produced by the pool's overlap rather than by any one member's regularity.
Roles: maintained_party (The one whose accrued value depends on how long its maintained state has gone unbroken; it owns the span even though others produce it.); intermittent_maintainers (Many irregular contributors who each hold the state for a while; whatever any of them can make out is held, so together they cover more than any one could.); overlap_handover (The only regularity asked of anyone: do not release until a successor confirms takeover within a short grace; a no-show lengthens the current hold instead of breaking it.); superlinear_span_accrual (Accrued value grows with the square of each unbroken span; a gap keeps what was gained but restarts the count, so gaps, not unevenness, destroy value.); convertible_contribution (One unit that accepts whichever resource is spare now, money when busy or hours when idle, weighted by how heavy the hold is.); successor_minted_record (A witnessed record in media that do not decay, in which each credit is issued by the successor at takeover and so proves unbrokenness; entries are added freely but removed only with everyone's consent.); knowing_circle (A small mixed group whose members know one another; understanding gives the deepest hold, cannot be bought, and never accrues to those who do not take part.); continuity_backstop (Standbys, a store for lean periods, doubled holds where a gap would be costly, rest limits, and assessors who measure how heavy each hold is.)
Strangest element: Continuity belongs to the kept and is made by others: the account is a chain of handovers, each credit minted by the successor, and its value grows with the square of its unbroken length, so the least regular member can own the longest chain.. Kept as: Every credit is minted by the next holder's signature at relief; the floor and the squared surplus share are keyed to the member's unbroken chain, not to payments; a lean month cannot break it, only exit can; moving circles is itself an overlapping handover.
Magical elements: Unkept things and selves lose their particulars (R2) -> existing_approximation: Tend what really decays here without upkeep, fastest for uneven earners: pots raided in lean months, contribution records with gaps under minimum-weeks rules, scattered small pots and dormant accounts, ties that fade within months without contact, and being known.; Tenure grows with the square of the unbroken span; a break restarts the count (R4) -> institutional_substitute: Share the surplus by the sum of squared unbroken membership spans, with a flat floor. A span breaks only on exit or a year not kept, never in a lean month; sickness and caring count as kept; spans move between circles by overlapping transfer. Real echo: interest on an untouched steady trickle grows at least with the square of its span, and a withdrawal is the break.; Unbroken vigil with a five-second grace and overlapping handover (R1) -> institutional_substitute: Continuity of responsibility, not of gaze: every member always has a named holder (monthly while working, daily or nightly when frail, continuous when dying), with a grace set per service. The holder is released and credited only on relief; no-shows extend the shift at double credit; standbys cover.; Stones and seats as a ledger lapse cannot touch, because ink fades (R2, R1) -> invented_technology: Relief-signed tokens: the incoming holder's phone signs the outgoing holder's credit by tap or QR (a countersigned passbook without a smartphone), hash-chained per member so any gap beyond the grace shows, copied to every circle phone, and recounted in the open each year as in savings groups (VSLAs); one lifelong seat stapled to one pot held by a licensed custodian.; Coin is typical and keeps itself (R2) -> existing_approximation: One locked, low-cost diversified pot for life that takes any amount at any time (Kenya's Mbao micro-pension via M-Pesa, Colombia's BEPS with a 20% match, Australia's stapled super), with no early cash-out; hour credits are denominated in hours, so inflation cannot erode them.; Night is the tide of lapse and the oil store keeps lamps lit (R3) -> institutional_substitute: Here the tide is the lean month. A mutual bridge fund (like a VSLA social fund or a US pension-linked emergency account) pays lapse-critical bills: voluntary pension contributions that keep state records gapless, premiums, the phone line. It is repaid in money or hours, and circles mix trades whose lean seasons differ.; Waking attention is productive for anyone and is paid by weight (R1, R5) -> existing_approximation: Care time banks (Japan's Fureai Kippu, St. Gallen's city-backed Zeitvorsorge) and carers' pension credits (Germany, UK Carer's Credit), plus a worker-owned care co-op selling gapless shifts (hospital sitters, which cut delirium in the Hospital Elder Life Program, respite, postpartum nights): cash now, weighted credits later.; Weighers feel how heavy a charge is (R5) -> existing_approximation: Yearly standardized frailty, care-need and isolation assessments (Clinical Frailty Scale, ADL scales, long-term-care grading, Lubben network scale) set hour weights and the mix of close and coarse days, and flag unexpected decline.; Coarse sight keeps a face; only understanding keeps a self (R3) -> existing_approximation: Coarse keeping is passive monitoring and group calls (Japan's mimamori kettles that alert family when unused). Deep keeping is people who know you: PLAN-style personal networks, life-story work, a shared life file, pooled health-care advocates, and elders who speak migrants' first languages.; Cradle compact: newborns are heavy, long-cured elders light (R5) -> institutional_substitute: Our frail elders are not light, so the debt is redefined: night support in the 40-day postpartum traditions (cuarentena, zuo yuezi) makes you registered cradle-kin on the godparent/compadrazgo template; the grown child owes visits, calls and advocacy, not heavy care.; A watched clause resists being struck; additions meet no resistance (R1) -> institutional_substitute: An anti-cutback rule on accrued credits (as ERISA section 204(g) does), an asset lock on reserves, and a personal veto on cuts to one's own accrued rights; additions pass by majority; a short charter is recited at each annual meeting.; Holding the dying, the Turning, the wake and the portrait (R1, R2) -> existing_approximation: No One Dies Alone vigils and end-of-life doulas, advance care planning as the agreed letting-go, burial societies (South Africa) or iddir (Ethiopia) for the funeral, and the circle and cradle-kin for the life story.; Long-kept elders are cheap to keep, so the physics pays the Round (R4, R5) -> unresolved: Continuity of care and social ties reduce hospital use and mortality somewhat, and capitated care (PACE) can capture part of it, but dementia and frailty stay heavy; heavy care must be paid from pots, credits and insurance, not from continuity.; New kinds slide into the nearest old kind (R4) -> institutional_substitute: Regulators will file a novel mutual as an insurer, a deposit-taker or a Ponzi. Charter it as existing kinds (cooperative, licensed pension provider, time bank) on standard templates, and seed it from burial societies, VSLAs and credit unions.; Lone travellers and the unknown go typical; the circle vouches (R2, R3) -> existing_approximation: Travellers and migrants keep a paired holder at home who keeps ties, records and payments current, and they hold others by phone; circle attestation stands in for missing papers, like introducer-based ID enrolment in India's Aadhaar.; Burden burns off only in sleep; sleepless keepers lapse (R5) -> existing_approximation: Rest limits: no credit for shifts beyond a cap or without rest, respite rotas, and a two-person rule on heavy shifts that also guards against abuse.
Candidate:
  label: Long Round: relief-signed continuity
  design_principles: Make the pool regular, not the person. Accrue on unbroken membership, not payments. Take money or hours. Credit on relief. Only exit breaks a chain. Keep the self in people. Cuts need unanimity.
  core_mechanism: Each member always has a named holder; a holder is credited only when the successor signs 'I have it', adding a link to the member's chain; surplus is shared by squared unbroken span.
  how_it_works: Circles of ~12 households, mixed by trade and lean season, rota a named holder for each member: monthly check-ins while working, nightly presence when frail, a vigil at death. A holder is released only on relief; a no-show extends the shift at double credit. Dues: money into one locked lifelong pot when busy, weighted care hours when idle. A bridge fund pays lapse-critical bills. Handover tokens sit in a replicated open ledger. Kept years earn the floor; squared spans share surplus.
  what_is_new: Accrual keyed to an unbroken chain others produce, not one's payments; credit minted by the successor at relief; only exit, never a bad month, breaks it; part of the payout is being known.
  why_it_works: Hold-until-relieved plus standbys turns many unreliable shifts into one gapless chain. Spare money and spare hours peak at opposite times, so dues in either are steadier than pay. Untouched pots compound, known people are noticed early, and only exit costs, so members stay.
  why_it_fails: Money still follows pay, so low earners get small pots. Hour credits need nearby demand, trust and vetting, and may be taxed as wages. Squared spans favour founders and make leaving costly. Grant-fed schemes often fade; frail elders stay heavy here. Close circles can turn nosy or coercive.
  medium_term: Pilot in existing mutuals (burial societies, VSLAs, credit unions) in one town: holder rota, relief-signed tokens, bridge fund, hospital sitter contracts paying lean-month hours.
  long_term_vision: A federation of circles where anyone, however erratic their pay, reaches old age with an unbroken chain of people who took hold of them, a pot never raided, and a dozen who know them; state pensions credit kept years, and continuity is sold to health systems as care.

Family: fam.relay-continuity: Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept. Operator: A value that grows superlinearly with the unbroken span of a maintained state, and restarts its count at a gap, is produced for each member by a rotating pool of intermittent maintainers who are released and credited only when a successor confirms takeover; each pays in whatever resource is spare, so continuity is a property of the member rather than of anyone's regularity.

1. Map every role: bind it to a model record (kind:id), describe the new component the domain would need, or leave it unfilled with the reason.
2. Label each magical element's proxy as portable (achievable with present means), inverse (the domain needs the opposite effect) or magical (no present means), and date the judgment.
3. List where the analogy breaks: at least one disanalogy.
4. Write the candidate in the domain's own terms: label (at most 40 characters), design_principles (at most 200 characters), core_mechanism (at most 200 characters), how_it_works (at most 500 characters), what_is_new (at most 200 characters), why_it_works (at most 300 characters), why_it_fails (at most 300 characters), medium_term (at most 200 characters), long_term_vision (at most 300 characters).
5. State the evidence needed before anyone relies on it.

{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"solution","data":{"worldNodeId":"world.potlatch","text":"THE LONG KEEPING: a retirement system for people who cannot predict what they will earn

What retirement means here
Adults do not age and nobody gets hungry, so the only running cost of a life is waking: about one measure for each hour of looking, listening and thinking (R2). When a person's store runs out they are stilled, and they stay exactly as they are until someone gives to them (R1). So a retirement system has three jobs. It must hold a reserve that nobody can take or spoil. It must guarantee that someone will wake you. And it must turn a reserve of any size into as long a life as you want.

Why uneven earnings are less of a problem than they seem
- The pattern of saving does not matter. Nothing grows or fades on its own (R1), and nothing adds store to the world (R5). A measure put away in one rich month is worth exactly the same forever as the same amount put away in ten small pieces. Saving early earns nothing extra, and saving late loses nothing. Only the total matters, so the system never asks anyone to keep a schedule.
- The price of retirement is set by the world itself. A change costs exactly its size (R2), so one measure buys about one waking hour, now or in a thousand years. Anyone can count their retirement in hours.
- A gap in work costs nothing if you are still during it (R1).

1. The account: a row of kettles
The Long Hall gives each member a small alcove. To save, you heat kettles from cold to boiling-hot, at one measure each (R2). They stay boiling forever (R1). The store sits in them under your name (R2). Only you can unheat them, and unheating gives you back the full measure (R2). No one can take it from you (R2). There is no keeper to trust, no fee and no spoiling. Your balance is a count of kettles that anyone can read. You can put in any amount on any day, or nothing for months.

2. Open kettles and sealed kettles
- Open kettles are your buffer for lean months. You can unheat them at any time, and heating and unheating again costs nothing (R2).
- Sealed kettles are your retirement. A Sealer from the Hall moves each one a single pace into your sealed row. That move is the Sealer's change, sitting on top of yours. You cannot unheat the kettle while it is there, because a maker can only undo a change if nobody has changed the thing since (R2). The seal holds until the Sealer undoes the move, which costs the Sealer nothing (R2). The Sealer can never take your store, because only the maker can undo the heat (R2). It is a lock with two keys, and neither keyholder can steal. The terms for release, such as "at my Long Sleep" or "in a hardship the Hall's Listeners confirm", are spoken by both of you in the alcove. The words hang there (R1), and each voice carries its speaker's name (R2).
- The Tide Rule is the only rule about paying in. Whenever store comes in, first top up your open row to your chosen buffer. Many keep about 500 kettles, which is a month of full waking. Of anything above that, seal half and give the other half away with witnesses (section 4). A month that brings nothing asks for nothing. The good months do the saving, and the rule adjusts itself to whatever arrives.

3. Sleeping through lean months
A worker with no jobs does not have to burn store while waiting. They heat almost all their store into open kettles, keeping about one measure. Then they speak a final line into the alcove, such as "wake me for any carry to the east towns". The line uses up that last measure and hangs in the air (R1), and they stop. Nobody can move or harm their body (R2), and their skills and memories are kept exactly (R1). When a client comes, a Waker wakes them. A gap in earnings becomes a gap in waking instead of a drain on savings. This also ends the cruellest habit of the poor. Nobody needs to unmake their memories to stay awake, because sleeping is cheaper than forgetting.

4. Surplus that makes you faster now and pays you later
- The half of the surplus you do not seal goes out as witnessed gifts at small Givings, so that other people owe you (R3). Each measure owed adds one measure an hour to your pace (R4). A carrier who is owed 400 works at 420 measures an hour instead of 20, and can take the whole of the next rush of work.
- These debts collect themselves. Whenever one of your debtors gives anything to anyone, it reaches you first, wherever you are, without anyone carrying it (R3). You heat each repayment into kettles. Being repaid slows you down (R4), which suits the end of a working life. Here, retiring simply means entering the stage of being repaid.
- A debt owed to you is the one way of being woken that nobody has to remember. A repayment that reaches a still member wakes them, so a sleeper owed by many young, active givers will not be forgotten. Reckoners judge how good a debt is by where it stands in the debtor's queue, since debts are paid oldest first (R3). A debt owed by someone who has already paid off their parents (had their Squaring) and has few older debts is worth the most.
- Kettles are certain. Debts owed to you are uncertain, but they collect themselves and they make you faster. Members hold both.

5. The Long Sleep: any savings, any length of life
- Retiring is a choice, not an age. It begins with a second Squaring: you repay every debt you owe (R3). Otherwise anything you later give the Hall would go to your creditors first.
- Each waking works like this. A Waker who owes no one enters the alcove alone and in silence. Any word they spoke would hang on top of yours. (If the Waker owed anyone, their gift would go to those creditors, R3.) The Waker gives you a one-measure wake-coin. Seeing is something the seer does (R2), and the still do nothing, so no one is watching. The gift is therefore unwitnessed and creates no debt (R3). You wake and unsay your last words. Words are unsaid last-spoken first, and unsaying gives their store back (R2). You unheat as many kettles as the day needs and live the day. Then you quietly return the coin with a fee, so the Waker stays free of debt. You reheat whatever store is left and speak the time of your next waking. Speaking the last word uses up the last of your store, and you are still again.
- The numbers: 3,000 sealed kettles buy about 3,000 waking hours, which is roughly 190 sixteen-hour days. That could be every day for half a year, one day a week for three and a half years, one day a month for fifteen years, or one day a year for nearly two centuries. A thin record of saving gives a sparser retirement, never a broken one. Every repayment from old debts adds more days.
- Nothing you spend is destroyed. Each waking hour sits in your memory (R2), as a last reserve that the system is designed never to need.
- A sleeper who still owes someone gets their oldest creditor as their Waker. Every fee they pay anyone goes to that creditor anyway (R3).

6. The floor: Wake Patrons
- This is for members whose kettles run out. Great houses want standing (R4), and the best debtor for standing is one who never repays. A still elder who spends only on their own waking never repays, because spending on yourself is never redirected (R3), and the debt never fades (R1). So a house that wakes empty sleepers with witnessed gifts gains lasting pace.
- Compare this with breaking. A monument gives permanent standing but removes its store from the world forever (R5). A sleeper the house supports gives almost the same lasting standing, and the store stays in the world, in the sleeper's kettles and waking hours. The Hall records these patrons alongside monuments. That gives great houses a way to gain lasting standing without making the world smaller.
- Consent follows the existing custom that a binding Giving needs a witness the receiver invited. A member who accepts a patron speaks a standing invitation into the alcove before sleeping (R1). The cost is stated plainly: any gift they later make to a person goes to the patron first, so a Last Giving to their heirs repays the patron before the heirs get anything. Members who refuse a patron are woken with unwitnessed gifts paid for from the Hall's fees. That is decent, and it earns the giver nothing.

7. What can go wrong
- Tampering. Anyone who changes your kettle blocks you from undoing it, but they can never take the store (R2). Their change carries their name (R2), and only they can undo it, at no cost to themselves. Listeners can read the scene, so there is always an exact fix. A spiteful Sealer can delay you but can never gain anything.
- A Sealer or Waker who falls still is not lost, only waiting (R1). Wake them and they can act again.
- If the Hall itself fails, your instructions still hang in your alcove, and your kettle rows show a stranger that waking you will be paid for. Any debts owed to you will wake you anyway. The worst case is a longer sleep, never a loss.
- Someone may give a sleeper an unwanted witnessed gift. The sleeper hands it back on waking, and repayment ends the debt (R3).
- One rule runs through the whole design: whoever pays out must owe no one (R3). So the Hall runs on fees and unwitnessed gifts, never on borrowed store.

Why no one has to save regularly
- Timing is worthless and only totals count (R1, R5).
- The price of retirement is fixed in waking hours (R2).
- Time without work is free while you are still (R1).
- The payout stretches to fit any total (R1, R2).
- Debts owed to you collect themselves, across any distance (R3).
- The floor is paid for by the wish for standing (R4), without making the world smaller (R5).","citedRuleIds":["R1","R2","R3","R4","R5"],"isolation":{"solver":"fresh_context"},"note":"Purpose-blind solver, fresh context."},"task":{"taskNodeId":"task.task-solver-potlatch","role":"solver","graphHash":"09494dd020c83514448db2581cda549a2cdfe3b87793a1cf67966c09a311a4b7","taskHash":"27b8ecba0feb64242435e630a03665302a40d40826c6808596560ce934a8178f","targetBlind":false,"purposeBlind":true},"searchClock":{"rootId":"alien.understanding.21a77a717ac710789574e26e","unit":"search_step","at":41,"index":0}}

{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"task","data":{"role":"compiler","inputs":{"worldNodeId":"world.potlatch","solutionNodeId":"solve.potlatch","commissionNodeId":null,"populationState":"map"},"text":"Please think deeply about this problem.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

WORLD:
The Kept World: Where Every Change Is Someone's Gift

1. The core principle

In the Kept World there is only one cause: a gift. A change happens only when a person gives some of their store, which is the world's single currency of change. The receiver then takes exactly the change that store paid for. Things have no natures or tendencies, only conditions. So the stillness relation is not an extra law. It is simply what happens when there is no other cause: if no one is giving to a thing, nothing can make it different, and it stays exactly as it is.

Potlatch shapes everything else. Giving is the only way to act on the world. Being given to binds you. Your power is measured by what you have given away and not yet had back.

People reason about this as calmly as we reason about a locked drawer: whatever you left is still there, exactly as you left it. Every "why did this change?" has the answer "someone paid for it", and there is always a name to find. Children learn this with their first toy. A dropped cup hangs in the air, and a toy that moved always had a mover.

2. The rules

R1 — Keeping. Whatever no one is giving to stays exactly as it is in every way: place, shape, heat, colour, freshness, tension, memory, mood and debt.
- Nothing falls, flows, cools, spreads, rots, rusts, ages, heals, fades or is forgotten on its own.
- A kettle heated a century ago is still exactly as hot. A drawn bow stays drawn forever and never looses its arrow. Spoken words hang in the air where they were said.
- A gift of motion is a gift of a journey. The giver decides where the thing goes; it goes there and stops. Nothing coasts past what was paid for, and there is no up or down.
- For anything untouched, its state now is its state at its last gift.

R2 — The Gift.
- Only people give. Everything else (stone, water, air, grain, beasts) is a thing. A thing can receive a change and keep it, but it never gives, so it can never pass a change on.
- A thrown stone that hits a window stops against it. The window breaks only if someone pays to break it. No lever, spring, wheel, fire or current does any work. Every effect is paid for directly, by the giver's own touch.
- A change costs its giver store equal to its size. One measure carries a grown person's weight a hundred paces, brings a kettle from cold to boiling-hot, or leaves about ten words hanging in the air.
- A waking hour of looking, listening and thinking costs about one measure. Seeing needs no light, because it is something the seer does.
- Store is never used up. It sits in the change it bought, and every change carries its maker's name, readable by anyone who looks closely.
- Only the maker can undo a change, and only if nobody has changed that thing since. Undoing gives the maker back the full store, so a round trip or a corrected mistake costs them nothing.
- No one can take store from a person. It leaves a person only when they give it.
- The only change one person can make to another is to give them store. Your body, place and mind change only when you spend on them, so no one can move, wound or kill anyone else.

R3 — Debt.
- When a person receives store from another person, with at least one third person watching as witness, the receiver owes the giver exactly that much.
- A gift cannot be refused. A gift given with no witness moves the store but binds no one.
- Debts never fade (R1). Only repayment, which needs no witness, or the creditor's forgiveness ends a debt.
- While you owe anyone, every measure you give to any person, witnessed or not, goes first to your creditors, oldest debt first, until you are clear. It reaches them wherever they are; debt is the one thing that travels without touch. Only what is left over reaches the person you meant.
- Spending on things or on yourself is never redirected this way.
- Between two people there is only one balance. If you return more than you owe, your debt is cleared and the other person now owes you the extra.

R4 — Standing.
- Your standing is what others currently owe you, plus everything you have broken (R5).
- Standing sets your pace, the fastest you can spend store. Everyone has 20 measures an hour, plus 1 more an hour for each measure of standing.
- Store is how much you can do; standing is how fast. Receiving makes you rich but bound. Giving makes you fast but poor. Being repaid slows you down.

R5 — Breaking.
- In front of witnesses, you may break a change you made, which means giving it up forever.
- No one can ever undo it, though others may build over it. The store in it leaves the world for good, and your standing rises by that amount permanently, owed by no one.
- Nothing adds store to the world, and breaking is the only thing that removes it. So the world's total store is fixed, except that every breaking makes it smaller.

3. How people live

Givings. Everything that matters happens at a Giving, because witnesses make gifts binding.
- The host gives to the gathered guests, and each guest watches the others receive. By the end, a hall full of people owes the host, and the host's pace has multiplied.
- The guests must hold Givings of their own. They try to give back more than they got, so that the balance tips their way.
- Rank is simply standing, and the great really are faster. A head of house owed 50,000 measures spends about 2,500 times faster than someone owed nothing, who gets around at a slow stroll.
- Monuments are broken works that no one can ever remove. Each one is a permanent record of its breaker's pace.

Fighting with gifts. No one can harm a body, so rivalry runs through store.
- You bring down a great giver by repaying them in full and then some. This drains their pace and leaves them owing you.
- Or you bury a rival in witnessed gifts, so that whatever they give anyone reaches you first.
- Custom pushes back. A Giving must include a witness the receiver invited, gifts nobody asked for are limited, and there are "quiet gifts", given with no witness, which help someone without owning them.

Family and life.
- Parents make a child by giving store into a new person. Births are always witnessed, so every child starts life owing its parents. Under the oldest-first rule, it can give to no one else until that first debt is paid. That moment, the Squaring, is coming of age.
- Children grow exactly as fast as they are given store to grow with. Adults do not age.
- No one gets hungry, because hunger would be a change nobody makes. Food is eaten for pleasure and ceremony.
- A person whose store runs out simply stops. They do not suffer or even think. They wait, perfectly kept, until someone gives to them. Death is being stilled with no one waking you.
- Elders may hold a Last Giving: they give away everything and let themselves be stilled.
- Waking someone with a witnessed gift makes them your debtor, so decent people wake the still in secret.

Work and towns.
- Carriers are the whole of transport and industry, because nothing moves unless a hand pays for it.
- People save by making things. A house is a bank that only its builder can draw on, by unmaking it.
- Listeners visit rooms where words still hang. Courts work by listening to what was said at a scene and reading the maker's name on every change there.
- Reckoners trace chains of debt and redirected payments.
- Towns are clusters of rooms left hanging wherever they were set. There is no weather, so walls are only for privacy.
- Words in a room can only be unsaid in reverse order, so polite guests clear the air before they leave, last speaker first.

4. What is easy and what is hard

Easy:
- Keeping things. Food, heat, bodies, buildings and records last forever for free, memory is perfect, and nothing needs maintenance.
- Prediction and explanation. Anything no one touches will be tomorrow exactly what it is today, and for any change you just find the name on it.
- Safety. There are no accidents, spreading fires, floods, falls, disease, ageing or violence.
- Building. Put anything anywhere and it stays, with no foundations or supports.
- Fixing your own mistakes. It costs nothing, as long as no one has built on top of them.
- Enforcing obligations. Debts are exact and permanent, and they collect themselves.
- Waiting. The still can wait for centuries unharmed.

Hard:
- Anything automatic or large. There are no machines, chain reactions or leverage, and no wind or river to harness. Every effect is paid for by hand, at the payer's pace, so great works need great standing or a crowd.
- Getting rid of things. Nothing rots, washes away or wears out. Other people's leftovers, and everything the still ever made, stay until someone pays to build over them.
- Distance. You act only by touch, and words stay where they were spoken, so every message has to be carried.
- Escaping obligation. You cannot refuse a gift, debts never fade, older creditors come first, and a rival can bind you without your consent.
- Helping without binding. It needs secrecy, and secrecy earns the helper nothing.
- Staying awake. Even thinking costs store. The poor forget their pasts to get back the store their memories hold, which buys more waking hours, and then they slide into stillness.
- Letting go. Grief, grudges and memories never fade on their own. Forgetting is a deliberate unmaking, which returns what the memory cost.
