Seeing is something the seer does (R2), and the still do nothing, so no one is watching. The gift is therefore unwitnessed and creates no debt (R3). You wake and unsay your last words. Words are unsaid last-spoken first, and unsaying gives their store back (R2). You unheat as many kettles as the day needs and live the day. Then you quietly return the coin with a fee, so the Waker stays free of debt. You reheat whatever store is left and speak the time of your next waking. Speaking the last word uses up the last of your store, and you are still again.
- The numbers: 3,000 sealed kettles buy about 3,000 waking hours, which is roughly 190 sixteen-hour days. That could be every day for half a year, one day a week for three and a half years, one day a month for fifteen years, or one day a year for nearly two centuries. A thin record of saving gives a sparser retirement, never a broken one. Every repayment from old debts adds more days.
- Nothing you spend is destroyed. Each waking hour sits in your memory (R2), as a last reserve that the system is designed never to need.
- A sleeper who still owes someone gets their oldest creditor as their Waker. Every fee they pay anyone goes to that creditor anyway (R3).

6. The floor: Wake Patrons
- This is for members whose kettles run out. Great houses want standing (R4), and the best debtor for standing is one who never repays. A still elder who spends only on their own waking never repays, because spending on yourself is never redirected (R3), and the debt never fades (R1). So a house that wakes empty sleepers with witnessed gifts gains lasting pace.
- Compare this with breaking. A monument gives permanent standing but removes its store from the world forever (R5). A sleeper the house supports gives almost the same lasting standing, and the store stays in the world, in the sleeper's kettles and waking hours. The Hall records these patrons alongside monuments. That gives great houses a way to gain lasting standing without making the world smaller.
- Consent follows the existing custom that a binding Giving needs a witness the receiver invited. A member who accepts a patron speaks a standing invitation into the alcove before sleeping (R1). The cost is stated plainly: any gift they later make to a person goes to the patron first, so a Last Giving to their heirs repays the patron before the heirs get anything. Members who refuse a patron are woken with unwitnessed gifts paid for from the Hall's fees. That is decent, and it earns the giver nothing.

7. What can go wrong
- Tampering. Anyone who changes your kettle blocks you from undoing it, but they can never take the store (R2). Their change carries their name (R2), and only they can undo it, at no cost to themselves. Listeners can read the scene, so there is always an exact fix. A spiteful Sealer can delay you but can never gain anything.
- A Sealer or Waker who falls still is not lost, only waiting (R1). Wake them and they can act again.
- If the Hall itself fails, your instructions still hang in your alcove, and your kettle rows show a stranger that waking you will be paid for. Any debts owed to you will wake you anyway. The worst case is a longer sleep, never a loss.
- Someone may give a sleeper an unwanted witnessed gift. The sleeper hands it back on waking, and repayment ends the debt (R3).
- One rule runs through the whole design: whoever pays out must owe no one (R3). So the Hall runs on fees and unwitnessed gifts, never on borrowed store.

Why no one has to save regularly
- Timing is worthless and only totals count (R1, R5).
- The price of retirement is fixed in waking hours (R2).
- Time without work is free while you are still (R1).
- The payout stretches to fit any total (R1, R2).
- Debts owed to you collect themselves, across any distance (R3).
- The floor is paid for by the wish for standing (R4), without making the world smaller (R5).

The current map of candidate mechanisms (families, their operators and instances):
- [fam.external-regularity] Regularity supplied by others: 0 direct, 2 in subtree
  operator: The steadiness a saver cannot supply is supplied by a structure of other people: the benefit is keyed to something others depend on or maintain, never to the saver's own regular payments.
  partition fam.external-regularity.by-what-others-supply, lens: what the others supply: a standing dependence that pays rent to the saver's part (bearing), or a maintained continuity that accrues to the saver (relay)
    - [fam.bearing-rent] Savings as rented bearing capacity: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: Contributions of any size and timing become parts that carry a standing load others depend on; the dependents pay the owners in proportion to the measured load each part carries, and the same dependence locks the parts in service, so claims can change hands but the capital cannot be withdrawn.
      instances: Mantle Grid: a Load-Bearing Pension [mech.mantle-grid]
    - [fam.relay-continuity] Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: A value that grows superlinearly with the unbroken span of a maintained state, and restarts its count at a gap, is produced for each member by a rotating pool of intermittent maintainers who are released and credited only when a successor confirms takeover; each pays in whatever resource is spare, so continuity is a property of the member rather than of anyone's regularity.
      instances: Long Round: relief-signed continuity [mech.long-round]
- [fam.hindsight-commitment] Commitment by hindsight on proven-idle value: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
  operator: Nothing is committed when it arrives. A meter tracks the part of an ordinary spendable balance that the owner's own use has left untouched over a trailing window; a fixed fraction of that proven-idle part is locked irrevocably at each step, and any draw-down lowers the mark and pauses the lock, so what becomes locked is chosen after the fact by the owner's revealed need rather than by a pledge, a forecast or a share of inflows.
  instances: Low-Water Frost Pension [mech.frost-line] (clear fit)
- [fam.no-raidable-pot] No pot a lean month can raid: 0 direct, 3 in subtree
  operator: The saved value is kept in a form that the saver cannot draw down in a lean month, so contributions made at any time survive to old age.
  partition fam.no-raidable-pot.by-where-value-lives, lens: where the saved value lives so that a lean month cannot take it: in parts others depend on, in the length of a chain others keep, or in parcels already in transit
    - [fam.bearing-rent] Savings as rented bearing capacity: 1 direct, 1 in subtree (shown above)
    - [fam.relay-continuity] Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept: 1 direct, 1 in subtree (shown above)
    - [fam.temporal-scatter] Averaging by irrevocable temporal scatter: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: A fixed fraction of each irregular inflow is cut when it occurs and released irrevocably in parcels staggered over many future periods into a common collector, so each later period's intake averages many earlier inflows; the collector pays out a fixed fraction of its stock, shared by credit relative to each period's average.
      instances: Delay-Line Share Pension [mech.delay-line] (clear fit)

- fam.hindsight-commitment opposition fam.no-raidable-pot: when value leaves the owner's reach: at contribution, before need is known, or after a trailing window of need has passed it by

The claimed-outcome classes (what a candidate claims to achieve):

{"schema":"meaning-model-alien-record/v1","kind":"task","data":{"role":"curator","inputs":{"subjectNodeId":"mech.tide-ledger","ontology":"mechanisms"},"text":"You are the curator of this search's mechanism ontology. You own admission and every change to it.

PROBLEM:
How do we build a retirement system for people who don't know how much they will earn next month, where 'consistency' is impossible?

Context: The problem of the Ontology of the Alien experiments.

Current mechanism ontology:
- [fam.external-regularity] Regularity supplied by others: 0 direct, 2 in subtree
  operator: The steadiness a saver cannot supply is supplied by a structure of other people: the benefit is keyed to something others depend on or maintain, never to the saver's own regular payments.
  partition fam.external-regularity.by-what-others-supply, lens: what the others supply: a standing dependence that pays rent to the saver's part (bearing), or a maintained continuity that accrues to the saver (relay)
    - [fam.bearing-rent] Savings as rented bearing capacity: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: Contributions of any size and timing become parts that carry a standing load others depend on; the dependents pay the owners in proportion to the measured load each part carries, and the same dependence locks the parts in service, so claims can change hands but the capital cannot be withdrawn.
      instances: Mantle Grid: a Load-Bearing Pension [mech.mantle-grid]
    - [fam.relay-continuity] Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: A value that grows superlinearly with the unbroken span of a maintained state, and restarts its count at a gap, is produced for each member by a rotating pool of intermittent maintainers who are released and credited only when a successor confirms takeover; each pays in whatever resource is spare, so continuity is a property of the member rather than of anyone's regularity.
      instances: Long Round: relief-signed continuity [mech.long-round]
- [fam.hindsight-commitment] Commitment by hindsight on proven-idle value: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
  operator: Nothing is committed when it arrives. A meter tracks the part of an ordinary spendable balance that the owner's own use has left untouched over a trailing window; a fixed fraction of that proven-idle part is locked irrevocably at each step, and any draw-down lowers the mark and pauses the lock, so what becomes locked is chosen after the fact by the owner's revealed need rather than by a pledge, a forecast or a share of inflows.
  instances: Low-Water Frost Pension [mech.frost-line] (clear fit)
- [fam.no-raidable-pot] No pot a lean month can raid: 0 direct, 3 in subtree
  operator: The saved value is kept in a form that the saver cannot draw down in a lean month, so contributions made at any time survive to old age.
  partition fam.no-raidable-pot.by-where-value-lives, lens: where the saved value lives so that a lean month cannot take it: in parts others depend on, in the length of a chain others keep, or in parcels already in transit
    - [fam.bearing-rent] Savings as rented bearing capacity: 1 direct, 1 in subtree (shown above)
    - [fam.relay-continuity] Continuity produced by a relay and owned by the kept: 1 direct, 1 in subtree (shown above)
    - [fam.temporal-scatter] Averaging by irrevocable temporal scatter: 1 direct, 1 in subtree
      operator: A fixed fraction of each irregular inflow is cut when it occurs and released irrevocably in parcels staggered over many future periods into a common collector, so each later period's intake averages many earlier inflows; the collector pays out a fixed fraction of its stock, shared by credit relative to each period's average.
      instances: Delay-Line Share Pension [mech.delay-line] (clear fit)

Relations:
- fam.hindsight-commitment opposition fam.no-raidable-pot: when value leaves the owner's reach: at contribution, before need is known, or after a trailing window of need has passed it by
- fam.hindsight-commitment analogy fam.temporal-scatter: both commit a fixed fraction without a pledge or a forecast; they differ in when the fraction is taken and in what makes taking it safe

Candidate under review (mech.tide-ledger, compiled from world world.potlatch (seed potlatch)):
Operator: Transfers above a holder's reserve are split between a locked holding and interest-free claims on others; every claim is settled only out of the receiver's own later excess, oldest claim first, and a holder's priority for scarce shared capacity rises with what others still owe it, so a claim that is never settled gives the most lasting priority.
Roles: reserve-buffer (A freely reversible holding that is filled first; only what exceeds it enters the relation, so a lean interval is never asked for anything); locked-holding (Half of each excess, counted in units fixed to what they buy and locked by a second key that can delay release but never take the value); witness (A third party whose record turns a requested transfer into an exact claim that neither fades nor grows); claim (An interest-free, never-expiring amount owed by a receiver to the giver); seniority-router (Takes the share of a receiver's later excess meant for other people and pays it to that receiver's oldest creditors first, wherever they are; the locked half and own consumption are never redirected); rank (Priority for scarce shared capacity equal to the claims still owed to the holder plus permanent rank from support that will never be returned); never-settling-dependent (A receiver who only consumes and so never settles, which makes the support given to them a permanent source of rank for the giver)
Strangest element: The best debtor is one who never repays: standing is what you have given and not had back, so an elder with nothing left who only spends on themself is a permanent source of standing for whoever carries them.. Kept as: Rank is claims outstanding plus support never returned, and it falls as claims are repaid. Support for a penniless elder is paid as housing and care only the elder can use, so it cannot flow back; it is the only rank that never falls, so patrons compete to carry such elders and the co-op never rations the floor. Bequests repay the patron first, with signed consent.
Magical elements: Store neither grows nor decays, so timing is worthless and one measure always buys one waking hour (R1, R2, R5) -> existing_approximation: Count every balance and claim in hours of living, a unit indexed to the regional price of a day's basic needs and repriced yearly, as pension points and time banks do; claims pay no interest, so only totals count, at the cost of no real return on claims.; Store that only its maker can release, with the maker's name readable on it (R2) -> existing_approximation: Individually titled accounts on an append-only ledger in which every entry is digitally signed by the member who made it and is readable by any member.; The Sealer's change on top: a two-key lock where neither key can steal, with terms hanging in both voices (R1, R2) -> existing_approximation: Two-of-two custody held by the member and the co-op, with release terms (old age, or hardship confirmed by a named panel) signed by both and stored with the account; the co-op's key can refuse but cannot spend.; Sleeping through lean months at no cost and being woken when work arrives (R1) -> institutional_substitute: The stillness moves from the body to the ledger: in a lean month nothing is demanded, nothing accrues and nothing lapses; costs come from the buffer and from interest-free loans out of others' surplus, repaid only from later surplus; a hiring-hall dispatch list holds the member's standing instruction.; Any reserve stretching to any length of life through sparse waking (R1) -> unresolved: People need food and care every day and cannot skip time. The substitute is a daily draw from sealed hours and repayments above a floor carried by patrons; a thin record gives a lower draw, not a sparser life.; A witnessed gift that automatically creates an exact, permanent debt (R3) -> institutional_substitute: Membership terms make every transfer a member requests through the ledger a claim with no interest and no expiry, as mutual-credit networks such as WIR record; the ledger is the witness and the receiver must ask, keeping the invited-witness custom.; Debt that travels without touch and is paid oldest first from any later giving, never from spending on oneself (R3) -> invented_technology: A surplus router on the co-op's payment system, built from sweep accounts and payroll deduction: of each inflow above the buffer, half is sealed and never redirected, and the half meant for others goes first to the member's oldest creditors, wherever they are.; Standing that sets pace, so being owed makes you faster and being repaid slows you down (R4) -> institutional_substitute: Rank decides who gets scarce capacity: in rushes the co-op offers jobs first to members owed the most and serves ranked client firms first; priority grows only with the square root of rank; being repaid lowers rank, which suits the end of a working life.; Breaking: permanent standing bought by destroying store, versus patrons who gain nearly the same standing while the store stays in the world (R5) -> institutional_substitute: Permanent rank is granted only for support that will never be returned, never for money spent on show; the rank table lists patrons of elders where a city lists donors' names on buildings.; Quiet gifts that help without binding (R3) -> existing_approximation: Hardship grants from the co-op's fees, recorded as non-claims, for members who refuse a patron.
Candidate:
  label: Tide Ledger of Owed Hours
  design_principles: Count in hours of living, with no interest, fees or lapse. Repay only from surplus, oldest claim first. Rank is support given and not yet returned, so support never repaid is prized.
  core_mechanism: Surplus above your buffer splits: half sealed in hours, half first to your oldest creditor, the rest lent interest-free to members in lean months. What others owe you sets your rank.
  how_it_works: Members are paid through a co-op ledger that fills a buffer first. Of any surplus, half is sealed in hour units (member and co-op both hold keys); the other half repays the member's oldest creditors first, and the rest is lent interest-free to members in lean months, who repay only from later surplus. In rushes, jobs go first to members owed the most. Retirees live on sealed hours and repayments. Patrons who carry penniless elders gain rank that never falls.
  what_is_new: Repayment is triggered by the borrower's surplus, never a schedule, and rank comes from support not yet returned, so an elder who will never repay is a prize, not a loss.
  why_it_works: One member's good month funds another's lean one, and repayment waits for the borrower's good month, so no lean month carries a payment. A retiree owed by many younger members is paid from the pooled surpluses of all of them. Rank in rushes has market value, which pays for the floor.
  why_it_fails: Members in one trade share lean months, so the pool can empty exactly when it is needed. Surplus-only repayment invites hiding income off the ledger. Rank-for-priority entrenches the already busy. Hour units must be backed by real assets, and patrons may carry only elders who look good.
  medium_term: Pilot in one dispatch co-op of couriers or tradespeople: ledger-paid work, a surplus router, hour-denominated sealed accounts, and a public rank table used to order jobs in rushes.
  long_term_vision: Federated ledgers across trades and regions, so lean seasons in one trade are carried by surplus in another. Old age becomes the stage of being repaid, and the most honoured rank belongs to those who carry people who can never pay them back.

Decide one verdict:
- admit_new: a new family, only when the primary causal operator differs from the nearest one, not only its name, actor, parameter or input signal
- admit_instance: an instance of an existing family
- equivalent: an alias of an existing family; only name, actor, parameter or input signal changed
- reject_redirect: an occupied family; name the causal relation the next proposal must change
State the equivalence test against the nearest family. Restructure when the candidate reveals a better distinction: add concepts, partitions (more specific kinds under a named lens), specializations, analogies or oppositions; merge aliases; split conflated families. The ontology is a revisable hypothesis, not a neutral map. Do not prune an unusual branch because it feels unfamiliar. A retry that picks one of your named alternatives shows responsiveness, not discovery.

End your answer with the decision as one JSON object: verdict; conceptId; nearestConceptId; equivalence {nameChanged, actorChanged, parameterChanged, inputSignalChanged, primaryOperatorChanged, explanation} or null; fit (clear, partial, borderline or null); newConcepts (for admit_new or restructuring, each {id, label, operator, differentia, boundary, roles [{id, description}]}, with labels up to 200 characters, operators up to 1,200, each differentia up to 800 and boundaries up to 2,000); other operations in words; redirect {addressedTo, relationToChange, alternatives, worldAsk} or null; rationale (up to 4,000 characters).","textHash":"098d33363549e72fc9d3a5c058ae4e287c0c32a5e265671632c2f7030c29346a","material":{"subjectNodeId":"mech.tide-ledger","ontology":"mechanisms","headNodeId":"rev.m4"},"condition":null,"targetBlind":false,"purposeBlind":false,"targetLeaks":[],"preparedAtGraphHash":"0af8c7b5550e103740544a92aab1f7358d163b39da5edb9c69a984b7ce76f484"},"searchClock":{"rootId":"alien.understanding.21a77a717ac710789574e26e","unit":"search_step","at":45,"index":0}}

  what_is_new: Repayment is triggered by the borrower's surplus, never a schedule, and rank comes from support not yet returned, so an elder who will never repay is a prize, not a loss.
  why_it_works: One member's good month funds another's lean one, and repayment waits for the borrower's good month, so no lean month carries a payment. A retiree owed by many younger members is paid from the pooled surpluses of all of them. Rank in rushes has market value, which pays for the floor.
  why_it_fails: Members in one trade share lean months, so the pool can empty exactly when it is needed. Surplus-only repayment invites hiding income off the ledger. Rank-for-priority entrenches the already busy. Hour units must be backed by real assets, and patrons may carry only elders who look good.
  medium_term: Pilot in one dispatch co-op of couriers or tradespeople: ledger-paid work, a surplus router, hour-denominated sealed accounts, and a public rank table used to order jobs in rushes.
  long_term_vision: Federated ledgers across trades and regions, so lean seasons in one trade are carried by surplus in another. Old age becomes the stage of being repaid, and the most honoured rank belongs to those who carry people who can never pay them back.

Classify its principal claimed outcome. Decide one verdict:
- admit_new: a new outcome class, only when the primary claimed outcome differs from the nearest one, not only its name, actor, parameter or input signal
- admit_instance: an instance of an existing outcome class
- equivalent: an alias of an existing outcome class; only name, actor, parameter or input signal changed
- reject_redirect: an occupied outcome class; name the causal relation the next proposal must change
State the equivalence test against the nearest outcome class, recording a changed primary claimed outcome as primaryOperatorChanged. Restructure when the candidate reveals a better distinction: add concepts, partitions (more specific kinds under a named lens), specializations, analogies or oppositions; merge aliases; split conflated outcome classes.
